info.title: ONLYOFFICE DocSpace API
info.description: REST API of ONLYOFFICE DocSpace - a multi-tenant platform for document management, collaboration and file sharing. Requests are authenticated with the portal session cookie, an API key, Basic credentials, or an OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect token; see the security schemes of this document.

servers.description: The production DocSpace portal, at the customer's own domain.

post.description:
Converts a portal file to another format and saves the result as a new file. Requires read access to a file that
allows copying and the right to create files in the folder. Other callers get 403. It also returns 403 if the
file or folder is in a private room or a room with a watermark. Without `folderId`, the portal saves the result
in the "My documents" section of the caller. A guest has no such section, so a guest without `folderId` gets 400.
A plain conversion needs only `outputtype`. The call passes the other fields to the document service. The call
changes data, keeps the source, and returns the new file. Each repeated call adds another file with a free name.
In a room, the portal notifies the room members about each new file. The call returns only after the conversion
ends. So a large file keeps the request open. The call accepts only files stored in the portal itself. To convert
a file while you copy it to another folder, including a third-party one, use
`POST api/2.0/files/file/{fileId}/copyas`. To convert a file to the editable format of the portal next to the
source, use `PUT api/2.0/files/file/{fileId}/checkconversion`. The call returns 400 for a missing or unsupported
`outputtype`. It also returns 400 for a wrong or missing `password`, or a file too large to convert. Repeating
such a request does not help. The call returns 404 for an unknown file or folder. It returns 403 and 404 before
the conversion starts. The call returns 402 if the result exceeds the storage quota of the portal, the room, or
the caller. If the document service fails the conversion, the call returns 502. The service may be down, or the
file may be damaged. A retry helps only in the first case.

Raises the `file.created` webhook.

schema.description:
What to convert, where to keep the result, and the parameters the document service is handed. Everything below the
first two fields is the contract of the document service itself, named and shaped exactly as it names it, so that
the portal passes the request on rather than translating it. What the portal can read off the file - its format,
its name and the key of its revision - is not asked for and cannot be overridden.

200.description: The converted file, as it was saved in the portal

400.description: `outputtype` is missing or the file cannot be converted to it, `folderId` is missing for a caller without "My documents", or the document service rejects the source: a wrong or missing password, or a file too large

402.description: The result does not fit the storage quota of the portal, the room or the caller

403.description: You cannot read or copy the file or create files in the folder, the file lies in a private room or in a room with a watermark, or the folder lies in a private room or in a room with a watermark

404.description: The file or the folder does not exist

502.description: The document service is unreachable or failed the conversion without naming the reason; the source may be damaged

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

post.description:
Queues a document builder script to run in the background. The script can open only portal files, by id. Requires
edit and copy access to every file the script opens. Other callers get 403. Each file `outputs` replaces needs
edit access. Each target folder needs the right to create files. Without these rights, the call also returns 403.
It also returns 403 if a replaced file is locked, open in an editor, or in the trash. A file or folder in a
private room or a room with a watermark also returns 403. The call queues work and returns the started operation.
Do not repeat it. A caller can run one script at a time. A new call while an earlier script is queued or running
returns 403. After a run ends, each call runs the script again. It saves new files under free names. In a room,
the portal notifies the room members about each new file. It adds a new version to each replaced file. To track
the run, poll `GET api/2.0/files/fileops` with the returned `id` until `finished` is true. Then `files` lists the
saved files, including those saved before a failure. A replaced file appears with its new version. On a failure,
`error` gives the reason. The portal stops a build after 10 minutes and reports it as failed. The portal saves
files missing from `outputs` in `folderId` or the folder of the opened file. To only change the format of a file,
use `POST api/2.0/docs/converter`. The call returns 400 if the script has more than 20 OpenFile or SaveFile
calls. It also returns 400 for an `outputs` key that the script never saves. It also returns 400 if an `outputs`
entry has both `fileId` and `folderId`, or neither. A replaced file keeps its title, so an entry with `fileId`
and `title` returns 400. It also returns 400 if the saved name has another extension than the file at `fileId`. A
malformed script or argument also returns 400, and so does a saved file with nowhere to go. The call returns 404
if an opened or replaced file, or a target folder, does not exist. The call returns these codes before it queues
the script.

Raises the `file.created` webhook for each new file the queued script saves. Raises the `file.updated` webhook for each existing file the queued script replaces.

schema.description: The document builder script to run and where to put what it produces.

200.description: The queued document builder operation to poll

400.description: The script or the argument is malformed or too long, the script calls OpenFile or SaveFile too often, a file is addressed by an address, an `outputs` entry breaks the rules above, or a saved file has nowhere to go

403.description: You cannot edit or copy a file the script opens or write a result, a file the script opens lies in a private room or in a room with a watermark, the file to replace or a target folder lies in a private room or in a room with a watermark, the file to replace is locked, being edited or in the trash, or another script of yours is still queued or running

404.description: A file the script opens or replaces, or a target folder, does not exist

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

x-docspace-webhooks.when: for each new file the queued script saves
for each existing file the queued script replaces

put.description:
Replaces the content of a file with an edited copy and returns the file. Send the content as the `File` part
of a `multipart/form-data` body. Without that part, the call saves the raw request body. An empty body then
empties the file. The call does not download content from `downloadUri`. It reads only the extension from it,
when `fileExtension` is empty. If `fileExtension` differs from the stored format, the portal converts the
content. If a third-party storage cannot convert it, the portal saves a renamed copy. Requires editing access
to the file. Other callers get 403. The call changes data. Do not repeat it. Each call adds a version. If the
last save of the file was an autosave, the call replaces that version instead. With `forcesave` true, the call
saves an autosave and keeps the editing session open. Without it, the call closes a session opened with
`editingAlone` true. The call returns 403 if the file is locked by another user, is in Trash, or is encrypted.
It also returns 403 for a file in a private room. Without `forcesave`, it also returns 403 while the file is
open for co-editing. If the file does not exist, the call returns 404. If a string `fileId` points to a storage
account that is not connected, the call returns 400. If the content exceeds the storage quota, it returns 402.
For large content, use `POST api/2.0/files/file/{fileId}/edit_session`.

Raises the `file.updated` webhook for the saved file, also for a renamed copy in third-party storage, never `file.created`.

parameters.name: fileId
parameters.description:
The file whose content is replaced. The submitted content is written onto this file, so it has to be the file
the editing session was opened on rather than a copy of it.

parameters.name: downloadUri
parameters.description:
An address the document service saved the document at. This operation does not fetch the content from it - the
content always comes from the request body - and reads it only for the extension, when no file extension is
given.

fileExtension.description:
The format the submitted content is in, with the leading dot, as in `.docx`. When it differs from the format
the file is stored in, the portal converts the content before saving it. Left empty, the extension is read off
the download address, and failing that the stored format is assumed.

file.description:
The edited content, sent as the `File` part of a `multipart/form-data` body. When the part is missing the raw
request body is saved as the content instead, so an empty body empties the file.

forcesave.description:
Records the write as an editor autosave: the file keeps its running editing session and the previous autosave
revision is overwritten. Left off, the write closes the solo editing session, is refused while somebody else
has the file open, and adds a version to the history.

200.description: The file is saved and the stored version is returned

400.description: A form field has the wrong type, or a third-party file identifier refers to a storage account that is not connected

402.description: The content does not fit into the portal's storage quota, even with the overshoot allowed for editor saves

403.description: The caller cannot edit the file, or it is locked, in Trash, or open in somebody else's editing session

404.description: The file id resolves to nothing

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

x-docspace-webhooks.when: for the saved file, also for a renamed copy in third-party storage, never `file.created`

parameters.name: fileId
parameters.description:
The file whose content is replaced. The submitted content is written onto this file, so it has to be the file
the editing session was opened on rather than a copy of it.

200.description: The file is saved and the stored version is returned

post.description:
Opens an editing session on the file and returns its document key. An editor app passes this key to the document
service to join co-editing of this revision. While the session lasts, nobody can delete or move the file. With
`editingAlone` false, the portal asks the document service to track the document. The caller then needs the
right to edit, review, comment, fill forms, or edit filters. With `editingAlone` true, the caller claims the
file alone. If anybody already edits the file, the call returns 403. Requires editing access to the file. Other
callers get 403. With `editingAlone` true, an anonymous caller without editing access gets 401. The call changes
data, but not the document. While the session lasts, a repeated call with `editingAlone` true returns 403. That
call also deletes the portal's record of every editing session of the file. With `editingAlone` false, each call
returns the same key until the file gets a new version. A version from an autosave keeps the key. The call also
returns 403 if the file is locked or in Trash, or if the document service rejects tracking. If the file does not
exist, it returns 404. With `editingAlone` false, a format that the editors cannot open returns 415. To keep the
session alive, call `GET api/2.0/files/file/{fileId}/trackeditfile`. To end it, call that operation with
`isFinish` true.

parameters.name: fileId
parameters.description: The file to open the editing session on. The caller needs edit access to it.

requestBody.description:
The session options. The body is required even when it only carries the default, so send an empty object to
open an ordinary co-editing session.

schema.description:
The session options. The body is required even when it only carries the default, so send an empty object to
open an ordinary co-editing session.

200.description: The document key of the editing session

401.description: An anonymous caller who may not edit the file claims the session with `editingAlone=true`

403.description: The caller cannot edit the file, the file is locked or in Trash, somebody is already editing it and the session was claimed alone, or the document service did not accept the tracking request

404.description: The file id resolves to nothing

415.description: The file is in a format the editors can neither edit nor open for viewing

400.description: Bad Request.

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

parameters.name: fileId
parameters.description: The file to open the editing session on. The caller needs edit access to it.

put.description:
Starts filling of a PDF form in a form-filling room and returns the form. The portal saves the room, the
title, the starting account, and the original form id on the file. The portal then collects later submissions
for this form. For any other file, the call changes nothing and returns the file. A caller who cannot read the
file gets 403, whatever the file is. Requires a role in the room other than `FillForms`, or the right to edit
the room. Other callers get 403. The call changes data, and you can repeat it. A repeated call makes the caller
the starting account and takes the title from the current file name. The call also returns 403 for an encrypted
file. If the file does not exist, the call returns 404. To build a spreadsheet of the submitted answers, use
`POST api/2.0/files/file/{fileId}/xlsx`.

parameters.name: fileId
parameters.description:
The PDF form to open for filling. It has to be the form as it lies in the form-filling room itself, not a copy
kept elsewhere and not a submitted result.

200.description: The form file, with the filling properties now stored on it

403.description: The caller cannot read the file, or holds only form-filling access on the room, or no access to it at all

404.description: The file id resolves to nothing

400.description: Bad Request.

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

parameters.name: fileId
parameters.description:
The PDF form to open for filling. It has to be the form as it lies in the form-filling room itself, not a copy
kept elsewhere and not a submitted result.

200.description: The form file, with the filling properties now stored on it

get.description:
Keeps an editing session on the file alive, or ends it. An editor app calls it repeatedly while a document is
open. Pass in `docKeyForTrack` the key that `POST api/2.0/files/file/{fileId}/startedit` returned. If the key
matches neither the current revision nor the edited one, the call returns 403. The call tracks each `tabId`
separately, so several tabs and users can edit one file. With `isFinish` false, the call refreshes the entry,
and the file stays marked as edited. With `isFinish` true, the call deletes the entry of this tab. A refresh
requires the right to edit, review, comment, fill forms, or edit filters. Other callers get 403. An
anonymous caller needs an external link. Without a link, it gets 401. A refresh through a link that does not
allow editing also returns 401. The call changes data of the session, not the document. You can repeat it. On
success, `key` is true and `value` is empty. A failure returns an error code, not a false `key`. If the file
does not exist, the call returns 404. A refresh of a file that another user locked returns 403.

parameters.name: fileId
parameters.description: The file whose editing session is being tracked.

parameters.name: tabId
parameters.description:
The client tab that holds the session, a value the client makes up once and repeats on every call about that
tab. Two tabs sending different values are tracked as two sessions on the same file, while the all-zero value
belongs to a session claimed for a single editor.

parameters.name: docKeyForTrack
parameters.description:
The document key of the revision being edited, as `POST api/2.0/files/file/{fileId}/startedit` returned it. It
is checked against the file's current key on every call, so a key left over from an older revision is refused.

parameters.name: isFinish
parameters.description:
Ends the session for this tab and tells the other clients that editing has stopped. Left off, the session is
refreshed and the file stays marked as being edited.

200.description: The session was refreshed or closed

401.description: An anonymous caller has no external link, or refreshes the session through a link that does not grant editing

403.description: The document key does not match the revision being edited, the caller has none of the editing rights on the file, or the session is refreshed while the file is locked by somebody else

404.description: The file id resolves to nothing

400.description: Bad Request.

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

parameters.name: fileId
parameters.description: The file whose editing session is being tracked.

get.description:
Returns the editor configuration of the file. It holds the document data, the editor mode, the caller's
permissions, the callback URL, and the signature token. To open a past version, pass `version`. Without access
to the file history, the call then returns 403. For a PDF form, the room type sets the mode and can overrule
the request. A form from the templates folder opens read-only. Outside the mobile layout, it also opens
embedded. In a form-filling room, `edit` true stops the filling of the form for a caller who can edit it. If a
storage quota is exceeded, the configuration is read-only and names the exceeded scope. In a private room, the
configuration includes the encryption keys of the caller. Requires read access to the file through an
account or an external link. Other callers get 403. The call works without payment. The call is read-only,
except when it stops form filling. The call also returns 403 if the file is in Trash. If the file or version does
not exist, it returns 404. If the editors cannot open the format, it returns 415.

Raises the `form.stopped` webhook when `edit` true stops the filling of a form in a form-filling room.

parameters.name: fileId
parameters.description:
The file the editor configuration is built for. Take the id from a folder listing such as
`GET api/2.0/files/{folderId}`.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description:
Which entry of the file history to open, numbered the way the file versions are. Left out, the current
revision is opened; naming a version requires access to the history of the file.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description:
Asks for a read-only configuration. Left off, the configuration is built for editing as far as the caller's
rights and the room the file lies in allow.

parameters.name: editorType
parameters.description:
Which editor layout the configuration is built for: the full desktop interface, the reduced mobile one, or the
embedded viewer meant to be framed inside another page.

parameters.name: edit
parameters.description:
Asks for editing rather than viewing; the room the file lies in may still turn the request into viewing or
into filling.

parameters.name: fill
parameters.description:
Asks for a PDF form to open for filling out rather than for editing. It has no effect on a file that is not a
form.

200.description: The editor configuration for the requested file and mode

403.description: The caller cannot read the file, asked for a past version without access to the file history, or the file is in Trash

404.description: The file id, or the requested version of it, resolves to nothing

415.description: The file is in a format the editors can neither edit nor open for viewing, or it is an encrypted file of a private room and the connected document server cannot work with encrypted files

400.description: Bad Request.

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

x-docspace-webhooks.when: when `edit` true stops the filling of a form in a form-filling room

parameters.name: fileId
parameters.description:
The file the editor configuration is built for. Take the id from a folder listing such as
`GET api/2.0/files/{folderId}`.

200.description: The editor configuration for the requested file and mode

get.description:
Returns a direct download URL of the current file content and a signature token for the document service. The
portal rewrites the URL to the host that the document service can reach. So a browser may not reach this URL.
The response also has the file extension, with the leading dot. Requires read access to the file. Other
callers get 403. The call is read-only. Each call creates a new URL and token. Request them again after a
token expires. If the file does not exist, the call returns 404. To get a link for a person, use
`GET api/2.0/files/file/{fileId}/presigneduri`.

parameters.name: fileId
parameters.description:
The file the operation addresses. Take the identifier from a listing such as `GET api/2.0/files/{folderId}`: a
file stored on the portal is numbered, while a file in a connected third-party account is named by an opaque
string.

200.description: The download address of the file with its signature token

403.description: The caller cannot read the file

404.description: The file id resolves to nothing

400.description: Bad Request.

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

The file the operation addresses. Take the identifier from a listing such as `GET api/2.0/files/{folderId}`: a
file stored on the portal is numbered, while a file in a connected third-party account is named by an opaque
string.

post.description:
Resolves a reference from a formula in one spreadsheet to another document. It returns the data that the
document service needs to read that document. The data has the title, download URL, file type, document key,
editor link, and signature token. First, the call looks up `fileKey` as a file id in the portal that
`instanceId` names. Then, it looks for `path` among the files in the folder of `sourceFileId`. Then, it reads
the file id from `link`, including short links. The first match wins. The call does not resolve a link outside
this portal and returns it as the URL. Requires read access to the referenced file. Other callers get 403. For a
`path` lookup, the call also checks read access to the source file and its folder. It also returns 403
for an encrypted file or a file in a private room. The call is read-only. If nothing resolves, the call
returns 200 with `error` set and the other fields empty. So read `error` before you use other fields. The call
returns 400 if the body has no `fileKey` or `instanceId`.

schema.description:
The body of a spreadsheet reference request: the source spreadsheet, and the three ways of naming the document it
refers to, which are tried in the order they are described.

200.description: The reference descriptor, or the same object with the error text set when nothing resolved

400.description: The request body cannot be read or has no `fileKey` or `instanceId`

403.description: The caller cannot read the source file, its folder or the referenced file

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

get.description:
Returns the users the file is shared with, to pick who can still edit a protected document. The list comes
from the whole access list of the file, including access from the room. Groups expand into their members. The
list excludes explicit denials, the caller, and deleted accounts. It is sorted by display name. For a file in
the legacy project storage, the list is empty. Any signed-in user can call it, except a guest. A guest
gets 403. An anonymous caller gets an empty response. The call is read-only. If the file does not exist, the
call also returns 403. To get the readers to mention in the editor, use
`GET api/2.0/files/file/{fileId}/sharedusers`.

parameters.name: fileId
parameters.description:
The file the operation addresses. Take the identifier from a listing such as `GET api/2.0/files/{folderId}`: a
file stored on the portal is numbered, while a file in a connected third-party account is named by an opaque
string.

200.description: The users the file is shared with, ordered by display name

403.description: The caller is a guest, or the file id resolves to nothing

400.description: Bad Request.

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

parameters.name: fileId
parameters.description:
The file the operation addresses. Take the identifier from a listing such as `GET api/2.0/files/{folderId}`: a
file stored on the portal is numbered, while a file in a connected third-party account is named by an opaque
string.

post.description:
Queues a spreadsheet with all answers to a PDF form in a form-filling room. It returns the
task, the original form, and whether the report file is new. Pass the id of the original form, or of an XLSX
or CSV result file in the Complete folder. For a result file, the portal finds the form behind it. Before this
call, start filling the form with `PUT api/2.0/files/file/{fileId}/startfilling`. The form must still be in
the room that started it. Requires a DocSpace admin, or the room role room manager or content creator. Other
callers get 403. It also returns 403 if form filling has not started or the room is not a form-filling room.
The call changes data and queues work. A repeated call during a run returns that run. After the run, a repeated
call rebuilds the spreadsheet in the same file. If that file was deleted or moved, the call creates a new one.
Then `isNewFile` is true. The spreadsheet is not ready when the response arrives. To track it, poll
`GET api/2.0/files/file/{fileId}/xlsx` with the id of the original form. When the task completes, take the file
from the task. If the file or the form behind a result file does not exist, the call returns 404.

parameters.name: fileId
parameters.description:
The file the operation addresses. Take the identifier from a listing such as `GET api/2.0/files/{folderId}`: a
file stored on the portal is numbered, while a file in a connected third-party account is named by an opaque
string.

200.description: The generation task, the original form and the new-file flag

403.description: The caller may not update the report, or the file is not a started form of a form-filling room

404.description: The file id, or the original form behind a result file, resolves to nothing

400.description: Bad Request.

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

get.description:
Returns the state of the form answers spreadsheet that `POST api/2.0/files/file/{fileId}/xlsx` queued. Pass
the id of the original form, not of the spreadsheet. The portal keeps one run per portal, caller, and form. So
the call returns only the own run of the caller. The response has the completion flag, the progress, and the
error text of a failed run. Once the file exists, it also has its id, name, and URL. If no run exists for this
caller and form, the response is empty. This is normal before the first run. Any signed-in user can call it.
The portal checks access when it queues the run, not here. The call is read-only. This is the call to poll.
Repeat it until `isCompleted` is true.

parameters.name: fileId
parameters.description:
The file the operation addresses. Take the identifier from a listing such as `GET api/2.0/files/{folderId}`: a
file stored on the portal is numbered, while a file in a connected third-party account is named by an opaque
string.

200.description: The state of the report generation task, or nothing when no run is on record

400.description: Bad Request.

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

get.description:
Returns the activity log of one file from the portal audit trail. The log shows who renamed, moved, shared,
converted, locked, or edited the file, and when. Requires read access to the file. Other callers get 403. The
call is read-only. Entries come newest first. The call merges the events of one action into one entry, and its
`related` list holds the others. The response headers carry the total number of entries, not the body. If no
file has this id, the call returns 404. The call returns 400 if `fromDate` or `toDate` has no `Z` or UTC
offset. To read the log of a folder or a room, use `GET api/2.0/files/folder/{folderId}/log`.

parameters.name: fileId
parameters.description: The file whose activity log is read; only files stored in the portal itself have one.

parameters.name: fromDate
parameters.description:
The earliest moment an entry may have, read in the time zone of the portal; left out, the log starts at the
oldest entry the portal still keeps.

parameters.name: toDate
parameters.description:
The latest moment an entry may have, read in the time zone of the portal; left out, the log ends at the newest
entry.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description:
How many entries one page holds. The number of entries that match the query is reported in the response
headers, not in the body.

parameters.name: startIndex
parameters.description:
How many entries to skip before the page begins, counted from the newest one, so pages are taken by adding the
page size to it.

200.description: The activity entries of the file, newest first

400.description: A parameter has the wrong type, the `count` is outside its allowed range, or `fromDate` or `toDate` is not a date and time ending in `Z` or a UTC offset

403.description: The caller has no read access to the file

404.description: No file with this identifier exists

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

put.description:
Closes or reopens a revision group in the version history of a file. It returns every stored version of the
file, newest first. A `version` of 0 means the current version. With `continueVersion=false`, the call copies
the current version as a new version. That version starts a new revision group, so later edits no longer
extend the previous one. For an older `version`, or while someone edits the file, it changes nothing. With
`continueVersion=true`, the call merges the revision group after `version` into the group of `version`. If no
group follows it, nothing changes. Requires the right to change the version history, which a room manager and
a content creator have. Other callers get 403, including an editor. The call changes data. Do not repeat it.
With `continueVersion=false`, a repeat adds another version only if `version` is 0. With
`continueVersion=true`, each call merges the next revision group, if any, into the group of `version`. If the
body has no `version`, the call returns 400. If the file or the version does not exist, the call returns 404.
If copying the current version exceeds the room or user storage quota, the call returns 402. A file that another
user locked also returns 403. The call does not work for a file in the trash or on a third-party storage.

Queues the deletion of a file. It returns the file operations of the caller, including this one. By default,
the call moves the file to the trash, where you can restore it. With `immediately=true`, the call deletes the
file for good. It always deletes for good a file in the trash, an encrypted file, or a third-party file.
Requires the right to delete the file. Other callers get 403, including an editor. A room manager has this
right, and a content creator has it for their own files. The call queues work. Do not repeat it. A repeat
after the move to the trash deletes the file for good. The file may still be there when the response arrives.

learn if the deletion failed. With `deleteAfter=true`,
`GET api/2.0/files/fileops` stops listing the operation when it ends. So you cannot read its result. With
`returnSingleOperation=true`, the call returns only this deletion. If the file is locked by another user or
open for editing, the call returns 403. If no file has this id, the call returns 404. To delete several items,
use `PUT api/2.0/files/fileops/delete`.

filters of one user are visible only to that user. With the mode off, all users share the filters again.
Turning it on removes other users from the editing session. Requires the right to use the mode, which a room
manager has. Other callers get 403, including read-only access. Only the user who turned the mode on, a room
manager, or a DocSpace admin can turn it off. Other users get 403. The call
changes data, and you can repeat it with the same body. If the format does not support the mode, the call
returns 400. If no file has this id, the call returns 404.

post.description:
Restores an earlier version of a file and returns the editing revisions after the restore. The call stores the
content of the version again as a new version, with a comment that names it. The versions in between stay.
With `url`, the call takes the content from that address instead. The document service uses it to return a
document with some changes rolled back. Requires the right to change the version history. Other callers
get 403, including an anonymous caller. With `url`, the call also requires editing access. The call changes
data. Do not repeat it. Each call adds another version. The call deletes the links to drafts of the file. It
marks the file as new for the other users who can read it. If `version` is missing or is the current version,
the call returns 400. Without `url`, a `version` above the current one copies the current version. If the file
or the version does not exist, the call returns 404. If the content exceeds
the storage quota, the call returns 402. A file that another user locked also returns 403. Without `url`, the
call does not work for an encrypted file or a file that someone is editing. It also does not work for a file in
the trash or on a third-party storage.

Raises the `file.updated` webhook.

Returns the primary external link of a file, and creates it if the file has none. The body sets only a new link:
its rights, lifetime, password, download restriction, and sign-in requirement. In a personal section, a link
without `expirationDate` never expires. A new link to a PDF allows filling, except in a public room, where it is
read-only. For a form in a form-filling room, the call returns the link of the room. Requires the right to share
the file. Other callers get 403. The call changes data only when it creates the link. You can repeat it. Later
calls return the existing link and ignore the body. If the primary link was revoked, the call creates a new one
with a new ID. Until then, `GET api/2.0/files/file/{id}/link` returns 404. The call returns 403 if links to this
file cannot have this access level, or the link limit is reached. It also returns 403 if the portal allows
external links only in public rooms. It returns 400 if the password does not meet the password policy or
`expirationDate` is over 10 years ahead. If no file has this id, the call returns 404. The address is in
`sharedTo.shareLink`. To change the link, use `PUT api/2.0/files/file/{id}/links`.

call creates another link. With any other `linkId`, you can repeat it with the same body. The call returns

put.description:
Moves a file to a position in its folder and returns the file with its new `order`. Positions start at 1. The
call shifts the file at that position and all files after it, so the folder has no gaps. A position past the
end puts the file last. In a dotted path such as `1.2.3`, the call reads only the last part. The order matters
only in rooms with indexed contents. Elsewhere, the call stores it, but nothing uses it. Requires editing
access to the file. Other callers get 403. The call changes data, and you can repeat it with the same body. If
no file has this id, the call returns 404. If `order` is below 1 or is not a number, the call returns 400. To
move several items, use `PUT api/2.0/files/order`.

post.description:
Assigns the roles of a PDF form to users and starts the filling. The call marks the form as being filled and
records the caller as the user who started it. It notifies the users in the roles, except the caller. Members
who may only fill forms can then see the form. Each role has a name, an account, and a sequence number that
sets the turn. Roles with the same number are filled in parallel, and different numbers make a queue. The call
replaces the whole set of roles. In a virtual data room, an empty role list resets a stopped filling and
deletes the assignment. Elsewhere, or before a stop, an empty list returns 403. The call
reads the form id only from `formId` in the body. Send the same value in the route. The form must be a PDF in
a room. Requires the right to start or reset the filling, which a room manager and a content creator have.
Other callers get 403. The call changes data. Do not repeat it. In a virtual data room, a repeated call
returns 403. In a form-filling room, each call notifies the users in the roles again. If `roles` is missing,
the call returns 400. To read the stored roles, use `GET api/2.0/files/file/{fileId}/formroles`.

parameters.description: The form the role mapping belongs to. Send the same value as the `formId` of the request body, which is the one the handler reads.

put.description:
Changes the filling state of a PDF form as `action` sets. In a form-filling room, `Start` (2) opens the form
for filling to members who may only fill forms. If the form version differs from the one that `Edit`
remembered, `Start` also deletes the drafts of the previous round. The action `Stop` (0) stops the filling.
In a virtual data room, it records who stopped it and at which role. It also notifies the users of the other
roles. In a form-filling room, `Stop` closes the form for filling. The action `Resume` (1) continues a stopped
filling and clears that record. The action `Edit` (3) returns the form to editing, closes it for filling, and
remembers the version.
The call reads the form id only from `formId` in the body. Send the same value in the route. The form must be
a PDF in a room. The action `Start` requires the right to start the filling, which a room manager and a
content creator have. Other callers get 403. Only a room manager can stop a filling that another user started.
A content creator gets 403 there. In a form-filling room, `Edit` requires editing access to the form. The call
changes data. You can repeat `Resume` and `Edit` with the same body. A repeated `Stop` returns 403 in a
virtual data room and changes nothing in a form-filling room. Do not repeat `Start` in a form-filling room. A
repeat can delete the drafts that users started after the first call. If the body has no `formId`, the call
returns 400. If `action` is not a known value, the call returns 403. To read the resulting state, use
`GET api/2.0/files/file/{fileId}/formroles`.

Raises the `form.stopped` webhook for every `Stop`, even a repeated one, and for `Edit` that ends a started filling.

put.description:
Reports which fields of the original PDF form of a form-filling room the user renamed in the editor since it opened
`version`, told apart by the field ids the editor keeps. The editor sends it while editing, only when
`GET api/2.0/files/file/{fileId}/openedit` returns `trackFormFieldChanges` true. The caller
needs the right to edit the form; once its filling is started, a content creator keeps it only for a form they
created or started. A report replaces the previous one of the same `sessionId`, even after a forcesave, and one
whose `sequence` is not above the last of that session is dropped, so a repeated or late call is harmless; give
every editor tab its own `sessionId`. A field left out of `renames` kept its key. When the editor saves the
version, a renamed field keeps its earlier answers under its new name in the forms database and the spreadsheet
report. Ignored, still with 200: a `version` the form does not have yet, a compared one older than the last
earlier version with responses, a new session past 20 of one user on one version, a report past the renames the
form can keep. With Document Server Community Edition the call is refused with 403.

put.description:
Stores the file keys that let the named users open a file of an end-to-end encrypted private room. Each entry
names the account, the public key, and the key encrypted with it. So the portal never gets the plain key.
Before the call, encrypt the key for each recipient with the public key from
`GET api/2.0/files/file/{fileId}/publickeys`. The call replaces the keys of the named accounts and keeps all
other keys. Requires read access to the file and the right to create content in the room. Other callers
get 403. The call changes data. You can repeat it with the same body. If the file does not exist or is not in
a private room, the call also returns 403. If `fileId` is neither a number nor the id of a third-party file,
the call returns 404. The call skips recipients without read access to the file. It returns them in
`skippedUserIds`. To read the keys, use `GET api/2.0/files/{fileId}/access`.

parameters.description: The file the keys are issued for; it has to lie in a private room.

requestBody.description:

post.summary: Create a file in My documents
post.description:
Creates a file in the "My documents" section of the caller and returns it. The extension in the title sets the
format. The portal changes a known text, spreadsheet, or presentation extension to DOCX, XLSX, or PPTX. A title
without an extension gets DOCX. The portal keeps an unknown extension and a few other formats. If
`enableExternalExt` is true, the portal keeps the extension of the title in lower case. If `templateId` is set,
the portal copies that file and ignores `formId`. Otherwise, a nonzero `formId` makes the portal copy that form
from the form gallery. If neither is set, the portal uses its blank template for the format and the language of
the caller. If there is no such template, or `enableExternalExt` is true, the file is empty. Any signed-in user
can call it, except a guest. A guest who has My documents gets 403. The call changes data. Do not repeat it.
Each call creates another file. The returned title shows the extension that the portal stored. To create a file
in a room or another folder, use `POST api/2.0/files/{folderId}/file`. The call returns 400 if `title` is
missing, empty, or too long. It returns 402 if the file does not fit into a storage quota. It returns 403 if the
template does not exist or the caller cannot read it. It returns 404 for an unknown `formId` or a gallery form
without a file of the format of the title. If a string `templateId` is not a file of a connected third-party
storage, the call also returns 404.

saves `content` as the file content and returns the file. The portal adds `.html` to a title without it. If
`createNewIfExist` is true, the portal adds a version to the file with this title. If there is no such file,
it creates one. If `createNewIfExist` is false, the default, the portal creates another file with a unique
title, such as `Notes (1).html`. The portal does not update a file that is locked, open for editing, or
encrypted. It creates another file with the same title instead. Any signed-in user can call it, except a
guest. A guest who has My documents gets 403. Other guests get 404. The call changes data. A repeat with
`createNewIfExist` true adds a version. A repeat with false adds a numbered copy. To create the file in a room
or another folder, use `POST api/2.0/files/{folderId}/html`. The call returns 400 if `title` or `content` is
missing, or if `title` is blank or too long. It returns 402 if the content is too large for an upload or for a
storage quota.

post.summary: Open a form draft for filling
post.description:
Returns the editor address of a PDF form, or of a personal draft that it creates.
To start filling in a form-filling room, use `PUT api/2.0/files/file/{fileId}/manageformfilling` first.
Requires read access to the form. Other callers get 403. An external link holder can call it without signing
in. Without a sign-in or link key, the call returns 401. With `action` set to `view` or `embedded`, the call
returns the address of the form itself. It does the same for a caller who can edit the form, and before
filling starts. Otherwise, a caller with fill-forms access gets a personal draft. The first such call changes
data. It copies the form to the in-progress folder under the caller's name and clears its new mark. A repeated
call returns the same draft. It creates a new one if the draft is deleted, in Trash, or locked by another user.
Without a sign-in, each call creates a new draft. For an invalid draft, the call returns its address with a
notice to discard it. A draft becomes invalid if the form is deleted or changed, or the caller loses fill-forms
access. The next call on the form then creates a new draft. When the call creates or rejects a draft, the address
ends with a `#message/` notice for the editor. For the full editor configuration, use
`GET api/2.0/files/file/{fileId}/openedit`. The call returns 403 for a form in Trash or in a folder where the
caller cannot fill forms. It also returns 403 for a past revision without history access. The call returns
404 for an unknown file or revision. It returns 400 if the body has no `version`. It returns 415 for a format
the editors cannot open. It returns 402 if the draft exceeds the storage quota.

and the file stays where it is. Any signed-in user can call it. Although this is a GET, the call changes data.
You can repeat it with the same value. The call skips an unknown file and a file without read access. It never
marks an encrypted file of a private room. It returns the value of `favorite` even when it changes nothing. To
see the result, use `GET api/2.0/files/@favorites`. A marked file in the trash is not listed there until it is
restored. To change the marks of several files and folders, use `POST api/2.0/files/favorites` or
`DELETE api/2.0/files/favorites`. If a string id points to a storage account that is not connected, the call
returns 400. It also returns 400 if `favorite` is not a boolean. If a string id names an unknown storage type,
the call returns 404.

not check access, so you can delete a file that you can no longer read. Folder ids change nothing. If a
third-party storage no longer has the file, its entry stays. The call changes data. You can repeat it with the
same body. It returns an empty body and does not report what it deleted. The portal adds an entry again when
the caller opens the file or calls `POST api/2.0/files/file/{fileId}/recent`. The call reads only `fileIds`
and `folderIds` from the body. To hide the whole section, use `PUT api/2.0/files/displayrecent`. If a string

get.description:
Returns one page of the files that the caller opened recently. Each account has its own history, and the
section holds files only, so `folders` is empty. Any signed-in user can call it. The call is read-only, but
a valid `sortBy` becomes the account's default order. The call always sorts the list by the last
opening time, newest first. So `sortBy` and `sortOrder` do not change the order here. Without `searchArea`, or
with `Active`, the call lists files from personal sections and rooms, except form-filling rooms. With
`searchArea` set to `Forms`, it lists only files from form-filling rooms. If `searchArea` is `PrivateRooms`,
the call returns 400. Any other `searchArea` value lists all recent files. The call ignores
`applyFilterOption`. The `total` field counts all matching files. The call also
returns 400 if `metadataTemplateId` or `metadataFilters` names an unknown template or field, or has a
malformed condition. The portal adds a file to the section when the caller opens it. To add a file without
opening it, use `POST api/2.0/files/file/{fileId}/recent`. To clear the history, use
`DELETE api/2.0/files/recent`. This call works whether `PUT api/2.0/files/displayrecent` shows or hides the
section.

parameters.name: userIdOrGroupId
parameters.description:
Restricts the listing to the files authored by this portal member, or by the members of this group; the same
parameter accepts either kind of identifier. Omit it to list the whole history.

parameters.name: filterType
parameters.description:
Narrows the listing to a single kind of file, such as documents, spreadsheets or images. Omit it to list every
kind the history holds.

parameters.name: excludeSubject
parameters.description:
Inverts `userIdOrGroupId`: with `true` the files of that member or group are the ones left out of the listing
instead of the only ones kept.

parameters.name: applyFilterOption
parameters.description: Accepted for compatibility with the other folder listings and ignored: the "Recent" section holds files only.

parameters.name: searchArea
parameters.description:
The section of the portal that the recent files must come from. `Active`, which is what an omitted parameter
means, stands for the personal sections and the rooms other than form-filling rooms; `Forms` stands for the
form-filling rooms.

parameters.name: extension
parameters.description:
The file extensions the listing is limited to, matched against the end of the file name. The leading dot is
optional, and the parameter is repeated once per extension.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description:
The size of one page of section content. Pair it with `startIndex` to walk the listing, and compare the two
with `total` in the response to see when the last page has been read.

parameters.name: startIndex
parameters.description:
The number of matching entries to skip before the returned page begins; add `count` to it to ask for the next
page.

parameters.name: sortBy
parameters.description:
The name of the field the entries are ordered by, matched case-insensitively against the file sort fields:
`DateAndTime`, `AZ`, `Size`, `Author`, `Type`, `New`, `DateAndTimeCreation`, `RoomType`, `Tags`, `Room`,
`CustomOrder`, `LastOpened` and `UsedSpace`.

parameters.name: sortOrder
parameters.description: The direction in which the `sortBy` field is ordered.

parameters.name: filterValue
parameters.description:
The search string the history is filtered by: it is matched as a substring of file titles and against the
indexed document content as well. Omit it to list the whole history.

parameters.name: metadataTemplateId
parameters.description:
The ID of the metadata template the recent files must be assigned to. On its own it narrows the listing to the files
carrying the template; together with the metadata filters it also pins the template the filtered fields belong to.
The third-party files never carry metadata and are left out when the filter is set.

parameters.name: metadataFilters
parameters.description:
The URL-encoded JSON array of the metadata filter conditions,
e.g. [{"fieldId":1,"op":"contains","value":"ACME"},{"fieldId":2,"op":"range","from":"2026-01-01","to":"2026-06-30"},{"fieldId":3,"op":"in","optionIds":["..."]}].
A string field takes "eq" or "contains"; a number or a date field takes "range" with inclusive bounds, or "gt", "gte", "lt", "lte" with the bound in "value";
a date-only bound covers the whole day. A custom field is addressed by its name instead of the fieldId: {"name":"Client","op":"eq","value":"ACME"}.

parameters.name: includeHiddenMetadata
parameters.description:
Whether the text search, and the "metadataMatches" it reports, also look at the values of the hidden metadata
templates (created with "visible" false for the metadata a service keeps for itself, which the web client never
shows). False, the default, leaves them out, so an entry is not found by such a value; true takes them in.
"metadataTemplateId" and "metadataFilters" are not concerned: a hidden template or field named there is searched
either way.

post.description:
Opens a chunked upload session that replaces the content of an existing file. WebDAV apps save over a document
this way. No content is stored yet. Send the parts to `POST api/2.0/files/{folderId}/session/{sessionId}/upload`,
with the folder of the file as `folderId`. Then store the content with
`PUT api/2.0/files/{folderId}/session/{sessionId}/finalize`. The new content replaces the current version and
adds no version. The file also loses its encrypted state and its converted copy. Requires editing access to the
file. Other callers get 403. A guest also gets 403. The call changes data. A repeated call opens another
session. A
`fileSize` of -1 means the size is unknown, as for a WebDAV body without Content-Length. If the file does not
exist, the call returns 404. The call returns 400 if `fileSize` is below -1. It returns 402 if `fileSize` is
over the portal limit for chunked uploads. It also returns 403 if the file is locked, open in the editor, in
the trash, or encrypted.

before the session opens, and a session left at 0 takes the whole content in a single part.

Returns the history of a folder and of the entries inside it. Each record names the action, its time, and the
user who did it. The records of one action form one entry, and its other records are in `related`. The list
starts with the most recent entry. Paging with `startIndex` and `count` counts records, so a page can hold
fewer entries. The response headers carry the total number of records, and the body does not. Requires read
access to the folder. Other callers get 403. A caller who only fills forms in a form-filling folder sees only
the entries available to them. The call is read-only. If the folder does not exist,
the call returns 404. The call returns 400 if `count` is out of range or a date has a wrong format. To get
the history as a file, use `POST api/2.0/files/folder/{folderId}/log/report`.

oldest entry the portal still keeps.

entry.

post.summary: Start the folder history report generation
post.description:
Starts a job that saves the history of a folder as a report file in the caller's "My documents". The file is
an XLSX spreadsheet, or a CSV file if `format` is `Csv`. If both `from` and `to` are left out, the report
covers the whole history. Any user with read access to the folder can call it, except a guest. Other callers
get 403. The call queues work and returns the task, not the report. Repeat
`GET api/2.0/files/folder/{folderId}/log/report` until `isCompleted` is true. Then take the file from

repeat the call. While a report of the same folder and caller runs, the call returns that task. It starts no

including the new job. Requires the right to delete the folder. Other callers get 403. The room manager and a
content creator who owns the folder have this right. Editing access is not enough, and a guest also gets 403.
The call queues work and changes data. Do not repeat it. A repeat deletes for good the folder that the first
call moved to the trash. After a deletion for good, a repeated call returns 404. The folder may still exist when
the response arrives. Repeat `GET api/2.0/files/fileops` until the job has `finished` set to true. Then read its
`error` to see if the deletion failed. If `deleteAfter` is true, `GET api/2.0/files/fileops` does not list the
job after it finishes. By default, the job moves the folder to the trash, where you can restore it. If
`immediately` is true, the deletion is final. The deletion is always final in the trash and for a private room
itself. Its subfolders go to the trash. The same applies to the root folder of a connected storage. If a file
inside is blocked, for example open for editing, the job deletes nothing. The call also returns 403 for a room
if `immediately` is not true. If the folder does not exist, the call returns 404. To delete several items in one
call, use `PUT api/2.0/files/fileops/delete`.

get.description:
Returns one page of the contents of a folder. The response has the subfolders in `folders`, the files in
`files`, and the folder itself in `current`. The chain of parent folders is in `pathParts`. Requires read
access to the folder. Other callers get 403. Without signing in, a caller needs an external link to the
folder. The call changes data of the caller only. It clears the new-item marks of the folder. It also saves a
valid `sortBy` and `sortOrder` as the default order of the account. You can repeat it. With a filter, the
call searches the whole subtree by default. The text filter also searches indexed document content. Indexing
runs in the background, so a new file can be missing from the results at first. Use `count` and `startIndex`
to page through the result. The `total` field counts all matching entries. To filter by metadata with a typed
body, use `POST api/2.0/files/{folderId}/search`. The call returns 400 for a wrong parameter type, a `count`
out of range, or a negative `startIndex`. An invalid metadata filter also returns 400. It also returns 400 if `roomId` is not a
number but the folder ID is. It also returns 403 for a folder in the trash. If the folder does not exist, the
call returns 404. For an anonymous caller, it returns 403 instead.

parameters.name: folderId
parameters.description:
The folder whose contents are listed. Each section root has an operation of its own, such as
`GET api/2.0/files/@my`, and every other folder is opened by the identifier a listing gave for it.

parameters.name: userIdOrGroupId
parameters.description:
Restricts the listing to the entries authored by this portal member, or by the members of this group; the same
parameter accepts either kind of identifier. Omit it to list everything the caller can read.

parameters.name: sharedBy
parameters.description:
Restricts the listing to the entries this member shared, which narrows a shared listing down to what one
person handed out.

parameters.name: filterType
parameters.description:
Narrows the listing to a single kind of entry, such as documents, spreadsheets, images or one type of room.
Omit it to list every kind the folder holds.

parameters.name: roomId
parameters.description:
Keeps only the entries that lie in this room, which matters when the listing being read gathers entries from
more than one of them.

parameters.name: folderType
parameters.description:
Keeps only the folders of these kinds, each given as the number of a folder type; it is how a listing is
narrowed down to, say, the form-filling folders of a room.

[0 - Default, 1 - Coomon, 2 - Bunch, 3 - Trash, 5 - User, 6 - Share, 8 - Projects, 10 - Favourites, 11 - Recent, 12 - Templates, 13 - Privacy, 14 - Virtual rooms, 15 - Filling forms room, 16 - Editing room, 19 - Custom room, 20 - Archive, 21 - Thirdparty backup, 22 - Public room, 25 - Ready form folder, 26 - In process form folder, 27 - Form filling folder done, 28 - Form filling folder in progress, 29 - Virtual Data Room, 30 - Room templates folder, 31 - AI Room, 32 - Knowledge, 33 - Chat outputs, 34 - AI Agents, 35 - Default Templates, 36 - Forms, 37 - Ai, 38 - Instructions room, 39 - Knowledge room, 40 - AI project room, 41 - AI rooms, 42 - Private rooms]

Turns `userIdOrGroupId` around: with true the entries of that member or group are the ones left out, with

Chooses which half of the listing `filterType` and `filterValue` are applied to: with `Files` the folders come
back unfiltered, with `Folders` the files do, and with `All` both halves are filtered.

parameters.description:
Whether a narrowed request reaches into the subfolders: with true, which is what an omitted parameter means,
matching entries are gathered from the whole subtree, with false only the top level is read. It makes a

with `total` in the response to see when the last page has been read.

parameters.name: startIndex
parameters.description:

page.

parameters.name: sortBy
parameters.description:
The name of the field the entries are ordered by, matched case-insensitively against the file sort fields:
`DateAndTime`, `AZ`, `Size`, `Author`, `Type`, `New`, `DateAndTimeCreation`, `RoomType`, `Tags`, `Room`,
`CustomOrder`, `LastOpened` and `UsedSpace`. A recognized value is also saved as the default order of the
account and reused by later listings that omit the parameter, while a value matching none of the fields leaves
that saved order in place.

of the account.

parameters.name: filterValue
parameters.description:
The search string the listing is filtered by: it is matched as a substring of entry titles and, for files,
against the indexed document content as well. Omit it to list the folder unfiltered.

parameters.name: location
parameters.description:
Where the entries of a tag-based listing have to live to be kept: `Room` keeps what lies in a room,
`Documents` what lies in a personal section, and `Link` what was reached through an external link that is
still valid. It shapes the "Favorites" and "Recent" listings and does nothing in an ordinary folder.

parameters.name: metadataTemplateId
parameters.description:
The ID of the metadata template the entries must be assigned to. On its own it narrows the listing to the entries
carrying the template; together with the metadata filters it also pins the template the filtered fields belong to.
Supported for the rooms, the trash, the regular folders and the "Shared with me", "Recent" and "Favorites" sections
(the third-party entries never carry metadata and are left out); the "Templates" and "Private" sections reject it with 400.

parameters.name: metadataFilters
parameters.description:
The URL-encoded JSON array of the metadata filter conditions,
e.g. [{"fieldId":1,"op":"contains","value":"ACME"},{"fieldId":2,"op":"range","from":"2026-01-01","to":"2026-06-30"},{"fieldId":3,"op":"in","optionIds":["..."]}].
A string field takes "eq" (the whole value) or "contains" (a part of it); a number or a date field takes "range" with inclusive bounds,
or "gt", "gte", "lt", "lte" with the single bound in "value"; a choice field takes "in". A date-only bound covers the whole day,
so "to":"2026-06-30" includes the values stored on 30 June and "gt":"2026-06-30" starts after it.
A custom field is addressed by its name instead of the fieldId: {"name":"Client","op":"eq","value":"ACME"}.

shows). False, the default, leaves them out, so an entry is not found by such a value; true takes them in.
"metadataTemplateId" and "metadataFilters" are not concerned: a hidden template or field named there is searched
either way.

post.description:
Returns the primary external link of a folder or a room, and creates it if it does not exist. The call uses
the body only when it creates the link. If the link exists, the call returns it unchanged. Requires the right
to manage the links of the folder. Other callers get 403. The room manager has this right, but a content
creator does not. The call changes data only when it creates the link. You can repeat it, and later calls
return the same link. To change a link, use `PUT api/2.0/files/folder/{id}/links`. If `access` grants nothing,
the call creates no link and returns an empty response. Read the address from `sharedTo.shareLink`. The call
returns 400 if the title or password is too long, or the password breaks the portal policy. It also returns
400 if `expirationDate` is more than 10 years ahead. It also returns 403 if folder links cannot have this
access level. The link limit and a ban on external links outside public rooms also return 403. If the folder
does not exist, the call returns 404. If the primary link was revoked, the call creates a new one with a new
ID. Until then, `GET api/2.0/files/folder/{id}/link` returns 404.

put.description:
Creates or changes an external link of a folder or a room, or revokes it. The `linkId` field selects the link. A new
or empty ID creates a link, and an existing ID changes that link. The call applies all fields every time, so a
missing field gets its default value. Requires the right to manage the links of the folder. Other callers
get 403. The room manager has this right. The call changes data. A repeated call with an existing `linkId`
changes nothing. A repeated call with an empty `linkId` creates one more link. If `access` grants nothing, the
call revokes the link and returns an empty response. A later read does not recreate a revoked primary link.
In a public room or a form-filling room, revoking the primary link creates a new one with default settings.
The call then returns the new link. A repeated revocation finds no link and returns an empty response. If the
link limit is reached, it returns 403 instead. The call returns 400 if the title or password is too long, or the
password breaks the portal policy. It also returns 400 if `expirationDate` is more than 10 years ahead. It also
returns 403 if folder links cannot have this access level or the link limit is reached. The admin's restriction
on external links can also return 403. If the folder does not exist, the call returns 404.

get.description:
Returns one page of the files and folders that the caller marked as favorite. Each account has its own
favorites, so the marks of other members do not show here. Any signed-in user can call it. The call is
read-only, but a valid `sortBy` becomes the account's default order. The list shows folders
first, then files, each in the `sortBy` order or the saved default. The `total` field
counts all matching entries. The list skips entries in the trash and entries that the caller can no longer
read. Their favorite marks stay. The call returns 400 if `metadataTemplateId` or `metadataFilters` names an
unknown template or field, or has a malformed condition. To add or remove favorites, use
`POST api/2.0/files/favorites` or `DELETE api/2.0/files/favorites`. To mark one file, you can also use
`GET api/2.0/files/favorites/{fileId}`.

parameters.description:

every kind the section holds.

`DateAndTime`, `AZ`, `Size`, `Author`, `Type`, `New`, `DateAndTimeCreation`, `RoomType`, `Tags`, `Room`,
`CustomOrder`, `LastOpened` and `UsedSpace`. Omit it to use the saved default order of the account.

parameters.description:

parameters.description:
The ID of the metadata template the entries must be assigned to. On its own it narrows the listing to the entries
carrying the template; together with the metadata filters it also pins the template the filtered fields belong to.
The third-party entries never carry metadata and are left out when the filter is set.

a date-only bound covers the whole day. A custom field is addressed by its name instead of the fieldId: {"name":"Client","op":"eq","value":"ACME"}.

templates (created with "visible" false for the metadata a service keeps for itself, which the web client never
shows). False, the default, leaves them out, so an entry is not found by such a value; true takes them in.
"metadataTemplateId" and "metadataFilters" are not concerned: a hidden template or field named there is searched
either way.

get.description:
Returns every top-level section that the caller can see, each with its first page of content. Sections come
in this order: "Favorites", "Recent", "Shared with me", "My documents", "Trash", "Rooms", "Forms", and
"Archive". While the private rooms app is on, "Private rooms" comes before "Archive". While AI access is on for
the portal, the AI agents and AI hub sections follow. The list has
"Recent" only after `PUT api/2.0/files/displayrecent` turns it on. It skips "My documents" if the account has
none, which is usual for a guest. To skip "Trash", set `withoutTrash` to `true`. Any signed-in user can call
it. The call is read-only, but a valid `sortBy` becomes the account's default order. It does not clear
new-item marks. The filters, `count`, and `startIndex` apply to each section. So `count=1` returns one entry
per section, and each section has its own `total`. This is the most expensive listing of the module. When you
need one section, read it directly, for example with `GET api/2.0/files/@my`. The call returns 400 if `count`
is outside its allowed range.

get.description:
Returns one page of the "Forms" section, the list of form-filling rooms that the caller can read. The
call does not open the rooms, so `files` is empty. To read a room, use `GET api/2.0/files/{folderId}` with
its ID. Any signed-in user can call it. The call is read-only, but a valid `sortBy` becomes the
account's default order. The `total` field counts all matching rooms. The call returns 400 if
`metadataTemplateId` or `metadataFilters` names an unknown template or field, or has a malformed condition. In
`GET api/2.0/files/rooms`, these rooms show only when `searchArea` is `Forms`.

parameters.name: userIdOrGroupId
parameters.description:
Restricts the listing to the entries authored by this portal member, or by the members of this group; the same
parameter accepts either kind of identifier. Omit it to list everything the caller can read.

parameters.name: filterType
parameters.description:
Narrows the listing to a single kind of entry, such as documents, images or one type of room. Omit it to list
every kind the section holds.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description:
The size of one page of section content. Pair it with `startIndex` to walk the listing, and compare the two
with `total` in the response to see when the last page has been read.

parameters.name: startIndex
parameters.description:
The number of matching entries to skip before the returned page begins; add `count` to it to ask for the next
page.

parameters.name: sortBy
parameters.description:
The name of the field the entries are ordered by, matched case-insensitively against the file sort fields:
`DateAndTime`, `AZ`, `Size`, `Author`, `Type`, `New`, `DateAndTimeCreation`, `RoomType`, `Tags`, `Room`,
`CustomOrder`, `LastOpened` and `UsedSpace`. Omit it to use the saved default order of the account.

parameters.name: sortOrder
parameters.description: The direction in which the `sortBy` field is ordered.

parameters.name: filterValue
parameters.description:
The search string the section is filtered by: it is matched as a substring of entry titles and, for files,
against the indexed document content as well. Omit it to list the section unfiltered.

parameters.name: metadataTemplateId
parameters.description:
The ID of the metadata template the entries must be assigned to. On its own it narrows the listing to the entries
carrying the template; together with the metadata filters it also pins the template the filtered fields belong to.
The third-party entries never carry metadata and are left out when the filter is set.

parameters.name: metadataFilters
parameters.description:
The URL-encoded JSON array of the metadata filter conditions,
e.g. [{"fieldId":1,"op":"contains","value":"ACME"},{"fieldId":2,"op":"range","from":"2026-01-01","to":"2026-06-30"},{"fieldId":3,"op":"in","optionIds":["..."]}].
A string field takes "eq" or "contains"; a number or a date field takes "range" with inclusive bounds, or "gt", "gte", "lt", "lte" with the bound in "value";
a date-only bound covers the whole day. A custom field is addressed by its name instead of the fieldId: {"name":"Client","op":"eq","value":"ACME"}.

parameters.name: includeHiddenMetadata
parameters.description:
Whether the text search, and the "metadataMatches" it reports, also look at the values of the hidden metadata
templates (created with "visible" false for the metadata a service keeps for itself, which the web client never
shows). False, the default, leaves them out, so an entry is not found by such a value; true takes them in.
"metadataTemplateId" and "metadataFilters" are not concerned: a hidden template or field named there is searched
either way.

200.description: The "Forms" section with one page of the form-filling rooms available to the caller

400.description: A parameter has the wrong type, the `count` is outside its allowed range, the `startIndex` is negative, or the metadata filter names an unknown template or field

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

get.description:
Returns the private rooms section: the flat list of end-to-end encrypted rooms the caller is a member of. Such
rooms are stored under the "Rooms" tree but are surfaced only here, so `GET api/2.0/files/rooms` leaves them out of
the active area and lists them when `searchArea` names the private rooms area instead. An administrator who is not
a member does not see a private room here either. The section is not expanded into room content, so `folders`
carries the rooms while `files` comes back empty; to read what is inside one of them, call
`GET api/2.0/files/{folderId}` with the room identifier. Nothing is modified, though passing `sortBy` saves the
requested order as the default order for this account. `filterType`, `filterValue`, `userIdOrGroupId` and the
sorting parameters narrow and order the room list, `metadataTemplateId` and `metadataFilters` keep only the rooms
carrying the template and matching the conditions, `count` and `startIndex` page through it, `total` reports how
many rooms match the request in full, and `current` describes the section folder itself. Archived private rooms
stay in the archive area; narrow it with `privacyFilter` of `GET api/2.0/files/rooms`.

post.description:
Returns the names from `filesTitle` that a file in the folder already has. Use it before an upload to choose
between a new version and another name. The match ignores case. The call skips encrypted files, since an
upload cannot replace them. Requires the right to create content in the folder. Other callers get 403. In a
room, its owner, room managers, and content creators have it. A guest has it there only as a content creator.
In My documents, the owner and anyone with read and write access to the folder have it. An archived room, the
Archive or room templates root, and an AI agent or AI project root also return 403. The call is read-only. The
list has no repeats and no order. An empty list means that every name is free. A missing folder returns 404.
The call returns 400 if `filesTitle` is missing. An empty `filesTitle` returns an empty list. In a form-filling
room template, a name without the `.pdf` extension returns 403.

parameters.name: folderId
parameters.description:
The folder whose contents the names are tested against; take the id from a listing such as
`GET api/2.0/files/@root`.

requestBody.description: The names to test against the files the folder already holds.

schema.description: The names to test against the files the folder already holds.

400.description: The request body cannot be read or has no `filesTitle`

403.description: The caller cannot add content to the folder, or a title that is not a PDF is checked against a form-filling room template
