post.description:
Uploads a file to the folder in one request and names it by `title`. The content can be a multipart part or
the raw request body. To name the file by the uploaded part, use `POST api/2.0/files/{folderId}/upload`.
Requires the right to create content in the folder. Other callers get 403. In a room, its owner, room managers,
and content creators have it. A guest has it there only as a content creator. In My documents, the owner and
anyone with read and write access to the folder have it. A section root, an archived or private room, and an
AI agent or AI project root also return 403. The call changes data. It removes characters that a title cannot
have and shortens a long name. If the folder has a file with this name, `createNewIfExist` true stores a copy
with a numeric suffix. With false, the call adds a new version to that file if the caller can edit it.
Otherwise, it stores a second file with the same name. A guest never adds a version this way. So a repeated
call adds another version or another file. A `version` above 1 in the response means that the call added a
version. The portal converts some formats in the background after the upload. To read that result with
`GET api/2.0/files/file/{fileId}/checkconversion`, pass `keepConvertStatus`. A missing folder returns 404.
The call returns 402 if the file is over the upload limit or a storage quota. If the installation does not
allow uploads with this extension, the call returns 415. If the file is not a PDF and the room is a
form-filling room, the call returns 403. To upload a large file, use `POST api/2.0/files/{folderId}/session`.

Raises the `file.created` and `file.uploaded` webhooks for a new file and for a new version of an existing file.

parameters.name: folderId
parameters.description:
The folder that receives the file; take the id from a listing such as `GET api/2.0/files/@root`. A room or an
ordinary folder inside one is accepted, a section root is not.

insertFile.file.description:
The content to store, sent as a `multipart/form-data` part. The same content may instead be sent as the raw
request body, which is what a client that cannot build a form does; when both are present the form part wins.

insertFile.title.description:
The name to store the file under, extension included. It wins over the name of the uploaded part, which is the
reason to choose this operation over the plain upload, and it is the only name available when the content
arrives as a raw body. Characters a title cannot hold are replaced with underscores and the name is cut to 170
characters before the file is stored.

insertFile.createNewIfExist.description:
Settles the clash with a file already carrying that title: left out, the content is written as the next
version of that file; set to true, both survive and the new one gets a numeric suffix in its title.

insertFile.keepConvertStatus.description:
Decides whether the outcome of the background conversion outlives the conversion itself. True keeps the queue
record, so `GET api/2.0/files/file/{fileId}/checkconversion` can still report the result or the error; left
out, the record is cleared the moment the conversion ends and that call finds nothing.

200.description: The stored file with its id and the title it was actually saved under; a `version` above 1 means the content was added to a file that already carried this name instead of creating a new one

installation does not allow the file extension, the call returns 415. To store a file in another folder, use
`POST api/2.0/files/{folderId}/insert`.

get.description:
Returns the metadata templates of the portal with their fields. A template is a set of fields that describes a file,
a folder, or a room. Any signed-in user can call it. The call is read-only. Every caller gets the same list. The
templates come in the order of their creation. Their fields come in display order, with the options of choice
fields. Without `visible`, the call returns both shown and hidden templates. The author and the last editor of a
template come as user objects. An empty list means the portal has no templates. The custom text fields of entries
are not templates, and the call does not return them. To read them, use `GET api/2.0/files/metadata/file/{fileId}`
or `GET api/2.0/files/metadata/folder/{folderId}`.

parameters.name: visible
parameters.description: Filters the templates by their visibility.

200.description: List of metadata templates

400.description: Bad Request.

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

post.description:
Creates a metadata template of the portal together with its fields. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers
get 403. The call changes data. A repeated call returns 400, since the name is then taken. A field without `order` goes
after the fields with one, in the order of the request. The response is the created template with the generated
option IDs. The values of `PUT api/2.0/files/metadata/file/{fileId}/values` refer to these IDs. To add fields
later, use `POST api/2.0/files/metadata/templates/{templateId}/fields`. The call compares names regardless of case.
It returns 400 if `fields` is empty, or the name is empty, `System`, or taken. It also returns 400 for a name
over 255 characters, repeated field names, an unknown field type, or wrong options. A choice field needs at least
one option, and its options must be unique. Other field types take no options. If any field is invalid, the call
creates nothing.

schema.description: The request parameters for creating a metadata template.

200.description: The created template with its fields and the generated identifiers of their options

400.description: An invalid template or field: no fields, a name in use, reserved or too long, an unknown field type, duplicate field names or wrong options

403.description: The caller is not a DocSpace admin

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

Returns one metadata template with its fields and the options of its choice fields. The fields come in display
order. Any signed-in user can call it. The call is read-only. Use it to get the names and fields of the IDs
in `assignedMetadataTemplates` of a file or a folder. If no template has this ID, the call returns 404.

put.description:
Renames a metadata template or changes whether it is shown in the pickers. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other
callers get 403. The call changes data, and you can repeat it with the same body. A property left out keeps its
value. This call does not change the fields. To change a field, use
`PUT api/2.0/files/metadata/templates/{templateId}/fields/{fieldId}`. With `visible` false, the template keeps its
assignments and values. Its fields leave the pickers, the filling, and the default text search. An entry with the
template then has `hasMetadataFields` false if no other visible template or custom field gives it fields. With
`visible` true, the call reverses this. The response is the whole template with its fields. If no template has
this ID, the call returns 404. The call returns 400 if another template has the new name in any case. It also
returns 400 for a name over 255 characters.

put.description:
Starts a background job that packs files and folders into one archive. The call converts the files of
`fileConvertIds` before it packs them. Requires the right to download the listed items. If the caller can
download none of them, the call returns 403. A room that forbids downloads denies this right to the Read role.
The settings of an external link can deny it too. The call checks the portal's own items and the items on
third-party storage as two separate groups. Each group with listed items needs one item the caller can
download. The archive skips the items the caller cannot download and the ids that do not exist. A caller who
is not signed in needs an external link to the items. Without one, the call returns 401. The call queues work.
Repeat `GET api/2.0/files/fileops` until `finished` is true. Then take the archive address from `url`. Do not
repeat the call while the job runs. Until it ends, each call of the same caller returns 403, even with an empty
selection. At other times, an empty selection queues nothing and returns the existing operations. The call
returns the download operations of the caller, including the new one. If no listed item of a group exists, the
call returns 404. The call returns 400 if the body cannot be read or an item of `fileConvertIds` has no `key` or
`value`.

Raises the `folder.downloaded` webhook for each listed folder or room when the job packs it, not for the folders inside. Raises the `file.downloaded` webhook for each listed file when the job packs it, not for the files inside listed folders.

put.description:
Starts a background job that copies files and folders into `destFolderId`. With `content` true, the call copies
the content of each listed folder, not the folder. Requires the right to create content in the destination and
to copy every listed item. Other callers get 403. In a room, room managers and content creators can create
content. A room that forbids downloads denies copying to the Read role. The call queues work. Repeat `GET
api/2.0/files/fileops` until `finished` is true. Its `files` and `folders` then name the copies. What a repeated
call does depends on `conflictResolveType`. With `Skip`, it skips clashing files, except encrypted files, rooms,
and copies into knowledge folders. With `Overwrite`, it adds a new version to each earlier copy of a file. With
`Duplicate`, it makes new copies under new names. The call returns the copy operations of the caller, including
the new one. An empty selection queues nothing and returns the existing operations. To find name clashes first,
use `GET api/2.0/files/fileops/move`. To check that the destination accepts the files, use `GET
api/2.0/files/fileops/checkdestfolder`. To move the items instead, use `PUT api/2.0/files/fileops/move`. The
call also returns 403 if the destination is inside a listed folder. A listed folder that would exceed a room or
user quota also returns 403. It also returns 403 if a file to overwrite is locked, open for editing, or not
editable by the caller. A file that is not a PDF form sent to a form-filling room also returns 403. A listed
file too large for a knowledge folder also returns 403. If the destination or a listed file or folder does not
exist, the call returns 404. The call returns 415 for a file format the portal does not accept for upload. It
also returns 415 for a format a knowledge folder cannot index.

Raises the `folder.copied` webhook for every copied folder, and for its subfolders only within one storage. Raises the `room.copied` webhook for every listed room copied into its own section, an AI agent included. Raises the `file.copied` webhook for every copied file, and for files inside copied folders only within one storage.

put.description:
Starts a background job that deletes files and folders. With `immediately` false, the call moves them to the
Trash of the caller. With `immediately` true, it deletes them for good. It always deletes for good the items in
the Trash, in a private room, or on a third-party storage. The call deletes a folder with all its content.
Requires the right to delete each listed item. Other callers get 403. In a room, a room manager can delete any
item, and a content creator only their own. The call queues work, and a deletion for good cannot be undone.
Repeat `GET api/2.0/files/fileops` until `finished` is true. A failure on one item shows in `error`, not as a
status code. Do not repeat the call. A repeat deletes for good the items that the first call moved to the Trash.
It moves the items restored in the meantime to the Trash again. After a deletion for good, a repeated call
returns 404. The call returns the delete operations of the caller, including the new one. An empty selection
queues nothing and returns the existing operations. To empty the Trash, use `PUT
api/2.0/files/fileops/emptytrash`. The call also returns 403 if an item is locked by another user or open for
editing. It also returns 403 for a room when `immediately` is false. If a listed file or folder does not exist,
the call returns 404.

Raises the `folder.trashed` webhook for every listed folder moved to the trash, not for the folders inside it. Raises the `folder.deleted` webhook instead for a listed folder deleted for good, not moved to the trash. Raises the `room.deleted` webhook for every listed room. Raises the `agent.deleted` webhook instead for a listed AI agent. Raises the `file.trashed` webhook for every listed file moved to the trash, not for the files inside listed folders. Raises the `file.deleted` webhook instead for a listed file deleted for good, not moved to the trash.

put.description:
Starts a background job that deletes versions from the history of one file. The file stays with its other
versions. An empty `versions` list deletes the whole file instead. Requires the right to delete the file.
Other callers get 403. A DocSpace admin also gets 403 for a file in the personal documents of another user.
The call queues work, and deleted versions cannot be restored. Repeat `GET api/2.0/files/fileops` until
`finished` is true. A failure during the job shows in `error`, not as a status code. The call skips version
numbers that do not exist, so you can repeat it. The call returns the delete operations of the caller,
including the new one. To delete the file itself, use `PUT api/2.0/files/fileops/delete`. The call also
returns 403 if `versions` includes the current version. It also returns 403 if the file is locked, open for
editing, in an archived room, or in the Trash. If the file does not exist, the call returns 404. The call
returns 400 if the body cannot be read or has no `fileId` or `versions`.

Raises the `file.updated` webhook once for every removed version. Raises the `file.deleted` webhook instead when `versions` is empty, which deletes the whole file for good.

put.description:
Starts a background job that deletes for good the content of the Trash of the caller. With `folderType`, the
call deletes only the items that came from sections or rooms of those types. Without it, the call empties the
whole Trash. Any signed-in user can call it. The call queues work, and the deletion cannot be undone. Repeat
`GET api/2.0/files/fileops` until `finished` is true. You can repeat the call. A repeat while a job of this
call still runs can show `error` for the items that job deleted. On an empty Trash, the call queues nothing and
returns the existing operations. The call returns the delete operations of the caller, including the new one.
To move items to the Trash, use `PUT api/2.0/files/fileops/delete`. If `folderType` is not a folder type, the
call returns 400.

Raises the `folder.deleted` webhook for every folder lying directly in the trash. Raises the `file.deleted` webhook for each file directly in the trash, not for the files inside trashed folders.

get.description:
Returns the background file operations of the caller that still run or have an unread result. The list starts
with duplications, then moves and copies, deletions, downloads, mark-as-read jobs, and builder runs. Anyone
can call it without signing in. Each caller sees only their own operations. An anonymous caller sees the
operations of their external link session. This is the call to poll. Repeat it until `finished` is true. A
finished operation appears in one answer only, here or in the answer of the call that started it. So an empty
list means nothing is left to report, not that the work failed. An unknown `id` returns an empty list. To read
one kind of operation, use `GET api/2.0/files/fileops/{operationType}`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The operation to report on, as returned in `id` when it was started; without it every operation of the caller
is reported. An id that is not among the caller's operations gives an empty answer rather than an error.

without signing in. Each caller sees only their own operations. As in `GET api/2.0/files/fileops`, a finished

records. The path `api/2.0/files/fileops/move` belongs to another operation. If `operationType` is not a known
kind, the call returns 400.

Starts a background job that clears the new-item badges of files and folders for the caller. Marking a folder
also clears the badges of its content. Other members keep their badges. Any signed-in user can call it. The
call skips the items the caller cannot read and the ids that do not exist, without an error. The call queues
work. Repeat `GET api/2.0/files/fileops` until `finished` is true. You can repeat it with the same body. The
call returns the mark-as-read operations of the caller, including the new one. An empty selection queues
nothing and returns the existing operations. To see new items, use `GET api/2.0/files/{folderId}/news` for a
folder or `GET api/2.0/files/rooms/news` for rooms.

put.description:
Starts a background job that moves files and folders into `destFolderId`. With `content` true, the call moves
the content of each listed folder, not the folder. Requires the right to create content in the destination and
to remove the items from their source. Other callers get 403. In a room, room managers and content creators
have the right to create content. In a room, a content creator can move only the items they created. The call
queues work. Repeat `GET api/2.0/files/fileops` until `finished` is true. What a repeated call does depends on
`conflictResolveType`. With `Skip`, it changes nothing. With `Overwrite`, it adds to each listed file a new
version of itself. With `Duplicate`, it gives each listed folder a new name and a new id. The call returns the
move operations of the caller, including the new one. An empty selection queues nothing and returns the
existing operations. A room can move only between the Rooms section and the archive. To archive a room, use
`PUT api/2.0/files/rooms/{id}/archive`. To find name clashes first, use `GET api/2.0/files/fileops/move`. To
check that the destination accepts the files, use `GET api/2.0/files/fileops/checkdestfolder`. To keep the
originals, use `PUT api/2.0/files/fileops/copy`. The call also returns 403 if the destination is inside a
listed folder. A listed folder that would exceed a room or user quota also returns 403. It also returns 403 if
a listed file is locked or open for editing. A file open for editing inside a listed folder also returns 403.
A file to overwrite that is locked, open for editing, or not editable by the caller also returns 403. A file
that is not a PDF form sent to a form-filling room also returns 403. A folder or several files moved into a
form-filling room from outside also return 403. A listed file too large for a knowledge folder also returns
403. If the destination or a listed file or folder does not exist, the call returns 404. The call returns 415
for a file format the portal does not accept for upload. It also returns 415 for a format a knowledge folder
cannot index.

Raises the `folder.moved` webhook for each listed folder, and for subfolders of a merged folder. Raises the `folder.copied` webhook instead for a listed folder merged into an existing one. Raises the `folder.restored` webhook instead for a folder moved out of the trash. Raises the `room.archived` webhook for every listed room moved to the archive. Raises the `room.restored` webhook for every listed room moved out of the archive. Raises the `file.moved` webhook for each listed file, and for files of merged folders. Raises the `file.restored` webhook instead for a file moved out of the trash.

get.description:
Returns the listed files and folders that have a same-named item in `destFolderId`. Use it to settle name
clashes before a move or a copy. With `content` true, the call checks the content of each listed folder
instead of the folder. Requires the right to create content in the destination. Other callers get 403. The
call is read-only, though `PUT api/2.0/files/fileops/move` has the same path. An empty list means no clashes.
The call ignores `conflictResolveType`, encrypted files, and ids that do not exist. It checks only the listed
folders the caller can read. To check that the destination accepts the files, use
`GET api/2.0/files/fileops/checkdestfolder`. The call also returns 403 if the destination is an archived room,
a listed folder, or inside one. A file or a plain folder sent to the Rooms, Forms, or AI agents root also
returns 403. A plain folder sent to a knowledge folder or the archive also returns 403. A room sent anywhere
except the Rooms root or the archive also returns 403. If the destination does not exist, the call
returns 404. Without `destFolderId`, the call returns 400.

get.description:
Returns whether the destination folder accepts the listed files before a move or a copy. The call reads only
`fileIds` and `destFolderId` from the request. A form-filling room accepts only PDF forms. Every other folder
accepts every file. A file listed twice counts once. Requires the right to create content in the destination.
Other callers get 403. The call also returns 403 for an archived room and for the Rooms, Forms, and AI agents
section roots. The call is read-only. It does not look for name clashes. To find them, use
`GET api/2.0/files/fileops/move`. If the destination does not exist, the call returns 404. Without
`destFolderId`, the call returns 400.

returns every operation of the same kind that the caller has running or unread. When nothing was queued, which
happens for an empty selection, `true` falls back to the full list.

put.description:
Cancels a background file operation of the caller and returns the operations that are left. Without `id`, the
call cancels every running operation of the caller. Anyone can call it without signing in. A caller can cancel
only their own operations. An anonymous caller reaches only the operations of their external link session. The
call stops the job but does not undo it. Items already copied, moved, or deleted stay that way. You can repeat
the call. An unknown `id` cancels nothing and is not an error. The answer is usually empty. After the job
stops, `GET api/2.0/files/fileops` lists it once, finished, with the status `Canceled`.

parameters.description:
The operation to cancel, as returned in `id` when it was started. A call that leaves the route segment out
cancels every operation of the caller, and an id that is not among their operations cancels nothing without
being an error.

post.description:
Marks files and folders as favorites of the calling account. Other users do not see the mark, and the entries
stay where they are. Any signed-in user can call it. The call skips items without read access, unknown ids,
and encrypted files of a private room. The call changes data. You can repeat it with the same body, and a
marked item stays listed once. It returns `true` even when it marks nothing. To see the result, use
`GET api/2.0/files/@favorites`. A marked entry in the trash is not listed there until it is restored. The call
reads only `fileIds` and `folderIds` from the body. To delete marks, use `DELETE api/2.0/files/favorites`. To
mark one file, use `GET api/2.0/files/favorites/{fileId}`. If a string id points to a storage account that is
not connected, the call returns 400. If it names an unknown storage type, the call returns 404.

unchanged and no longer appear in `GET api/2.0/files/@favorites`. Marks of other users stay. Any signed-in

same body. It returns `true` even when it deletes nothing. The call reads only `fileIds` and `folderIds` from

post.description:
Opens a chunked upload session for a file in the folder and returns it in a success envelope. This call is
deprecated. Use `POST api/2.0/files/{folderId}/session`, which returns the same session without the envelope.
No content is stored yet. Send the parts to `POST api/2.0/files/{folderId}/session/{sessionId}/upload`. Each
part is at most `chunkUploadSize` from `GET api/2.0/files/settings`. Then store the file with
`PUT api/2.0/files/{folderId}/session/{sessionId}/finalize`. Requires the right to create content in the
folder. Other callers get 403. In a room, its owner, room managers, and content creators have it. A guest has
it there only as a content creator. In My documents, the owner and anyone with read and write access to the
folder have it. A section root, an archived room, and an AI agent or AI project root also return 403. The call
changes data. A repeated call opens another session. It creates the folders of `relativePath` that do not exist
yet. If the folder has a file with this name, `createNewIfExist` true stores a copy with a numeric suffix. With
false, the upload adds a new version to that file if the caller can edit it. A guest never adds a version this
way. A session expires 12 hours after it opens or gets its last part. A missing folder returns 404. The call
returns 400 for a negative `fileSize`. In a private room, it also returns 400 if the name is not a lowercase
UUID with an optional extension. The call returns 402 if `fileSize` is over the limit for chunked uploads or
for a knowledge folder. It returns 403 if a private room gets a file without `encrypted`, or a knowledge folder
gets an unsupported format. It also returns 403 for a `relativePath` into a knowledge folder or an
instructions room. If the installation does not allow uploads with this extension, the call returns 415.

post.description:
Uploads the next part of a file to a chunked upload session. Send the part as the multipart `File` field. The
call adds parts in the order they arrive. Do not send two parts to one session at the same time. Any signed-in
user with the session ID can call it. The call finds the session by its ID and ignores the folder in the path.
The call changes data. Do not repeat a part. The session stores a repeated part as the next part. Then the file
has that part twice, or the session never stores the file. While bytes are missing, the response has `uploaded`
false. When the parts reach the size of the session, the call stores the file. It then returns 201, `uploaded`
true, and the file in `file`. A session below `chunkUploadSize` from `GET api/2.0/files/settings` stores the
file on the first call. It needs no `PUT api/2.0/files/{folderId}/session/{sessionId}/finalize`. After the call
that stores the file, a repeated call returns 404. The call returns 400 if the request has no `File` part. It
returns 402 if the part is over `chunkUploadSize`, or the file is over a quota or size limit. If the session
does not exist, is finalized, or has expired, the call returns 404. If the file is not a PDF and the room is a
form-filling room, the call returns 403.

Raises the `file.uploaded` webhook on the request that completes the upload, without `file.created`.

post.description:
Uploads one part of a file to a chunked upload session under the number in `chunkNumber`. The session keeps
parts by number. So you can resend a failed part with the same number. Without `chunkNumber`, the call numbers
parts in the order they arrive. Split the file into parts of at most `chunkUploadSize` from
`GET api/2.0/files/settings`. Any signed-in user with the session ID can call it. The call ignores the folder
in the path. It changes data. With `chunkNumber`, a repeated part replaces the part with that number. Without
it, the session stores a repeated part as the next part. Then the file has that part twice, or the session
never stores the file. The call returns the session, not the file. After the last part, store the file with
`PUT api/2.0/files/{folderId}/session/{sessionId}/finalize`. A session below `chunkUploadSize` stores the file
on this call but still needs that call. In such a session, each repeated call stores the file again and adds a
version. A session from `POST api/2.0/files/file/{fileId}/edit_session` keeps the version instead. To store the
file with the last part, use `POST api/2.0/files/{folderId}/session/{sessionId}`. The call returns 400 if the
request has no `File` part, or `chunkNumber` is below 1. It returns 402 if the part is over `chunkUploadSize`,
or the file is over a quota or size limit. If the session does not exist, is finalized, or has expired, the
call returns 404. If the file is not a PDF and the room is a form-filling room, the call returns 403.

put.description:
Sets one custom storage limit, in bytes, on each listed room. It returns the updated rooms in the order of
`roomIds`. Requires the room manager role in each room. Other callers get 403. The call changes data, and you
can repeat it with the same body. A room that already has this limit stays the same and is still returned.
The call skips unknown rooms and rooms in third-party storage. The call is not atomic. If a room fails, the
rooms before it keep the new limit. So check each room after a failed call. The call returns 403 if the room
quota feature is turned off, or `quota` exceeds the portal storage limit. For AI agents, it checks the agent
quota feature instead. It also returns 403 for a room in Trash or in the archive. To restore the portal
default, use `PUT api/2.0/files/rooms/resetquota`. To remove the custom limit, send a `quota` of `-1` to
`PUT api/2.0/files/rooms/{id}`.

Raises the `room.updated` webhook for every listed room, even when its quota does not change. Raises the `agent.updated` webhook instead for a listed AI agent. Raises the `folder.updated` webhook instead for a listed ID that is a folder, not a room.

`http://` to an address without a scheme. Requires the EditPortalSettings permission, which the portal owner
and DocSpace admins have. Other callers get 403. The call changes data, and you can repeat it with the same
body. The check calls the editor api script, the healthcheck, the converter, the command service, and the
document builder. If one fails, the portal restores all previous settings. Then the call fails. On success,
it returns what `GET api/2.0/files/docservice` returns without `version`. The call returns 400 if an address
cannot be parsed or is an absolute address with a query string. It also returns 400 for a secret without a
header. It also returns 400 for an `http` public address on a portal served over `https`.

`providerId`. It returns the root folder of the account. Third-party storage must be turned on with

or `providerKey` is missing, or `providerKey` names no known service. For a new account, it also returns 400 if a

`providerId`, the call returns 404. To create a room on the account, use

access alone. A value outside the published list is rejected as an invalid request.

Changes the owner of the listed rooms and files to one account. Requires the owner of each listed entry, or a
DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. The call changes data, one entry at a time. It stops at the first entry
it may not change, and earlier entries stay changed. An entry that the account already owns stays unchanged,
so you can repeat the call. The previous owner stays in a transferred room as its room manager. A transferred
file gets a new version by the new owner. The call skips third-party files. The call returns 403 if the
new owner is not an active DocSpace admin or room admin. It also returns 403 for a private room if the new
owner has no encryption keys. It also returns 403 for a folder that is not a room, or a file outside the
common section. A file that is locked or being edited also returns 403. If the new owner lacks keys to some
encrypted files of a private room, the call returns 409. To find these files, use
`GET api/2.0/privacyroom/{roomId}/access/missing`. After their keys are added, repeat the call. Without
`userId`, the call returns 400. It also returns 400 if a string file id points to a storage account that is
not connected.

`GET api/2.0/files/share/{key}`. Call it after that operation reports that the link requires a password.
Anyone can call it without signing in. A signed-in caller who can read the room does not need the password.
The call changes data but not the entry. The portal remembers a correct password for the caller, so later
requests with the token skip it. The portal counts only wrong passwords for each link and calling address. So
you can repeat the call with the correct password. A wrong password gives an invalid-password `status`, not an
HTTP error. The portal then forgets the remembered password. After too many attempts, the call returns 403 until
the block expires, even with the correct password.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description:
The token of the external share link, taken verbatim from the `requestToken` of a link returned by the link
operations of an entry, such as `GET api/2.0/files/rooms/{id}/link`. It is an opaque URL-safe string that
carries the link's own identifier, so it cannot be assembled by hand.

requestBody.description: The body of the request, holding the password to check.

schema.description: The body of the request, holding the password to check.

200.description: The entry the token points at, with the status the link reached after the password was checked

403.description: Too many attempts were made for this link from the calling address, and the block has not expired yet

400.description: Bad Request.

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

get.description:
Returns the third-party storage services that the portal can connect, in a short form. Each element is an array.
Its first item is the value to send as `providerKey` to `POST api/2.0/files/thirdparty`. The OAuth services are
`Box`, `DropboxV2`, `GoogleDrive`, and `OneDrive`. Their second and third items are the OAuth client ID and redirect
URL. With them, you can build the address of the consent screen. A service that uses a login and password
(`SharePoint`, `WebDav`, `kDrive`, or `Yandex`) has a one-item array. The list has only the services turned on in
the portal configuration. It also skips an OAuth service whose app is not set up. Any signed-in user can call it.
A guest gets an empty array instead of an error. The call is read-only. The array is also empty while third-party storage is
turned off for the portal. To turn it on, use `PUT api/2.0/files/thirdparty`. For display names, WebDAV presets,
and the flags of a connection form, use `GET api/2.0/files/thirdparty/providers`.

200.description: The provider keys, each with the OAuth client ID and redirect URL where the service uses OAuth

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

delete.description:
Disconnects a third-party storage account from the portal and returns the ID of its folder. The ID has the
`provider-accountId` form of third-party entries, not the numeric `providerId`. Requires the right to delete the
account folder, which the user who connected the account has. Other callers get 403. The call changes data and
cannot be undone. It deletes nothing at the storage service, and the files stay there. The portal deletes its
link to them, the stored credentials, and the sharing records and tags of its entries. If the account is the
backup storage of `POST api/2.0/files/thirdparty/backup`, the call also deletes the backup schedule. If a room
stands on the account, the call returns 403. To disconnect such an account, delete the room. If no account has
this `providerId`, the call returns 404. So a repeated call also returns 404.

parameters.name: providerId
parameters.description: The ID of the connected third-party storage account, as `providerId` of `GET api/2.0/files/thirdparty`.

200.description: The ID of the folder that stood for the removed account

403.description: The caller neither connected the account nor has the right to delete the folder it stands for

404.description: No third-party account with this ID exists on the portal

400.description: Bad Request.

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

get.description:
Returns the third-party storage accounts of the legacy Common section, as folder entries. Each entry stands for
one account, and the folder operations can browse it. Any signed-in user can call it. The call skips accounts
whose folder the caller cannot read, so the list differs between users. The call is read-only. It returns a
plain array without paging. In most portals the array is empty, and that is not an error. The reason is that
`POST api/2.0/files/thirdparty` attaches accounts to the Rooms section, not to Common. So only accounts from an
older portal appear here. The array is also empty if third-party storage is turned off or no storage service is
set up. For the caller's own accounts in any section, use `GET api/2.0/files/thirdparty`.

200.description: The third-party accounts attached to the Common section, as folder entries

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

get.description:
Returns the root folder of the third-party storage account where the portal saves scheduled and manual backups.
A portal has at most one such account. A DocSpace admin connects it with `POST api/2.0/files/thirdparty/backup`.
Any signed-in user can call it. The call is read-only. The body is `null` with status 200 if no backup account is
connected or the caller cannot read its folder. The answer does not tell these cases apart. The folder operations
accept the returned `id`. The `title` is the title of the account. The list of `GET api/2.0/files/thirdparty`
does not have this account. To remove it, use `DELETE api/2.0/files/thirdparty/{providerId}`.

200.description: The root folder of the backup storage account, or null when none is connected

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

post.description:
Connects the third-party storage account where the portal saves backups, and returns its root folder. Third-party
storage must be turned on with `PUT api/2.0/files/thirdparty`. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403.
The call changes data. A portal has one backup account. A second call re-authenticates and renames that account
instead of adding one. So you can repeat the call with the same body if it has no `token`. A `token` is a
one-time code of Google Drive, Box, Dropbox, or OneDrive. So the service rejects a repeat with the same `token`.
The credentials follow the rules of `POST api/2.0/files/thirdparty`. The call checks them at the service before
it saves anything. So wrong credentials leave the current account unchanged. The call returns 400 if
`providerKey` names no known service or a needed `url` is missing. While no backup account exists, a missing
`token` or `password` also returns 400. The call returns 403 if third-party storage is turned off or the service
rejects the credentials. While no backup account exists, a title that is empty after the call removes invalid
characters also returns 403. The list of `GET api/2.0/files/thirdparty` does not have this account. To read it,
use `GET api/2.0/files/thirdparty/backup`. To remove it, use `DELETE api/2.0/files/thirdparty/{providerId}`.

schema.description: The credentials and the title of the third-party storage account the portal writes its backups to.

200.description: The root folder of the backup storage account

400.description: The request body cannot be read, `providerKey` names no known storage service, `url` is missing or is not an HTTP address for a service that needs it, or, while no backup account is connected yet, the `token` or `password` the service needs is missing

403.description: The caller is not a DocSpace administrator, the portal-wide third-party switch is off or no storage service is enabled, the service rejects the credentials, or, while no backup account is connected yet, the title is empty once invalid characters are removed

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

get.description:
Returns the third-party storage services that the portal configuration lists, with the data of a connection form.
With `excludewebdav=true`, the list has only the OAuth services. Any signed-in user can call it. A guest gets an
empty array instead of an error. The call is read-only. The array is also empty while third-party storage is turned off for
the portal. To turn it on, use `PUT api/2.0/files/thirdparty`. The list also has OAuth services whose app is not
set up, with `connected` false. To list the accounts of the caller, use `GET api/2.0/files/thirdparty`.

parameters.name: excludewebdav
parameters.description:
Set to true to leave out the whole WebDAV family, the kDrive and Yandex presets included, and keep only the
services that authenticate through OAuth 2.0; false lists all of them.

200.description: The storage services this portal can connect

400.description: Bad Request.

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

post.description:
Starts a job that creates a room template from a room, and returns the job state. The portal saves the template
in the Templates section. The template takes the type, indexing, storage limit, lifetime, download, and
watermark settings of the room. The job copies the files and ordinary subfolders of the room, but not its
service subfolders. Requires room manager access to the source room. Other callers get 403, even a DocSpace
admin. The call queues work. Poll `GET api/2.0/files/roomtemplate/status` until `isCompleted` is true, then read
`templateId`. While a job of the caller runs, a repeated call starts nothing and returns its state. After the
job ends, a repeated call creates another template. If `public` is true, the call ignores `share` and `groups`
and shares the template with everyone. If `copyLogo` is true, the call ignores `logo`. If `roomId` is not a
room of the Rooms section, the call returns 404. The call returns 403 if the room is archived or private. It
also returns 403 if `quota` is set while room quotas are turned off. The call returns 400 if `roomId` is
missing, `title` is empty, or a value breaks its limits.

Raises the `room.created` webhook for the new template, once the queued operation builds it. Raises the `room.updated` webhook after it when `quota` is given. Raises the `agent.created` webhook instead for an AI agent template. Raises the `agent.updated` webhook instead for an AI agent template with `quota`.

schema.description: The parameters of a room template built from an existing room.

200.description: The state of the template creation just queued: `isCompleted` is still false, so the job has to be polled for its result

400.description: The request body cannot be read or has no `roomId`, `title` is empty or longer than 400 characters, `color` is longer than 6 or `cover` longer than 50 characters, or `logo` has no `tmpFile` or a position or size outside 0-1280

403.description: The source room is archived or private, the caller cannot edit it, or `quota` is set while the storage quota for rooms (for an AI agent, for agents) is turned off

404.description: No room with `roomId` exists in the Rooms section

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

get.description:
Returns the state of the room template job that the caller started with `POST api/2.0/files/roomtemplate`. Any
signed-in user can call it. The call is read-only and reports only the jobs of the caller. If the caller has
started none, the call returns no status object. This is the call to poll. Repeat it until `isCompleted` is
true, then read `templateId`. Use `isCompleted`, not `progress`, as the end signal. After the job ends, the call
returns the same state until the caller starts another job.

200.description: The state of the caller's latest template creation, or an empty body when this account has started none

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

get.description:
Returns whether a room template is shared with everyone. If `true`, the Everyone group has read access. Then any
user who can create rooms can use the template with `POST api/2.0/files/rooms/fromtemplate`. If `false`, only
the owner of the template and the users it is shared with can use it. Requires read access to the template.
Other callers get 403, even a DocSpace admin. The user types user and guest always get 403. The call is
read-only. It returns 404 if `id` is an ordinary room, a deleted template, or unknown. If `id` is less than 1,
the call returns 400. To change the setting, use `PUT api/2.0/files/roomtemplate/public`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The identifier of the room template. Take it from `templateId` of `GET api/2.0/files/roomtemplate/status`, or
from the folder list of `GET api/2.0/files/rooms` called with `searchArea` set to 4; an identifier of an
ordinary room is not accepted.

200.description: True when the template is shared with everyone, false when only its owner and the accounts it was shared with can reach it

400.description: A parameter has the wrong type, or `id` is less than 1

403.description: The caller has no read access to the template

404.description: `id` does not identify a room template

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

put.description:
Changes whether a room template is shared with everyone. If `public` is true, the Everyone group gets read
access. Then any user who can create rooms can use the template with `POST api/2.0/files/rooms/fromtemplate`.
If `public` is false, the Everyone group loses access. In both cases, the call removes access for all other
users and groups of the template. This includes the users from `share` at creation. So you cannot add one
recipient with this call. Only the owner of the template can call it. Other callers get 403, even the portal
owner. The call changes data and returns nothing. You can repeat it with the same body. The call returns 404 if
`id` is an ordinary room or unknown. It returns 400 if the body has no `id` or `id` is less than 1. To read the
setting, use `GET api/2.0/files/roomtemplate/{id}/public`.

schema.description: The public access to set on a room template.

200.description: The recipient list of the template has been rewritten to match the requested access; nothing is returned

400.description: The request body cannot be read or has no `id`, or `id` is less than 1

403.description: The caller is not allowed to change who the template is shared with

404.description: `id` does not identify a room template

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

post.description:
Creates a room in the Rooms section and returns it. The call creates an Instructions room, a Knowledge room,
or an AI project in the AI rooms section instead. You cannot change `roomType` after this call. Requires a DocSpace admin
or a room admin. Other callers get 403. The call changes data. Do not repeat it. Each call creates another room.
A repeat with the same `logo` returns 404 but still creates a room. That room has no logo, tags, or primary
external link. The call adds the tag names that the portal does not have yet. A public room and a form filling
room get a primary external link. To invite members, use `PUT api/2.0/files/rooms/{id}/share` after this call.
The call returns 400 if `title` is blank, `cover` is unknown, or `share` is not empty. It also returns 400 if
`private` is set together with `indexing`, a lifetime, or a watermark. A room of the AI rooms section also
returns 400 with settings that do not apply to its type. The call returns 402 if the portal reached the room
limit of its plan or its payment is overdue. Rooms of the AI rooms section do not count toward this limit. A
logo that does not fit into the storage quota also returns 402. The call returns 403 if `quota` is set while
room quotas are turned off, or is over the portal limit. It also returns 403 for a public room while the portal
forbids external sharing. A private room also returns 403 if the caller has no encryption keys. A Knowledge room
returns 403 while vectorization is turned off. If `logo.tmpFile` names no uploaded picture, or one already used,
the call returns 404.

Raises the `room.created` webhook when `roomType` is not `AiRoom`. Raises the `agent.created` webhook instead when `roomType` is `AiRoom`, which creates an AI agent in the Rooms section.

schema.description: The parameters of a new room in the Rooms section.

200.description: The created room with its id, type, settings, logo and tags

400.description: The request body cannot be read or has no `title` or `roomType`, `private` is set together with `indexing`, an enabled `lifetime` or an enabled `watermark`, `title` is blank or longer than 170 characters, `roomType` is not a known room type, `color` is not six hexadecimal digits, `cover` is longer than 50 characters or not a known cover, `share` is not empty, `lifetime` has an unknown `period` or a `value` outside 1-999, the `watermark` text is longer than 255 characters, `logo` has no `tmpFile`, a position outside 0-1280, a size outside 1-1280 or a position outside the uploaded picture, or a tag name is empty

402.description: The portal has reached the room limit of its pricing plan or its payment is overdue, or the logo does not fit into the portal storage quota

403.description: The caller is a user or a guest, `roomType` is a public room while the portal forbids external sharing, `private` is set while the caller has no encryption keys or the connected document server cannot work with encrypted files, `quota` is set while the storage quota for rooms is turned off or exceeds the portal storage limit, or `logo.tmpFile` is not a picture the caller uploaded

404.description: `logo.tmpFile` names no uploaded picture, or one already used

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

instead when `roomType` is `AiRoom`, which creates an AI agent in the Rooms section

get.description:
Returns one page of the rooms of a portal section. The `searchArea` parameter picks the section, by default the
active rooms. The other parameters filter the rooms by type, title, tags, member, owner, storage, quota, privacy,
and metadata. A room must match all filters. Any signed-in user can call it. If the caller cannot read the
section, the call returns 403. A caller sees only the rooms they created or were invited to. A DocSpace admin
sees all rooms. So an empty list means that the caller sees no matching room. The call is read-only, except
that it stores a `sortBy` value as the default sort order of the account. Without `sortBy`, the call uses the
stored order. The rooms come in `folders`, and `files` stays empty. The `current` field describes the section,
and `total` counts all matching rooms before paging. To read one room, use `GET api/2.0/files/rooms/{id}`. The
call returns 400 if `tags` is not a JSON array, `sortBy` is unknown, or the metadata filter is invalid.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description:
Keeps only the rooms of the listed kinds. Repeat the parameter to pass more than one value; they are combined
with OR, and omitting it returns the rooms of every kind.

items.description: The room type.

parameters.name: subjectId
parameters.description:
Keeps only the rooms this account or group has access to, which is how the rooms of one member are listed. The
identifier comes from the portal people and group listings, and the exclude flag turns the filter into its
opposite.

parameters.name: subjectOwnerId
parameters.description:
Keeps only the rooms created by this account, regardless of who else was invited to them. The identifier comes
from the portal people listing, and the exclude flag turns the filter into its opposite.

parameters.name: searchArea
parameters.description:
The section to list. Every section is a separate root and a room belongs to exactly one of them at a time, so
archiving a room moves it out of the active section. The default is the active section, which leaves the
form-filling rooms to their own value.

parameters.name: withoutTags
parameters.description:
When true, keeps only the rooms that carry no tag at all, which is the complement of the tag filter. When
false or omitted, tags play no part in the selection.

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description:
A JSON array of tag names serialized into a single query value, for example ["Important","Legal"]. A room
matches when it carries any one of them. Take the names from `GET api/2.0/files/tags`; a name that is not in
the catalog simply matches nothing.

parameters.name: excludeSubject
parameters.description:
Inverts the two subject filters: when true, the rooms of the named account are the ones left out of the answer
instead of the only ones kept. It does nothing on its own.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description:
Keeps only the rooms whose content lives in the named third-party service, for portals where rooms may be
connected to external storage. The default keeps rooms of every origin.

parameters.name: quotaFilter
parameters.description:
Splits the rooms by whether a storage quota was set on the room itself or it follows the portal default, which
is how rooms with a custom limit are found.

parameters.name: storageFilter
parameters.description:
Splits the rooms by where their content is stored, in the portal itself or in a connected third-party account.
It is the coarse form of the provider filter.

parameters.name: privacyFilter
parameters.description:
Splits the rooms by whether they are private, that is encrypted rooms whose content the portal cannot read.
Omitting it returns both kinds, except in the active rooms, which leave private rooms out.

parameters.name: withAiFolder
parameters.description:
Keeps only the rooms that provide skills to the AI chat: Instructions rooms, whose Markdown files are read
with `GET api/2.0/files/rooms/{id}/ai`. Omitting it returns rooms of every type.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description:
How many rooms one page may carry. Ask for the next page by raising the start index by the number of rooms
already received.

parameters.name: startIndex
parameters.description:
How many matching rooms to skip before the page begins. Page through the answer until the skip plus the rooms
received reaches the total it reports.

parameters.name: sortBy
parameters.description:
The field to order the rooms by, named as in the file listings: `AZ` for the title, `DateAndTime` for the last
change, `DateAndTimeCreation`, `Author`, `Size`, `Type`, `RoomType`, `Tags`, `UsedSpace`, `LastOpened`. The
name is matched ignoring case, an unknown one is rejected rather than ignored, and the accepted one also
becomes this account's stored order.

parameters.name: sortOrder
parameters.description:
The direction of the order chosen by the sort field. It has no effect when no sort field is given and the
stored order of the account is used.

parameters.name: filterValue
parameters.description:
Keeps only the rooms whose title contains this text, ignoring case. It is a substring match over the title
alone: room content and tags are not searched.

parameters.name: groupId
parameters.description:
Keeps only the rooms that belong to this room group. The identifier comes from `GET api/2.0/files/group`; the
groups of portal members are a different concept and their identifiers do not match here.

parameters.name: metadataTemplateId
parameters.description:
The ID of the metadata template the entries must be assigned to. On its own it narrows the listing to the entries
carrying the template; together with the metadata filters it also pins the template the filtered fields belong to.

parameters.name: metadataFilters
parameters.description:
The URL-encoded JSON array of the metadata filter conditions,
e.g. [{"fieldId":1,"op":"contains","value":"ACME"},{"fieldId":2,"op":"range","from":"2026-01-01","to":"2026-06-30"},{"fieldId":3,"op":"in","optionIds":["..."]}].
A string field takes "eq" (the whole value) or "contains" (a part of it); a number or a date field takes "range" with inclusive bounds,
or "gt", "gte", "lt", "lte" with the single bound in "value"; a choice field takes "in". A date-only bound covers the whole day,
so "to":"2026-06-30" includes the values stored on 30 June and "gt":"2026-06-30" starts after it.
A custom field is addressed by its name instead of the fieldId: {"name":"Client","op":"eq","value":"ACME"}.
The same filter is taken as a typed request body by POST api/2.0/files/rooms/search.

parameters.name: includeHiddenMetadata
parameters.description:
Whether the text search, and the "metadataMatches" it reports, also look at the values of the hidden metadata
templates (created with "visible" false for the metadata a service keeps for itself, which the web client never
shows). False, the default, leaves them out, so an entry is not found by such a value; true takes them in.
"metadataTemplateId" and "metadataFilters" are not concerned: a hidden template or field named there is searched
either way.

200.description: The rooms of the selected section with the paging counters

400.description: A parameter has the wrong type, the `count` is outside its allowed range, the `startIndex` is negative, or `tags` is not a JSON array of strings

403.description: The caller cannot read the selected section

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

get.summary: Get the skills folder of an Instructions room
get.description:
Returns one page of the root folder of an Instructions room. Its Markdown files are the skills of the AI chat.
The response has the same shape as `GET api/2.0/files/{folderId}`. Requires read access to the room. Other
callers get 403. The call is read-only. To find Instructions rooms, use the `withAiFolder` filter of
`GET api/2.0/files/rooms`. The call returns 404 if the room does not exist or is not an Instructions room. It
returns 400 if `count` is out of range or `startIndex` is negative.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The Instructions room whose skills are listed, named by the identifier that `GET api/2.0/files/rooms` reports
for it.

parameters.name: filterType
parameters.description:
Narrows the listing to a single kind of entry, such as documents, spreadsheets or images. Omit it to list every
kind the folder holds.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description:
The size of one page of the listing. Pair it with `startIndex` to walk through the result, and compare the two
with `total` in the response to see when the last page has been read.

parameters.name: startIndex
parameters.description:
The number of matching entries to skip before the returned page begins; add `count` to it to ask for the next
page.

parameters.name: sortBy
parameters.description:
The name of the field the entries are ordered by, matched case-insensitively against the file sort fields,
such as `DateAndTime`, `AZ`, `Size` or `Type`.

parameters.name: sortOrder
parameters.description: The direction in which the `sortBy` field is ordered.

parameters.name: filterValue
parameters.description:
The search string the listing is filtered by: it is matched as a substring of entry titles. Omit it to list
the folder unfiltered.

200.description: One page of the Instructions room root, with the room itself and the chain of its parents

400.description: A parameter has the wrong type, the `count` is outside its allowed range, or the `startIndex` is negative

403.description: The caller may not read this room

404.description: The room does not exist or is not an Instructions room

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

post.summary: Create a room from the template
post.description:
Starts a job that creates a room in the Rooms section from a room template. Requires read access to the
template and the right to create rooms. Other callers get 403. A user or a guest cannot create rooms. The call
queues work and returns the progress record of the job. The room does not exist yet when the response arrives.
Repeat `GET api/2.0/files/rooms/fromtemplate/status` until `isCompleted` is true. Then take `roomId` from it. A
non-empty `error` means that the job failed. The job fails if the template is a public room while the portal
forbids external sharing. The portal keeps one job record per account. Starting a new job deletes the record of
a finished one. Wait for the running job to end before you start the next one. Settings that the body leaves
out come from the template. With `copyLogo`, the call ignores `logo`. The call returns 400 if `title` is blank.
It returns 403 if `quota` is set while the quota for this kind of room is turned off. If no room template has
the `templateId`, the call returns 404.

Raises the `room.created` webhook once the queued operation builds the room. Raises the `room.updated` webhook after it when `quota` is given. Raises the `agent.created` webhook instead for a room built from an AI agent template. Raises the `agent.updated` webhook instead for such a room with `quota`.

Starts a job that exports the data of all original forms of a form filling room to the external
database. Requires editing access to a form filling room. Other callers get 403. Any other room also
returns 403. The call queues work and returns the job record. Repeat
`GET api/2.0/files/rooms/{id}/externaldbsync` until `isCompleted` is true. Then read `forms` for the result of each form. A form that fails does not stop

exports only the form data that the database does not have yet. The room keeps one job record. If no external
database is configured, the call returns 400 and queues nothing. If the room does not exist, the call returns

empty body changes nothing. Requires the room manager role in the room. Other callers get 403. A DocSpace
admin without an invitation also gets 403. The call changes data, and you can repeat it with the same body.

404. After each call with `lifetime`, the portal waits 6 hours by default before it deletes expired files. The
call trims a `title` and cleans it as at room creation. A blank `title` changes nothing. The `tags` array
replaces all tags of the room, and an empty array removes them. An empty `color` restores the default color. An
empty `cover` removes the cover. A `quota` of `-1` removes the custom limit. Any other negative `quota` restores
the portal default. A positive `quota` works only while the room quota feature is turned on. If you turn on
`indexing`, the call renumbers the room contents. The call returns 400 if the body has a property that the room
update does not define. It also returns 400 for `chatSettings` in a room that is not an AI room. A private room
with `indexing`, `lifetime`, or `watermark` also returns 400. If a new logo or watermark image does not fit the
portal storage quota, the call returns 402. It returns 403 for a room in Trash or in the archive, or a `quota`
over the portal limit. It also returns 403 if `logo.tmpFile` is not an image the caller uploaded. If the room or
the uploaded image does not exist, the call returns 404. To crop and set only a logo, use
`POST api/2.0/files/rooms/{id}/logo`.

Starts a background job that deletes a room with all its contents, and returns the job record. The job does
not move the room to Trash, so the deletion cannot be undone. An archived room is deleted the same way. Requires the right
to delete the room. Other callers get 403. The call checks the right before it queues the job. The job checks
it again, so read the `error` of the finished job. Repeat `GET api/2.0/files/fileops` until `finished` is

job ends. The job ignores `deleteAfter` in the body. If the room does not exist, the call returns 404. A repeat
after the job ends also returns 404. A repeat while the job runs queues a second job. If a string `id` points to
a storage account that is not connected, the call returns 400.

put.description:
Changes the members of a room in one call, and returns the access of the listed subjects. The call can add,
change, and remove members. Each entry names an account, a group, or the email of a person without an account.
An `access` of `None` removes the subject from the room. Requires the room manager role in the room. Other
callers get 403. The call changes data, and you can repeat it with the same body. It skips a subject that
already has the listed access, so a repeat sends no email. If `notify` is true, the portal emails the invitation
with `message`. A person who got the same invitation or access email for this room recently gets no new one. A
new `message` does not change this. The call ignores an entry without an access level. If a subject is listed
twice, the last level wins. An empty list changes nothing. The call skips subjects that the caller cannot see,
except current members that the room owner changes. So compare the answer with the request. Without `force`, the
call does not remove a member who has a form role. It reports this in `error` instead. The answer can also carry
a `warning`. The call returns 400 for an invalid or too long `email`, too many email invitations, or an invalid
`culture`. It returns 403 if an entry has an email and the portal forbids guest invitations. It also returns 403
if a subject cannot get the access, such as a user or guest as room manager. In a private room, a subject
without encryption keys also returns 403. If the room does not exist, the call returns 404.

get.description:
Returns one page of the members of a room with their access. The list starts with the owner, then room
managers, groups, other members, guests, and pending invitations. Use `filterType` to select what the call
lists. By default, it lists accounts and groups, without links. To read the links, use

matches by its email. Requires read access to the room. Other callers get 403. A DocSpace admin can read the

stays the same between calls. The response headers carry the total. To list links here, the caller needs the
right to see the links. Without it, the call returns an empty page. A `count` out of range returns 400. If the

put.summary: Set the room external or invitation link
put.description:
Sets one link of a room and returns it. The call creates, changes, or deletes the link. The `linkType` field
selects the type. An invitation link makes each person who opens it a member with `access`. An external link
opens the room without an account. Without `linkId`, the call creates a link. With the ID of a link, it
changes that link. An unknown ID creates a link with this ID. A change replaces all settings, so send every
field to keep. A change keeps the link type. An `access` of `None` deletes the link. Deleting the primary
external link of a public or form-filling room creates and returns a new one. After any other deletion, the
body is empty. Requires the right to manage the links of the room. Other callers get 403. The call changes
data. You can repeat a call with `linkId`, but each call without it creates another link. The `password`,
`denyDownload`, and `internal` fields apply only to external links, and `maxUseCount` only to invitation
links. Without `linkId`, an `internal` of false gives the portal default. In a public room, external links
are never internal. There, a change with `internal` true saves nothing. The call reads a past
`expirationDate` of an external link as none. It ignores the date for the primary link of a public or
form-filling room. For an invitation link, a past date returns 400. Only custom, public, and form-filling
rooms take external links, and a form-filling room only its primary one. A room has at most one invitation
link, and a second one returns 403. While an admin restricts external links, the call makes each external link
it sets internal. Then, setting an external link in a public room or deleting its primary link returns 403. Deleting the
primary link of a form-filling room also returns 403 if that link is not internal. The call also returns 403
for a private room, a room template, or too many links. It also returns 403 for a link type or access level
the room does not take. The call returns 400 for a too long title or password, a weak password, or an invalid
`maxUseCount` or `expirationDate`. If the room does not exist, the call returns 404.

get.description:
Returns the primary external link of a room, the address for people outside the portal. Public and form-filling
rooms get this link when they are created. If the room has no primary link yet, the call creates one. Requires
read access to the room. Other callers get 403. To create the link, the caller also needs the right to manage
the links of the room. Without it, the call returns 403. The call is read-only, except when it creates the link.
A repeated call returns the same link. An archived public room still returns its link to room managers. Other
members get 403. The entry is the same as in `GET api/2.0/files/rooms/{id}/links`, with the primary flag set. It
includes the request token that must go with the address. The call also returns 403 if the room type takes no
external links. An admin rule that allows external links only in public rooms also returns 403. If the link was
revoked, the call returns 404 and creates no new link. If the room does not exist, the call also returns 404. If
a string `id` points to a storage account that is not connected, the call returns 400.

the section, by default the active rooms, and `type` limits the room types. The `searchArea` field can also
pick the private rooms section. The active rooms do not include private rooms. With only `metadataTemplateId`,
the call keeps the rooms that have this template. A room must match every condition of `metadataFilters`. The

without them lists the whole section. Take the template and field IDs from

the call returns 403. A caller sees only the rooms they created or were invited to. A DocSpace admin sees all
rooms. So an empty list means that the caller sees no matching room. The call is read-only, except that it
stores a `sortBy` value as the default sort order of the account. Without `sortBy`, the call uses the stored
order. You can repeat it with the same body. The rooms come in `folders`, and `files` stays empty. The `total`
field counts all matching rooms before paging. To filter by tags, member, owner, storage, quota, or privacy,
use `GET api/2.0/files/rooms`. The call returns 400 for an unknown template or field, a field outside the
template, or more than 20 conditions. It also returns 400 for an unknown `sortBy`.

delete.description:
Deletes custom room tags from the portal catalog and removes them from every room. The rooms and their content
stay. Requires a DocSpace admin. Other callers get 403. A room admin can create tags but also gets 403 here. The
call cannot be undone. Creating the name again with `POST api/2.0/files/tags` restores the tag but not its
rooms. The call matches names, ignoring case on MySQL, and skips names that are not in the catalog. An empty
list changes nothing. So a success does not prove that a tag was deleted, and you can repeat the call. To check
a tag first, use `GET api/2.0/files/tags/{tagName}/haslinks`. The response has no body. To remove a tag from one
room only, use `DELETE api/2.0/files/rooms/{id}/tags`. The call returns 400 if `names` is missing, or a name is
empty, has only spaces, or is too long.

post.description:
Starts a background job that exports the index of a room to a spreadsheet, and returns the job. The room must
have indexing turned on. Requires a DocSpace admin or the room role room manager in this room. Other callers
get 403. It also returns 403 if the folder is not a room, the room is archived, or indexing is turned off. The
call queues work. Each account has one export job. If an earlier job still runs, the call returns that job and
starts nothing. So a repeated call during the export changes nothing. After the job ends, a new call replaces it
with a new job, which saves another spreadsheet. Repeat `GET api/2.0/files/rooms/indexexport` until
`isCompleted` is true. Then read `status` to tell success from failure or cancellation. The portal saves the
spreadsheet in the My documents section of the caller, not in the room. The `resultFileId` and `resultFileUrl`
fields of the job point to it. To cancel the job, use `DELETE api/2.0/files/rooms/indexexport`. If the room does
not exist or is a room template, the call returns 404.

for a failed or cancelled job. So read `status` for the result and `error` for the message. The `percentage`
field changes in large steps and does not show the remaining time. After a successful export, `resultFileId`,
`resultFileName`, and `resultFileUrl` point to the spreadsheet in the My documents section of the caller. If the

`PrivateRooms`. It also returns 400 for a malformed room identifier or a disconnected storage account. An empty
`rooms` list returns 403. If no listed room can be added, the call creates no group. It returns 403 if a listed
identifier exists but is not a room the caller can read. If all existing rooms are readable but in the other
section, it returns 400. If no listed room exists, it returns 404. A string identifier that names no third-party
storage also returns 404. If only some rooms can be added, the call creates the group with them but returns 403.

Creates an encryption key pair for the calling user. A user needs at least one key before anyone can invite
them to a private room. Any signed-in user can call it, except a guest. A guest gets 403. The call changes data,
and a repeated call with the same `id` returns 409. A body without `id` uses the all-zero `id`, so its repeat
also returns 409. It returns 201 with every key the caller now holds. Before DocSpace 4.0, it returned 200 with
the same body. To change an existing pair, use `PUT api/2.0/privacyroom/keys`. The call returns 400 if the body
is missing, `publicKey` or `privateKeyEnc` is blank, or a key is too long. A malformed `id` also returns 400.

under.

201.description: The encryption key is created. Answered 200 before DocSpace 4.0; the response body is unchanged

400.description: The key material is missing, blank or too large to be stored

403.description: The caller is a guest, who cannot own encryption keys

put.description:
Replaces the key material of one encryption key pair of the calling user. The call finds the pair by `id` and
leaves the other pairs unchanged. Without `id`, it replaces the pair with the all-zero `id`. The call replaces
both halves, so send the private half even when it does not change. Any signed-in user can call it, except a
guest. A guest gets 403. The call changes data, and you can repeat it with the same body. It returns every key
the caller holds after the change. After this call, `GET api/2.0/privacyroom/{roomId}/access` returns the new
public half. To create a pair, use `POST api/2.0/privacyroom/keys`. If the caller has no pair with this `id`,
the call returns 404. The call returns 400 if the body is missing, `publicKey` or `privateKeyEnc` is blank, or
a key is too long. A malformed `id` also returns 400. A 400 leaves the stored pair unchanged.

get.description:
Returns every encryption key pair of the calling user, including the encrypted private half. Any signed-in user
can call it. The call is read-only. If the caller has no key yet, the answer is an empty list or has no body. A
guest cannot create keys, so a guest gets this empty answer unless they had keys before. A user without a key
cannot be invited to a private room. To create a key, use `POST api/2.0/privacyroom/keys`. To get the keys of a
private room, use `GET api/2.0/privacyroom/{roomId}/access`. To get the keys of one file, use `GET
api/2.0/files/file/{fileId}/publickeys`.

200.description: The encryption keys of the current user

502.description: Bad Gateway. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

503.description: Service Unavailable. Returned by the reverse proxy, response body may be HTML and not JSON.

get.description:
Returns the encryption keys of all members of a private room, one entry per key. An app uses them to encrypt a
file key for every member. Requires membership in the room, with any access level, and a key of the caller's
own. Other callers get 403. A DocSpace admin who is not a member also gets 403. The call is read-only. Only the
caller's own entries include `privateKeyEnc`. The call skips entries without a public key. An archived private
room still returns its keys. To get the keys of one file, use `GET api/2.0/files/file/{fileId}/publickeys`. To
get the keys of users before you invite them, use `GET api/2.0/privacyroom/{roomId}/access/candidates`. If the
room is not private, the call returns 400. If the room is unknown or in Trash, the call returns 404.

parameters.description:
The private room whose access keys are read. Take it from the `id` of the room returned by
`POST api/2.0/files/rooms` or listed by `GET api/2.0/files/rooms`.
