get.summary: Get public keys of room invitees
get.description:
Returns the public encryption keys of users that you plan to invite to a private room. Use them to encrypt the
file keys of the room for these users before you invite them. Requires the right to change the access of the
room, which the room owner and room managers have. Other callers get 403. A DocSpace admin who is not a member
also gets 403. It also returns 403 for an archived room. The call is read-only and invites nobody. To invite
the users, use `PUT api/2.0/files/rooms/{id}/share`. The answer has one entry per key and never includes
`privateKeyEnc`, even for the caller. It has no entry for a user without a key, a guest, a disabled user, or an
unknown user. A user without a key must first create one with `POST api/2.0/privacyroom/keys`. The call counts
a repeated user ID once. Without `userIds`, it returns an empty list. To get the keys of current members, use
`GET api/2.0/privacyroom/{roomId}/access`. The call returns 400 if the room is not private or `roomId` is a
folder inside a room. A malformed user ID also returns 400. If the room is unknown, the call returns 404.

parameters.description:
The private room the people are invited to. Take it from the `id` of the room returned by
`POST api/2.0/files/rooms` or listed by `GET api/2.0/files/rooms`.

parameters.description:

get.summary: Get missing file keys of a room
get.description:
Returns the encrypted files of a private room that each user cannot open yet, in all folders of the room. An app
then writes only the missing keys with `PUT api/2.0/files/{fileId}/access`. With `userIds`, the call checks
these users, members or not. Without `userIds`, it checks the members of the room and the room owner. Before
you change the room owner with `POST api/2.0/files/owner`, check the new owner here. That call refuses a new
owner who misses a key. Requires the right to change the access of the room, which the room owner and room
managers have. Other callers get 403. A DocSpace admin who is not a member also gets 403. It also returns 403
for an archived room. The call is read-only. The answer has one entry per user who misses a key. An empty list
means that no key is missing. The call skips files stored without encryption and IDs of unknown users. The call
returns 400 if the room is not private or `roomId` is a folder inside a room.
A malformed user ID also returns 400. If the room is unknown, the call returns 404.

delete.description:
Deletes one encryption key pair of the calling user. The other pairs stay unchanged. Any signed-in user can call
it, except a guest. A guest gets 403. The deletion cannot be undone, and a repeated call returns 404. The call
returns 204 with no body. Before DocSpace 4.0, it returned 200 with the remaining keys. To read the remaining
keys, use `GET api/2.0/privacyroom/keys`. After the caller deletes the last key,
`GET api/2.0/privacyroom/{roomId}/access` returns 403 for all their private rooms. The rooms and their content
stay unchanged. To restore access, create a key with `POST api/2.0/privacyroom/keys`. If the caller has no
pair with this `id`, the call returns 404. A malformed `id` returns 400.

docServiceUrl.description:
The public address of the Document Server, the one a browser loads the editor from. An empty value drops the
portal's own setting, so the address configured for the deployment takes over again. A value with no scheme is
stored with `http://` prepended, and an absolute address may not carry a query string.

docServiceUrlInternal.description:
The address the portal itself uses for its server-to-server calls to the Document Server, for deployments
where that traffic stays inside the private network. Left empty, those calls go to the public address instead.

docServiceUrlPortal.description:
The address of this portal as the Document Server has to call it back on in order to fetch and save a
document. Set it when the Document Server cannot resolve the portal by its public name; left empty, the
portal's own resolved address is used.

docServiceSignatureSecret.description:
The shared secret that requests between the portal and the Document Server are signed with; it has to be the
same value the Document Server itself is configured with, otherwise the verification of the new settings
fails. It is write-only: the document service location is reported without it.

docServiceSignatureHeader.description:
The name of the HTTP header the signature travels in, which has to match the header the Document Server
expects. A secret without a header is not a usable pair and is rejected.

docServiceSslVerification.description:
Whether the portal validates the TLS certificate of the Document Server. With verification on, a self-signed
certificate breaks the connection; with it off, any certificate is accepted, which is meant for test
deployments only. Omitting the field turns verification on.

What the caller intends to do with the form. `view` asks for a read-only address and `embedded` for an address
to be shown inside a frame; both only resolve the address and leave the file untouched. Leave it out to enter
the filling flow, where the personal draft is created or reused. The value is matched case-insensitively, and
anything else behaves like an empty value.

Whether the caller asked for a read-only address. The server derives it from `action` being `view` and ignores
any value sent with the request.

requestEmbedded.description:
Whether the caller asked for an address to be shown inside a frame. The server derives it from `action` being
`embedded` and ignores any value sent with the request.

id.description:
The identifier of the reserved upload, repeated in the path of every call that follows it - the chunk uploads,
the finalize and the abort. It is thirty-two hexadecimal characters without separators, and it is the only
thing the server checks, so anyone holding it can write into this upload.

path.description:
The chain of folders leading to the destination, outermost first and the destination itself last, with folders
the caller cannot read left out. An answer that reports a stored part carries the destination folder alone
instead of the whole chain.

created.description: The moment the upload was reserved, in UTC.

expired.description:
The moment the reservation lapses and the parts buffered for it are dropped, in UTC. It is a gap rather than a
deadline for the whole transfer: every accepted part pushes it twelve hours past that part, so only a long
silence loses the upload.

location.description:
The absolute address of the separate chunk handler that also accepts the parts of this upload, kept for
clients written against it. A caller working through this API does not need it and sends the parts to the
session operations instead.

bytes_total.description:
The size in bytes that was declared when the upload was reserved, echoed back. It is what the arriving parts
are counted against to decide the file is complete, not the amount received so far.

ChunkedUploadSessionDto.description:
The reserved chunked upload: where the parts are sent, how much was declared and when the reservation lapses. No
content of the file is described here.

success.description:
Always true in a body that reaches the caller, because a call that does not succeed answers with an error
status and no body at all. It cannot be used to tell a refusal from a success.

data.description: The reserved upload itself, in the same shape the newer session operations answer with directly.

ChunkedUploadSessionResultDto.description: The reserved chunked upload wrapped in the envelope the two older session operations answer with.

response.description: The ChunkedUploadSessionResultDto object returned by the operation.

count.description: How many items this response carries: the length of the page for a list, 1 for a single object

total.description: How many items the whole list holds across all pages, for working out how many pages to request. Sent only by the operations that page their results, and left out of every other response

links.description: List of links related to the response

status.description: HTTP status code of the response

change.description:
Whether the user may switch between the two co-editing modes from the editor interface, or is held to the one
the portal preset.

fast.description:
Whether other participants see each change as it is typed. Left off, changes are exchanged only when a
participant saves, and the paragraph being edited is locked for the others meanwhile.

mode.description: The mode the two settings above amount to, as the editors name it.

CoEditingConfigDto.description: How co-editing is preset when the document opens, and whether the user may switch it afterwards.

oneOf.description: [Fast - Fast, Strict - Strict]
[0 - Fast, 1 - Strict]

document.description:
The document as the editors address it: its revision key, title, type, download address and the permissions of
this caller on it.

documentType.description:
The editor family the file opens in - `word`, `cell`, `slide`, `pdf` or `diagram`. It comes back empty for a
format no editor handles.

editorConfig.description:
How the editor is set up for this opening: the mode, the language, the interface customization, the callback
the editors save through, and the account they attribute changes to.

editorType.description:
The layout the configuration was actually built for. It echoes the requested one except where the room
overruled it, as the templates folder does by forcing the embedded viewer.

editorUrl.description:
The address of the editor api script the client has to load, with the shard key of this document already
appended. Load it as it is given rather than assembling it by hand.

token.description:
Signs this whole configuration so that the editors can trust it; anything a client changes in the
configuration invalidates it. It stays empty on a portal that has no signature secret configured for the
document service.

type.description:
The layout spelled as a lowercase word - `desktop`, `mobile` or `embedded` - the same value the editor type
carries as a number.

file.description: The file the configuration was built for, in the same shape the file listings report it.

errorMessage.description:
Filled in when the document could not be prepared for opening; the rest of the configuration should then not
be handed to the editors.

startFilling.description:
Whether this caller may start a filling session on the form from inside the editor. It stays empty when the
file is not a form opened where starting is possible at all.

fillingStatus.description:
True once the caller holds a role in the running filling session of this form. It stays empty outside a
virtual data room, where roles are the only place it is set.

startFillingMode.description:
Which filling button the editor offers: none at all, sharing the form out for others to fill, starting a
filling session, or starting one inside the form-filling room.

trackFormFieldChanges.description:
True when the editor should report the form fields renamed while the original form of a form-filling room is
edited, which is exactly when `PUT api/2.0/files/file/{fileId}/fieldchanges` accepts the reports. It is false
when the form is opened for viewing or filling, when the caller may not edit it, for a copy of a form, outside
a form-filling room, and with Document Server Community Edition, whose editors cannot tell the fields of the
open form.

fillingSessionId.description:
Identifies the filling session this opening belongs to, and is empty when the document is not opened as part
of one. Submissions made in the editor are collected under it.

quotaExceededScope.description:
Names the quota that ran out - the user, the room or the portal - and is set only when the document had to be
opened read-only because of it.

generationToolCallState.description:
The generation the editor should run as soon as the document opens. It is set only for a document an AI agent
produced and left waiting for its content, and is empty for every other file.

ConfigurationDto.description:
Everything an editor client needs in order to open one document: the document itself, the editor setup for this
caller, and the signature that lets the editors trust both.

response.description: The ConfigurationDto object returned by the operation.

count.description: How many items this response carries: the length of the page for a list, 1 for a single object

total.description: How many items the whole list holds across all pages, for working out how many pages to request. Sent only by the operations that page their results, and left out of every other response

links.description: List of links related to the response

status.description: HTTP status code of the response

statusCode.description: HTTP status code of the response (duplicate of status)

id.description:
The identifier of the conversion entry. The portal leaves it empty for file conversions, so a caller follows
its own conversion by the file it queued rather than by this value.

Operation.description:
Tells which kind of file operation the entry describes, so that a conversion can be told apart from the copy,
move and download entries that share this envelope. A conversion entry reports the conversion type.

progress.description:
How far the conversion has got, counted in percent from 0 while it is only queued to 100 once it is over -
whether it ended with a converted file or with an error. 100 is the value a polling caller waits for.

source.description:
Describes what is being converted: the identifier of the source file, the version that was taken and whether
an existing result may be overwritten, packed as a JSON object inside a string. It is what identifies the
entry when several conversions of the same caller are in flight.

result.description:
Carries the converted file once the conversion has finished, in the shape a file has elsewhere in this API
plus the title of the folder it was saved to, and stays empty while the conversion is still running. A
conversion that stopped because the source is password-protected reports the plain word `password` here
instead of a file.

error.description:
The reason the conversion stopped, in the language of the caller, and empty while it is running and after it
has succeeded. `progress` reaches 100 for a failure as well, so this field is what separates a converted file
from a broken conversion; a conversion still unfinished after ten minutes ends with a timeout reported here.

processed.description:
Reports whether the portal has taken the entry as far as it goes: `1` once the conversion has finished or
failed, and empty while it is still queued or still being converted. It is the bookkeeping of the conversion
queue rather than a result - what happened is in `progress`, `error` and `result`.

ConversationResultDto.description: The progress of one file conversion, together with the converted file once it exists.

drawPlaceHolders.description: Whether an empty form field shows its placeholder text in the result; false leaves it blank.

drawFormHighlight.description: Whether form fields keep their highlight colour in the result; false draws them without it.

isPrint.description:
Whether the print mode is turned on. It only applies to a docx converted into pdf: with the print mode off
the highlight flag does nothing and the placeholder flag saves the forms in the pdf.

ConvertDocumentLayoutRequest.description: The layout of forms printed as pdf documents or images.

textAssociation.description:
The rendering mode: blockChar reads the text by single characters, blockLine by separate lines, plainLine as
plain text with a paragraph per line, plainParagraph as plain text with lines combined into paragraphs.

ConvertDocumentRendererRequest.description: How the text of a pdf, xps or oxps source is read back when converting from it.

fileId.description: The id of the portal file to convert, as reported by a folder listing such as `GET api/2.0/files/{folderId}`.

folderId.description:
The id of the folder to save the converted file in, as reported by a folder listing such as
`GET api/2.0/files/{folderId}`.

codePage.description:
The encoding of a csv or txt source, as a code page number: 1251 for Cyrillic, 65001 for UTF-8, and so on.
Leaving it out lets the document service guess, which garbles non-latin text.

delimiter.description:
The character separating the values of a csv source: 0 - none, 1 - tab, 2 - semicolon, 3 - colon, 4 - comma,
5 - space.

documentLayout.description: The layout of forms printed as pdf documents or images.

documentRenderer.description: How the text of a pdf, xps or oxps source is read back.

outputtype.description:
The extension of the format to convert to, without the dot. The formats a source can become are listed under
`extsConvertible` in `GET api/2.0/files/settings`, keyed by the source extension, both with a leading dot there.

password.description: The password of the source document, for a document that is protected with one.

region.description: The culture code whose currency, date and time formats a spreadsheet converted to PDF is shown in.

thumbnail.description: How a thumbnail is fitted, when the target format is an image.

spreadsheetLayout.description: How a spreadsheet is laid out on the page, when it is converted to PDF.

pdf.description: The PDF settings, used when the target format is PDF.

ConvertFileRequestDto.description:
What to convert, where to keep the result, and the parameters the document service is handed. Everything below the
first two fields is the contract of the document service itself, named and shaped exactly as it names it, so that
the portal passes the request on rather than translating it. What the portal can read off the file - its format,
its name and the key of its revision - is not asked for and cannot be overridden.

form.description:
Whether the result is a fillable PDF form: true keeps the form fields of the source as fields to fill in,
false saves a plain PDF.

ConvertPdfRequest.description: The settings of a PDF result.

ignorePrintArea.description: Whether the print area chosen in the spreadsheet is ignored; false converts only that area.

orientation.description: The page orientation of the output PDF file: portrait or landscape.

fitToHeight.description: The number of pages the converted area is fitted into in height; 0 does not fit it.

scale.description: The scale of the output PDF file, in percent.

fitToWidth.description: The number of pages the converted area is fitted into in width; 0 does not fit it.

headings.description: Whether the row and column headings are printed in the output PDF file.

gridLines.description: Whether the grid lines are printed in the output PDF file.

margins.description: The margins of the output PDF file.

pageSize.description: The page size of the output PDF file.

ConvertSpreadsheetLayoutRequest.description: How a spreadsheet converted to PDF is laid out on the page. A field left out takes the document service default.

left.description: The left margin of the output PDF file.

right.description: The right margin of the output PDF file.

top.description: The top margin of the output PDF file.

bottom.description: The bottom margin of the output PDF file.

ConvertSpreadsheetMarginsRequest.description: The margins of the output PDF file, each a length with its unit: mm, cm or in.

height.description: The page height of the output PDF file.

width.description: The page width of the output PDF file.

ConvertSpreadsheetPageSizeRequest.description: The page size of the output PDF file, each side a length with its unit: mm, cm or in.

first.description: Whether a thumbnail is made of the first page only; false makes one of every page.

height.description: The thumbnail height in pixels; not used with aspect 2.

width.description: The thumbnail width in pixels; not used with aspect 2.

ConvertThumbnailRequest.description: How a thumbnail is fitted. A field left out takes the document service default.

destTitle.description:
The title of the copy, extension included. That extension decides the format: the same one as the source
copies the content as it is, a different one has it converted first.

destFolderId.description:
The folder the copy is placed in, as a number for a folder inside the portal and as a string for one in a
connected third-party storage; obtain it from `GET api/2.0/files/@root`. Anything else is answered with an
empty body and nothing is copied.

enableExternalExt.description: Whether the extension of the new title may be one the portal does not edit itself.

password.description: The password that opens the source document, for a file that is protected by one.

toForm.description:
Whether the copy is to become a PDF form rather than a plain document, which the conversion supports for the
text formats it can read.

CopyAsRequest.description: The parameters of a file copy that may change the format on the way.

color.description:
The background colour the room is drawn with while it has no logo, as six hexadecimal digits with no leading
number sign. An empty value restores the default colour of the room type.

cover.description:
The picture drawn on the room while it has no logo, named by an identifier from
`GET api/2.0/files/rooms/covers`. Any other value is rejected, and an empty value leaves the room without a
cover.

CoverRequestDto.description: The picture and the colour a room is drawn with while it has no logo.

response.description: The list of CoversResultDto objects returned by the operation.

count.description: How many items this response carries: the length of the page for a list, 1 for a single object

total.description: How many items the whole list holds across all pages, for working out how many pages to request. Sent only by the operations that page their results, and left out of every other response

links.description: List of links related to the response

status.description: HTTP status code of the response

statusCode.description: HTTP status code of the response (duplicate of status)

CoversResultArrayWrapper.description: The successful API response containing the list of CoversResultDto objects.

id.description:
The name of the cover, and the value to send as `cover` when a room is created or changed. The names are the
same on every portal and do not change with the language of the request.

data.description:
The drawing itself, as inline vector markup ready to be rendered as it is. It is the default size of the
cover, and it may change between product versions while the name stays.

CoversResultDto.description: One drawing of the built-in gallery of room covers.

title.description:
The title of the new file. The extension in it decides the format, and one of a known text, spreadsheet or
presentation format is rewritten to the DOCX, XLSX or PPTX of the portal unless `enableExternalExt` says
otherwise; a title with no extension gets DOCX added.

templateId.description:
An existing file the new one copies its content from, as a number for a file in the portal and as a string for
one in a connected third-party storage; the caller has to be able to read it. Left out, a blank template for
the format and the language of the caller is used.

enableExternalExt.description:
Whether the extension of the title is kept as it is: `true` stores the title verbatim, `false` rewrites a
known foreign format to the format the portal edits itself.

formId.description:
A ready form from the form gallery of the portal to copy instead of a template, named by the identifier the
gallery reports for it. It takes precedence over `templateId`; 0 means no form.

CreateFileRequest.description: The parameters of a file that the portal creates from a template or a blank document.

title.description:
The title the folder is given. It is trimmed before it is stored and may not be blank or consist of spaces
alone; it need not differ from the titles of the neighbouring folders, so the same title may appear twice in
one parent.

CreateFolderRequest.description: The title a folder is created with or renamed to.

visible.description: Specifies if the template is visible in the UI pickers.

items.description: The parameters of a metadata field.

fields.description: The template metadata fields. At least one field is required: a template without fields is not created.

CreateMetadataTemplateRequestDto.description: The request parameters for creating a metadata template.

templateId.description:
The room template to copy. Templates live in their own section and are listed by `GET api/2.0/files/rooms`
with a search area of 4; an ordinary room id is rejected here.

title.description:
The name of the room to create. It is sanitised and truncated the way a room title is, and a blank value is
rejected; the title of the template is not reused.

logo.description:
The picture to use as the room logo, named by the path that `POST api/2.0/files/logos` returned for an image
uploaded beforehand, plus the crop to take from it. Leaving the field out keeps the room on its cover and
colour. It is ignored when the logo of the template is copied instead.

copyLogo.description:
Whether the new room keeps the logo of the template. With it on the uploaded picture is ignored; with it off
the room starts with no logo unless one is supplied.

tags.description:
The labels to attach to the room, by name. Names the portal tag catalogue does not hold yet are added to it,
and `GET api/2.0/files/tags` lists what already exists. Leaving the field out keeps the tags of the template.

color.description:
The background colour the room is drawn with while it has no logo, as six hexadecimal digits with no leading
number sign. An empty value restores the default colour of the room type.

cover.description:
The picture drawn on the room while it has no logo, named by an identifier from
`GET api/2.0/files/rooms/covers`. Any other value is rejected, and an empty value leaves the room without a
cover.

quota.description:
The storage the room may take, in bytes. It is accepted only while the per-room quota feature is on for the
portal and must stay inside the portal own limit; leaving it out lets the room follow the portal default.

indexing.description:
Whether the room keeps a manual order of its contents. With it on every file and folder carries a position
that listings follow and that `PUT api/2.0/files/rooms/{id}/reorder` compacts; with it off the contents are
ordered by the sorting of the request. Leaving it out keeps the setting of the template.

denyDownload.description:
Whether members without editing rights are stopped from downloading and printing the contents of the room.
They can still open the documents in the editor. Leaving it out keeps the setting of the template.

lifetime.description:
How long files may stay in the room before they are deleted automatically. The countdown starts when the
setting is saved, and leaving the field out keeps the files forever. Leaving the field out keeps the setting
of the template.

watermark.description:
The watermark drawn over documents opened in the room. Leaving the field out adds no watermark, and sending it
with the switch turned off removes the one the room has. Leaving the field out keeps the setting of the
template.

private.description:
Whether the room is end-to-end encrypted. Its files can then be opened only in the desktop application by
members whose encryption keys are set up, and the flag cannot be changed after the room is created.

CreateRoomFromTemplateDto.description: The parameters of a room built from a room template.

title.description:
The name of the room. It is trimmed, characters that a folder name cannot hold are replaced with underscores
and the rest is truncated, so the stored title can differ from the one sent; a blank title is rejected. Titles
are not unique, and rooms are told apart by their id.

quota.description:
The storage the room may take, in bytes. It is accepted only while the per-room quota feature is on for the
portal and must stay inside the portal own limit; leaving it out lets the room follow the portal default.

indexing.description:
Whether the room keeps a manual order of its contents. With it on every file and folder carries a position
that listings follow and that `PUT api/2.0/files/rooms/{id}/reorder` compacts; with it off the contents are
ordered by the sorting of the request.

denyDownload.description:
Whether members without editing rights are stopped from downloading and printing the contents of the room.
They can still open the documents in the editor.

lifetime.description:
How long files may stay in the room before they are deleted automatically. The countdown starts when the
setting is saved, and leaving the field out keeps the files forever.

watermark.description:
The watermark drawn over documents opened in the room. Leaving the field out adds no watermark, and sending it
with the switch turned off removes the one the room has.

logo.description:
The picture to use as the room logo, named by the path that `POST api/2.0/files/logos` returned for an image
uploaded beforehand, plus the crop to take from it. Leaving the field out keeps the room on its cover and
colour.

tags.description:
The labels to attach to the room, by name. Names the portal tag catalogue does not hold yet are added to it,
and `GET api/2.0/files/tags` lists what already exists.

color.description:
The background colour the room is drawn with while it has no logo, as six hexadecimal digits with no leading
number sign. An empty value restores the default colour of the room type.

cover.description:
The picture drawn on the room while it has no logo, named by an identifier from
`GET api/2.0/files/rooms/covers`. Any other value is rejected, and an empty value leaves the room without a
cover.

roomType.description:
What the room is for. It decides which sharing links, roles and form features the room offers, and it cannot
be changed once the room exists, so a room of the wrong kind has to be recreated.

private.description:
Whether the room is end-to-end encrypted. Its files can then be opened only in the desktop application by
members whose encryption keys are set up, and the flag cannot be changed after the room is created.

items.description: One sharing entry: an account, a group or an email address, and the access level it is given.

share.description:
Not implemented on room creation: any non-empty value is rejected, and members are invited afterwards with
`PUT api/2.0/files/rooms/{id}/share`.

chatSettings.description:
The model and the prompt an AI room answers with. It belongs to AI rooms only and is rejected for a room of
any other kind.

sendFormToExternalDB.description:
For a form filling room, whether the data of every completed submission is also pushed to the external
database configured for the portal. It is what `POST api/2.0/files/rooms/{id}/externaldbsync` re-runs for the
forms already collected.

saveFormAsXLSX.description:
For a form filling room, whether the collected submissions are also gathered into a spreadsheet stored next to
the completed forms. With it off the submissions are kept only as the filled documents themselves.

CreateRoomRequestDto.description: The parameters of a new room in the Rooms section.

name.description:
The name of the tag to create, which is also its identity: tags are addressed by name everywhere, there is no
separate identifier. It is stored exactly as sent, spacing and case included, and a name that is already in
the catalog gives back that tag instead of a second one.

CreateTagRequestDto.description: The parameters for adding a custom tag to the portal catalog of room tags.

title.description:
The title of the file. The extension the operation stands for is appended unless the title already ends with
it, so "Notes" becomes "Notes.txt" or "Notes.html".

content.description:
The content of the file, as plain text or as HTML markup. A request carrying none is rejected as an invalid
request, and for a text file content that looks like markup makes the portal store it as HTML instead.

createNewIfExist.description:
What to do when the folder already holds a file of this title, the other way round than the name reads: `true`
updates that file and adds a version to its history, `false` creates another file and makes its title unique,
as in "Notes (1).txt".

CreateTextOrHtmlFileRequest.description: The parameters of a text or HTML file created from content sent in the request.

createAsNewFolder.description:
Creates a new folder named after `title` inside the folder named in the path and turns that subfolder into the
room, leaving the named folder itself untouched. When omitted, the named folder becomes the room and keeps
everything it already holds.

title.description:
The name the room is shown under. It is stored on the connected account, so it does not have to match the name
of the folder in the storage; with `createAsNewFolder` it is also the name given to the created subfolder.

roomType.description:
The kind of room the folder becomes, which decides the default access rules of its members and cannot be
changed afterwards.

private.description:
Restricts the room to the members explicitly invited into it. The flag is kept on the connected storage
account rather than on the folder, so every folder read through that account reports the same value.

indexing.description:
Keeps the contents of the room in an explicit numbered order, the one reported as `order` on every entry,
instead of leaving the order to the reader.

denyDownload.description:
Forbids downloading and printing the contents of the room, which leaves the members with viewing and editing
in the editor only.

color.description:
The background colour drawn behind the cover of the room, as six hexadecimal digits without a leading number
sign. An empty value restores the colour the portal picks by default.

cover.description:
The drawing shown on the room tile, named by one of the built-in cover identifiers returned by
`GET api/2.0/files/rooms/covers`. An empty value leaves the room without a cover, and any other unknown value
is rejected as an invalid request.

tags.description:
The tags to attach to the room, named by their text. A name that is not in the portal tag catalogue yet is
added to it, and `GET api/2.0/files/tags` lists the names already there.

logo.description:
The picture to use as the room logo, which has to be uploaded with `POST api/2.0/files/logos` first; leaving
it out keeps the room on its cover and colour.

CreateThirdPartyRoomRequest.description: The room to be created out of a folder of a connected third-party storage account.

name.description: The field name. The names are matched without regard to case.

value.description: The field value. Null or empty removes the field from the entry.

CustomFieldRequest.description: The parameters of a custom text field.

response.description: The list of CustomFieldValueDto objects returned by the operation.

count.description: How many items this response carries: the length of the page for a list, 1 for a single object

total.description: How many items the whole list holds across all pages, for working out how many pages to request. Sent only by the operations that page their results, and left out of every other response

links.description: List of links related to the response

status.description: HTTP status code of the response

statusCode.description: HTTP status code of the response (duplicate of status)

CustomFieldValueArrayWrapper.description: The successful API response containing the list of CustomFieldValueDto objects.

value.description: The field value on the entry.

CustomFieldValueDto.description:
The custom text field of an entry: a free-form name with its value. Custom fields belong to no template, need no
assignment and are addressed by name.

enabled.description:
The state to reach: `true` turns the mode on, so that the sorting and filtering each person applies stays
visible to that person alone, and drops the others out of a running editing session; `false` turns it off and
makes filtering shared again.

CustomFilterRequest.description: The Custom Filter state a spreadsheet is to be put into.

address.description: The postal address from the portal branding settings; empty when none was entered.

logo.description: The About-panel logo of the organization.

logoDark.description: The About-panel logo for a dark interface theme.

mail.description: The contact address from the portal branding settings.

name.description: The organization name shown in the editor.

CustomerConfigDto.description:
The branding of the organization running the portal, as the editor About panel shows it. It is reported on a
server installation only.

about.description: Whether the About entry of the editor menu is shown.

customer.description:
The branding of the organization running the portal. It is filled in on a server installation only and is
empty in the cloud.

anonymous.description: How an anonymous participant is treated in this session.

feedback.description: The support link the editor offers behind its feedback button.

forcesave.description:
Whether the editors write intermediate revisions while the document stays open. It is empty when the portal
leaves the decision to the editors themselves.

goback.description:
Where the editor returns the user to when they leave the document. It is empty when there is nowhere to go
back to, as in an embedded opening.

review.description: How tracked changes are displayed when the document opens; it depends on whether this session may write.

queued build.

The message of the failure that stopped the build. It is filled in only for a task that ended in the failed
state, and stays empty while the task runs and after it succeeds.

How far the build has got, from 0 to 100. It advances in a few coarse steps rather than smoothly, so it is a

report and is not unique: a second build adds another file instead of replacing the first.

publicKey.description:
The public half of the pair, the half a client encrypts file keys with. A pair whose public half is missing
is treated as no access and left out of a room's or a file's key set.

privateKeyEnc.description:
The private half, encrypted with its owner's password. It is filled in only when the pair belongs to the
calling user; on another member's entry it comes back empty, because the private half is not handed out.

cryptoEngineId.description:
The crypto engine this material was issued for, as a braced GUID. The engine is portal-wide, so the same value
comes back for every key of every member.

EncryptionKeyDto.description:
An encryption key pair as the portal reports it: the public half of some member's key, with the encrypted private
half filled in only when the pair belongs to the caller.

id.description:
Names the pair inside the caller's own key set. The client generates it, and leaving it out means the all-zero
GUID, which is the pair a client that never sends an identifier keeps working with.

publicKey.description:
The public half of the pair, as the client's crypto engine produced it and stored verbatim. This is the half
handed to the other members of a private room so that they can encrypt file keys for this user.

privateKeyEnc.description:
The private half of the pair, encrypted on the client with the user's password before it is sent. The portal
stores it as opaque text and cannot decrypt it, so material lost on the client cannot be recovered from here.

EncryptionKeyRequestDto.description:
The two halves of an encryption key pair to store for the calling user, plus the identifier the pair is kept
under.

id.description: The field ID.

items.description: The metadata field choice option.

options.description: The choice options of the field.

order.description: The field display order inside the template.

value.description: The value of the field on the entry, or `null` when the entry holds no value for it.

templates.description: The assigned metadata templates, each field carrying its value on the entry.

items.description:
The custom text field of an entry: a free-form name with its value. Custom fields belong to no template, need no
assignment and are addressed by name.

customFields.description: The custom fields with their values.

hasMetadataFields.description:
Whether the entry has a metadata field a user can see and fill, by hand or with the AI filling: a field of a
template in `templates` whose `visible` is true, or a custom field in `customFields`. False when both lists are
empty, when every template is hidden, or when none of the visible ones has a field. It says nothing about the
values: it stays true once every field is filled. The same flag is carried by the entry in a folder listing and
in the file and folder info responses as `hasMetadataFields`, so a client that has the listing needs no call here
to decide whether to offer the filling.

id.description:
The file of the original form whose collected data was exported. It is the form itself, not one of the filled
copies, so the same id can be read with the file operations of the portal.

title.description:
The name of that form file at the moment of the export. It is empty when the form file no longer exists, which
is also the case in which the export of that entry fails.

success.description:
Whether the data of this form reached the external database. One rejected form does not stop the others, so a
finished job can hold both successful and failed entries.

error.description:
Why this form was not exported. It is empty for a successful entry, and for a failed one it carries either the
message of the underlying failure or the generic export error of the portal.

ExternalDbSyncFormResultDto.description: What happened to one original form while the room was being exported to the external database.

id.description:
The identifier of the job, which stays the same while a job for this room exists and is worth quoting when a
failure has to be traced in the portal logs. Polling is done by room, so the value is not needed to read the
state again.

error.description:
The message of a failure that stopped the whole job. It is empty while the job is running and after a job that
ended without such a failure; a job that finished with individual forms rejected reports those in `forms` and
leaves this field empty.

percentage.description:
How much of the work is done, from 0 to 100. It advances as the forms of the room are processed one by one, so
it is a usable progress indicator for a room with many forms and jumps straight to the end for a room with
one.

isCompleted.description:
Whether the job has ended. It is set both for a job that finished its work and for one that stopped on an
error, so this is the flag to poll for, and `status` and `error` are what tell the two apart.

status.description:
How the job ended, or how far it has got: queued, running, finished, cancelled or failed. It is the only field
that separates a successful end from a failed one once `isCompleted` is set.

items.description: What happened to one original form while the room was being exported to the external database.

forms.description:
The outcome for every original form of the room, one entry each. The list is empty while the job is running
and is filled in only when the job ends, so it is what to read after `isCompleted` turns true; it stays empty
for a room that holds no forms at all.

portal.

status.description:
How validating the link went. It is the first field to read: a refused link is reported here with the answer
still arriving as a success. A link that resolved describes both the entry and the link, one that is waiting
for its password describes only the entry, and one that failed outright leaves the rest of the object empty.

id.description:
The identifier of the room, folder or file the link points at, always rendered as a string even where the
portal stores it as a number. It is null when the link could not be resolved.

title.description:
The title of the entry the link points at, suitable for showing to the visitor before they are let in. It is
null when the link could not be resolved.

type.description:
Whether the link points at a folder - a room counts as one - or at a single file. It is null when the link
could not be resolved.

tenantId.description:
The portal the link belongs to, which matters for a client that works with more than one. It stays 0 for a
link that did not resolve.

entityId.description:
The identifier of the entry that was asked about through the request's file or folder parameter, echoed back
once it was found under the link's target. It is null when nothing was asked about, or when the entry lies
outside what the link opens.

entityTitle.description: The title of that entry, null under the same conditions as its identifier.

entityType.description: Whether that entry is a folder or a file, null under the same conditions as its identifier.

isRoom.description:
True when the link opens a whole room rather than one entry inside it. It is null for a link to a file and for
a link that did not resolve.

shared.description:
True when the entry now sits in the calling account's own lists - it was already shared with that account, or
resolving the link has just put it there. It stays false for a visitor browsing without an account, who
reaches the entry through the link alone.

linkId.description:
The link the token belongs to, which is also the subject under which the link appears among the sharing rights
of the entry. It is an empty identifier when the link did not resolve.

isAuthenticated.description:
Whether the request carried a signed-in account. It says nothing about that account's rights on the entry, so
it must not be read as permission - it is false for every anonymous visitor and true for any member, even one
who is a stranger to the room.

isRoomMember.description:
Whether the signed-in caller already has rights of their own on the room that holds the entry, as opposed to
reaching it through this link. It is false for an anonymous visitor and for a member who has never been
invited.

ExternalShareDto.description: The outcome of validating an external share link and the entry it points at.

password.description:
The password chosen by the member who shared the entry, spelled exactly as they typed it. It is compared
against the stored value and never returned back; a mismatch is reported through the answer's status instead
of an error.

ExternalShareRequestParam.description: The password that unlocks a protected external share link.

externalShare.description:
Whether links that open a file or a room without a portal account may be created. While it is false the portal
also reports sharing on social networks as off and the default link type as internal, whatever was asked for.

defaultShareLinkInternal.description:
The kind of link the portal offers first: true means a link only accounts of this portal can open, false one
that anyone holding it can open.

externalShareApplyToDocuments.description:
Whether the restriction covers personal documents. It only has an effect while external sharing is off, so a
true here with sharing allowed restricts nothing.

externalShareApplyToRooms.description:
Whether the restriction covers rooms, including the creation of new public ones. It only has an effect while
external sharing is off.

blockExistingLinksOnRestrict.description:
Whether links created before the restriction stop opening as well. With false they keep working and only new
ones are refused.

ExternalSharingSettingsDto.description: The external sharing policy of the portal as it now stands.

externalShare.description:
Whether links that open a file or a room without a portal account may be created at all. This is the master
switch of the policy: while it is false the portal keeps the default link type internal, turns sharing on
social networks off, and applies the three restriction fields below.

defaultShareLinkInternal.description:
The kind of link offered first when a new one is created: true offers a link only accounts of this portal can
open, false one that anyone holding it can open. The portal keeps it at true while external sharing is
switched off.

externalShareApplyToDocuments.description:
Whether the restriction reaches personal documents: with true, no external link can be created for an entry in
the caller's own documents while external sharing is off. It has no effect while external sharing is allowed.

externalShareApplyToRooms.description:
Whether the restriction reaches rooms: with true, no external link can be created for a room or its content
while external sharing is off, and a new room cannot be made public. It has no effect while external sharing
is allowed.

blockExistingLinksOnRestrict.description:
What happens to the links that already exist once external sharing is switched off: with true they stop
opening for the sections named above, with false they keep working and only new ones are refused. This is the
field that changes access to data that is already shared.

ExternalSharingSettingsRequestDto.description:
The complete external sharing policy of the portal. Every field is written, so an omitted one is stored as
false.

FileConflictResolveType.description: The overwriting behavior of the file copying or moving.

folderId.description:
The folder the file is stored in. When the file was reached through a share and the caller cannot open its
real parent, the identifier of the Shared with me section is reported instead, so this is where the file is
visible rather than where it physically sits.

version.description:
The revision this entry describes. It starts at 1 and moves to the next number each time new content is stored
over the file, except for an editing session opened against the file itself, which replaces the content and
keeps the number. `GET api/2.0/files/file/{fileId}/history` lists them all.

versionGroup.description:
Groups revisions that belong together, which is how a history can fold a long editing session into one entry:
versions saved inside one session share this number, and an upload over the file starts a new group.

contentLength.description:
The size already formatted for display, with a unit and the separators of the caller's language. Read
`pureContentLength` for a number to calculate with.

pureContentLength.description: The size of the stored content in bytes, and null for an empty file.

fileStatus.description:
What the portal is currently doing with the file and how the caller stands towards it - open in the editor,
unread, being converted, and so on. The value is a bit mask that combines those states, so a file can report a
number that matches none of the published members on its own.

editingBy.description:
The accounts that have the file open in the editor at this moment, as account identifier to display name, and
empty when nobody has. The all-zero identifier stands for people who came in through an external link without
signing in, and its name carries their number in brackets when there is more than one.

mute.description:
Not a property of the file at all: it repeats, inverted, the calling account's own switch for new-item badges,
so it is the same in every entry of one answer. True means that account has badges turned off.

viewUrl.description:
The address that returns the bytes of the file - a download, in spite of the name; `webUrl` is the address a
person opens. When the file was reached through an external link the address carries the key of that link, so
it keeps working without signing in.

webUrl.description:
The page that opens the file in a browser: the editor for a format the portal edits, the media viewer for
pictures, audio and video, and the download address for a format it cannot show at all.

fileType.description:
The broad kind of content, worked out from the extension, which is what a client uses to pick an icon or a
viewer without parsing `fileExst` itself.

fileExst.description:
The extension of the stored file, leading dot included and always lower case. For a format the portal keeps in
a converted shape this is the extension it is served under, not the one it was uploaded with.

comment.description:
The note kept with this revision. The portal writes it itself for revisions it creates, an upload over an
existing file among them, and an editor stores the note a person typed when saving a version.

encrypted.description:
True for a file in a private room, whose content the server never sees and which therefore cannot be converted
or taken over by an upload. Null, rather than false, for an ordinary file.

thumbnailUrl.description:
The address of the generated preview image. It is filled in only while `thumbnailStatus` says the preview has
been created, and it carries a suffix that changes with the file, so an image cached for an earlier revision
is not reused.

thumbnailStatus.description:
How far the preview image has got. Only the created state means `thumbnailUrl` holds an address; the others
mean there is none, either because it is still being produced or because this format has no preview.

locked.description:
True while the file is held under a lock that stops anyone but its holder from editing it, and null rather
than false when there is no lock. `lockedBy` names the holder unless the caller is the holder.

lockedBy.description:
The display name of the account holding the lock, and null when the caller holds it - so `locked` true
together with no name here means the lock is the caller's own.

hasDraft.description:
For a fillable PDF form, whether the caller already has a filling draft of it, in which case `draftLocation`
says where that draft lives. Null for anything that is not a form.

formFillingStatus.description:
How far the filling of this form has got for the calling account, and whose turn it is now. It is worked out
only inside a virtual data room, where filling runs in steps; everywhere else it stays at the none value.

isForm.description: Whether the file is a PDF, and so offered as a fillable form. It is null for any other file type.

customFilterEnabled.description:
True while a spreadsheet is in the mode where each person sorts and filters their own view without changing
what the others see, and null rather than false when it is not.

customFilterEnabledBy.description: The display name of the account that turned that mode on, and null when the caller turned it on themselves.

startFilling.description:
For a form in a room for filling, whether it has been released for filling; until then it is still being
prepared and only the people running the room work with it. Null for a file this does not apply to.

isFillingPreparing.description:
True during the short window in which a released form is still being written out by the editor. Neither
filling nor editing is accepted while it lasts, so a client should wait and read the file again.

inProcessFolderId.description: Left empty by the portal: the folder holding the caller's draft is reported in `draftLocation` instead.

inProcessFolderTitle.description: Left empty by the portal, like the identifier beside it; the draft's folder is named in `draftLocation`.

resultsFolderId.description:
The folder that collects the completed copies of this form. It is filled in only for the original form of a
room for filling, and only for a caller allowed to work with that form; null everywhere else.

draftLocation.description:
Where the caller's own filling draft of this form is kept. Null when there is no draft yet, which is the same
thing `hasDraft` reports.

viewAccessibility.description:
Which ways of opening this format the portal supports at all - its own editor, the picture viewer, the media
player and so on. It answers whether the format can be shown, not whether this account may do it; rights are
reported in `security`.

lastOpened.description:
The moment the caller last opened the file. It is kept per account and is what orders the Recent section, so
it is null for a file this account has never opened. Written with the offset of the portal's time zone.

expired.description:
The moment the file falls under the lifetime rule of the room holding it and is removed. It is counted from
the first revision rather than the latest one, so editing a file does not postpone it, and it is null when the
room sets no lifetime. Written with the offset of the portal's time zone.

vectorizationStatus.description:
How far the indexing of the file's content for AI search has got. It is null for a file that has never been
queued for indexing, which is every file while the feature is off for the portal.

externalDbTableName.description:
The table collecting the submitted values of this form in the external database configured for its room. The
field is left out of the answer entirely when the form has no such table.

dimensions.description:
The pixel size of the picture, measured by reading the stored file rather than taken from any stored metadata.
Null for anything that is not a picture the portal can show, and also when the file could not be read.

FileDto.description:
A stored file as the calling account sees it: where it lives, which revision this is, how it can be opened and
what the portal is currently doing with it.

items.description:
An encryption key pair as the portal reports it: the public half of some member's key, with the encrypted private
half filled in only when the pair belongs to the caller.

userKeys.description:
The key pairs of the calling account, never those of the other people in the room. The private half of each
pair is stored encrypted with that person's own password and has to be decrypted on the client. An empty list
means the account has generated no key pair yet, and until it does no file key can be issued to it.

items.description: The encrypted file key issued to one user.

fileKeys.description:
The keys of this file that were issued to the calling account, each naming the public key it was encrypted for
so that the client can pick the matching private half. An empty list means the file has not been shared with
this account rather than that the file is unencrypted.

title.description:
The name shown for the entry. For a file it carries the extension, which is how the format is recognised, and
for a room it is the room name.

access.description:
The level the calling account holds on this entry, resolved from its own rights, the groups it belongs to and
any link it came in through. It is the level itself, not what the account may do with it - the action flags
below answer that.

sharedBy.description:
Who gave the calling account the access it is using. It is filled in only while the entry is being read
through a share, and never for a caller without an account.

ownedBy.description:
Who owns the place the entry is shared from - the creator of the room it lies in, or of the personal section
that holds it. It is filled in only while the entry is being read through a share, and never for a caller
without an account.

shared.description:
Whether at least one external link exists for the entry, whichever kind. It says nothing about accounts and
groups - those are counted by the flag for members below.

sharedForUser.description:
Whether at least one account or group has been given rights on the entry directly, as opposed to reaching it
through a link or through the room around it.

sharedExternal.description:
Whether one of the entry's links is open to people outside the portal, as opposed to a link that only its own
members can follow. This is the flag to watch when the concern is who can reach the content from outside.

parentShared.description:
Whether the entry is reachable because the room or folder around it is shared, rather than through rights of
its own. A copy or a move takes the entry out of that scope.

shortWebUrl.description:
A shortened address that opens the entry through the link it is being read with. It is an empty string
whenever no link applies, which is the usual case for a member browsing their own rooms.

created.description:
When the entry was created, written with the offset of the portal's time zone. For a file restored from an
older version this is still the moment the file first appeared.

createdBy.description:
Who created the entry. It is null for a caller without an account, who is told nothing about the portal's
members.

updated.description:
When the entry last changed, written with the offset of the portal's time zone. It is never reported as
earlier than the creation moment, so the two can be compared safely.

autoDelete.description:
When the entry will disappear on its own, written with the offset of the portal's time zone. It is filled in
only where a removal is actually scheduled - something in the trash while the portal cleans it up
automatically, or a guest's own documents - so a null means nothing is scheduled rather than that the entry is
permanent.

rootFolderType.description:
The section the entry ultimately belongs to, which is what tells a personal document from one inside a room,
from a template and from something in the trash or the archive.

parentRoomType.description:
The kind of room the entry lies in, which decides what the room allows - filling forms, public links,
indexing. It is null for an entry that is not inside a room at all.

updatedBy.description: Who changed the entry last. It is null for a caller without an account.

providerItem.description:
Set when the entry is stored on a connected third-party account rather than on the portal, and null when it is
stored on the portal. Such an entry is identified by a string rather than a number, and some operations skip
it.

providerKey.description:
Which third-party service holds the entry, matching the keys accepted by the third-party operations. It is
null for an entry stored on the portal.

providerId.description:
The connected account the entry comes from, for telling apart two connections to the same service. It is null
for an entry stored on the portal.

order.description:
The place of the entry in a room where the members arrange the content themselves, given as the position of
the entry preceded by the positions of the folders leading to it, separated by dots. It is empty when nothing
has been arranged.

isFavorite.description:
Set when the calling account has marked the entry as a favorite, which is what puts it into the favorites
listing. For a file that is not marked it is null rather than false.

fileEntryType.description:
Tells a folder from a file, and so which of the two shapes the rest of the object has. A room is reported as a
folder here.

entryKind.description: Which concrete type the object is: `file`, `thirdPartyFile`, `folder`, `thirdPartyFolder`. It is what tells the types apart in a list that mixes several of them; a response limited by `fields` may leave it out.

FileEntryBaseDto.description:
What every file and folder in an answer has in common; the concrete shape is a file or a folder, told apart by the
entry type.

id.description:
The identifier to pass back to the other operations of this entry. It is a number for storage on the portal
and a string for a connected third-party account, and it is unique only within its own kind, so files and
folders may carry the same value.

rootFolderId.description:
The section the entry ultimately lies in, as an identifier that can be listed like any other folder. For an
entry inside a room this is the rooms section, not the room.

originId.description:
The folder the entry was deleted from, which is where restoring it puts it back. It is left out of the answer
unless the entry is in the trash.

originRoomId.description: The room the entry was deleted from, left out of the answer for anything that was not deleted out of a room.

originTitle.description:
The name of the folder the entry was deleted from, for showing where it would be restored to. It is null for
an entry that is not in the trash.

originRoomTitle.description: The name of the room the entry was deleted from, null for anything that was not deleted out of a room.

canShare.description:
Whether the calling account may change who has access to the entry, and so whether offering a sharing dialog
for it makes sense. It is false in rooms whose access is fixed by the room itself, such as a private one, even
for its manager.

shareSettings.description:
How many links of each kind currently exist for the entry, counted separately for the primary link and the
additional ones. Kinds with no links are left out, and the whole field is null when the caller may not change
the access or no link exists at all.

security.description:
What the calling account may do with this entry, one flag per action, and the cheapest way to decide which
operations to offer without trying them. The flags already take the room's settings and the account's role
into account.

availableShareRights.description:
Which access levels may be handed out on this entry, listed per kind of recipient, so that a client offers
only levels the entry actually supports - a room for filling forms and a plain folder do not accept the same
ones.

requestToken.description:
The token of the link the entry is being read through, which is the value the external-share operations expect
and which also has to be carried by the download and preview addresses. It is null whenever the entry is not
being read through a link.

external.description:
Set when the link being used was made for this very entry, and false when the entry is reached through a link
to the room around it. It is null when no link is involved.

expirationDate.description:
When the link being used stops working, written with the offset of the portal's time zone. It is null for a
link that never expires and whenever no link is involved.

isLinkExpired.description:
Set when the link being used has already passed its expiration date, which is why the entry cannot be opened
even though it is described here. It is null when no link is involved.

assignedMetadataTemplates.description: The IDs of the metadata templates assigned to the file entry.

hasMetadataFields.description:
Whether the entry has a metadata field a user can see and fill, by hand or with the AI filling: a field of a
visible assigned template, or a custom field. False when the entry has no metadata, when its assigned templates
are all hidden, or when they have no fields. It says nothing about the values: it stays true once every field is
filled, and nothing about the caller's rights: writing the values still needs the right to edit the entry
(`security.Edit`). It cannot be derived from `assignedMetadataTemplates`, which lists hidden templates too and
never lists the custom fields. Present, with a value, in the folder listing and in the file and folder info
responses; absent in the other responses that carry an entry (the answer to a creation, an upload or a rename),
which do not compute it, and for an entry of a third-party storage, which has no metadata. The same flag is
answered by `GET api/2.0/files/metadata/file/{fileId}` and `GET api/2.0/files/metadata/folder/{folderId}`.

items.description:
Where a text search met the metadata of a file, a folder or a room: one string value that holds the searched text,
with the field it belongs to.

metadataMatches.description:
Where the search text of the listing was met in the metadata of the entry: one item per string value holding
the text, in the order of the fields. Present only in a listing filtered by text, and only for the entries whose
metadata contain it; an entry found by its title alone carries nothing here.

FileEntryDto.description:
The part of a file or folder that depends on how the entry is identified: by a number on the portal, or by a
string on a connected third-party account.

oneOf.description: [Folder - Folder, File - File]
[1 - Folder, 2 - File]

userId.description: The identifier of the user the file key was issued to.

publicKeyId.description: The identifier of the key pair the file key is encrypted for.

privateKeyEnc.description: The file key, encrypted with the public key of the pair.

tenantId.description: The identifier of the portal the file belongs to.

fileId.description: The identifier of the file the key unlocks.

createOn.description: The date and time when the file key was issued.

FileKeysDto.description: The encrypted file key issued to one user.

skippedUserIds.description:
The recipients whose key was not stored, because they can no longer read the file. Empty when every key was
stored.

FileKeysWrittenDto.description: The outcome of issuing file keys.

filetype.description:
The format the stored content is in, lower-cased and with the leading dot, which is how the document
service learns how to read the bytes behind the address. It stays empty when the file title carries no
extension at all.

token.description:
Signs the address and the format above so that the document service can trust them. It stays empty on a
portal that has no signature secret configured for the document service, and the address is then meant
to be fetched unsigned.

url.description:
Where the content is fetched from: the portal download handler, pinned to the revision the file was at
when the address was issued and carrying an authorisation key of limited validity. It is addressed to
the host the document service can reach, which on a deployment with a private editor network is not the
address a browser should follow.

FileLinkDto.description:
The address the content of a file is fetched from, together with the signature that authorises the fetch, as
the document service is handed it.

linkId.description:
The link to rewrite, as reported by `GET api/2.0/files/file/{id}/links`. An identifier that is not yet in use,
the empty one included, creates a link instead.

access.description: The rights the link grants to whoever follows it. The value that denies everything revokes the link.

expirationDate.description:
The moment the link stops working, read in the time zone of the portal. A date more than a few years ahead is
rejected as an invalid request; left out, the link does not expire on its own.

title.description:
The name the link carries in the sharing list of the file, for the people who manage it; it is not shown to
whoever follows the link.

internal.description:
Who may follow the link: `true` admits only accounts that are signed in to the portal, `false` admits anybody
who has the address.

primary.description:
Whether this link becomes the primary link of the file - the one the "Copy link" action of a client hands out.
A file has one primary link at a time.

denyDownload.description:
What a visitor may do with the content: `true` leaves them with viewing in the browser, `false` lets them
download and print it as their rights allow.

password.description: The secret a visitor has to type before the file opens; left out, the link opens without one.

id.description:
The identifier of the operation, the one to pass to `PUT api/2.0/files/fileops/terminate/{id}` to stop it.
Operations belong to the account that started them, so an identifier of somebody else is never listed here.

Operation.description:
What the operation does with the entries, which also decides what else is reported: only a download fills
`url`, and a deletion leaves `files` and `folders` empty.

progress.description:
How far the operation has come, from 0 to 100. Reaching 100 only means it stopped; whether it did what it was
asked for is told by `error`.

error.description:
The reason the operation could not finish its work, in the language of the request. Empty when nothing went
wrong, which is the only way to tell a successful operation from a failed one.

processed.description:
How many entries the operation has handled so far, written as a decimal number in a string. It counts items,
not percent, and stays behind `progress` on operations that walk into subfolders.

finished.description:
Whether the operation has stopped running. A finished operation is reported once and then dropped, so the next
read of the operation list no longer contains it.

url.description:
The address the packed archive can be downloaded from once a bulk download has finished. Empty for every other
kind of operation.

items.description:
What every file and folder in an answer has in common; the concrete shape is a file or a folder, told apart by the
entry type.

files.description:
The files the operation produced or moved, in the order it wrote them down. Empty while nothing has been
written yet and for a deletion, which reports no entries at all.

items.description:
What every file and folder in an answer has in common; the concrete shape is a file or a folder, told apart by the
entry type.

folders.description:
The folders the operation produced or moved, in the order it wrote them down. Empty while nothing has been
written yet and for a deletion.

status.description:
The state of the background task behind the operation, which tells a task that was cancelled or that crashed
from one that ran to its end.

FileOperationDto.description: One background file operation of the caller, as it stood when the answer was built.

returnSingleOperation.description:
Which operations the answer carries: `true` returns the operation this call started and nothing else, `false`
returns every operation of the same kind that the caller has running or unread. When nothing was queued, which
happens for an empty selection, `true` falls back to the full list.

FileOperationRequestBaseDto.description: The parameter shared by every request that starts a background file operation.

fileKey.description: The id of the document inside the portal named below.

instanceId.description:
The portal the document lives in. A reference whose value is not this portal cannot be resolved by the file
key and falls back to the path or the link.

roomId.description:
The room the document lies in. It is filled in only for a document opened in a virtual data room, and stays
empty everywhere else.

canEditRoom.description: Whether the caller may manage the room named above; it is only meaningful together with it.

FileReferenceDataDto.description: The pair of values that names a document across portals, as it is written into a spreadsheet formula.

referenceData.description:
How this document is named when another spreadsheet refers to it. Send it back as it stands to resolve the
reference again.

error.description:
Filled in when the reference resolved to nothing; the rest of the descriptor is then empty and must not be
handed to the editors.

path.description: The title of the document the reference resolved to.

url.description:
Where the content is fetched from. It is addressed to the host the document service can reach, which on a
deployment with a private editor network is not the address a browser should follow.

fileType.description: The format the content is in, without the leading dot.

key.description:
Identifies the exact revision to the editors: two clients that receive the same key read the same co-editing
session, and the key changes as soon as the document is saved.

link.description:
The address of the document in the portal web editor - the link to put in front of a person, unlike the
download address above.

token.description:
Signs this descriptor so that the editors can trust it. It stays empty on a portal that has no signature
secret configured for the document service.

FileShare.description:
The level of access a subject has to a file, a folder or a room. The same scale is used by the sharing
operations, by the default sharing rights and by the access records of a room, and not every level is
meaningful everywhere - a room accepts the role-shaped levels, a single file the editing ones.
