access.description:
The level the subject holds on the entry. On a link entry it is the level the link hands to whoever opens it,
and in a batch answer `Varies` means the subject holds different levels on the listed entries.

sharedTo.description:
Deprecated: repeats whichever of `sharedToUser`, `sharedToGroup` and `sharedLink` is filled in, so its shape
changes from entry to entry. Read the three fields themselves instead.

sharedToUser.description:
The account the entry belongs to. It is filled in only when `subjectType` says an account, and is null for a
group entry and for a link.

sharedToGroup.description:
The portal group the entry belongs to, which hands the level to everybody in it. It is filled in only for a
group entry, and is null otherwise.

sharedLink.description:
The sharing link the entry stands for, together with everything set on it. It is filled in only for a link
entry, and is null for an account or a group.

isLocked.description:
Whether this entry is the caller's own, which is why they cannot change its level. Link entries never report
it.

isOwner.description: Whether the subject created the entry the access is given on, and so cannot be removed from it.

canEditAccess.description:
Whether the caller may change the level of this entry. It is false on the caller's own entry, on every link,
and whenever the caller may not hand out access at all.

canEditInternal.description:
Whether the caller may switch this link between being open to anybody and asking the visitor to sign in to the
portal first.

canEditDenyDownload.description:
Whether the caller may forbid downloading through this link. Only a link of a virtual data room reports true,
and only while the room itself still allows downloads.

canEditExpirationDate.description: Whether the caller may move the moment this link stops working.

canRevoke.description: Whether the caller may take this entry away altogether, which for a link means deleting the link.

subjectType.description:
What the entry was given to, which tells which of the three subject fields is filled in: an account, a group,
or one of the kinds of link.

FileShareDto.description:
One access entry on a file, a folder or a room: who holds it, at which level, and what the caller may change about
it.

id.description: The identifier of the link, the one to send back as `linkId` to change or delete it.

title.description: The name the link is listed under, which its author is free to choose and to leave empty.

shareLink.description:
The shortened address to hand out. Opening it is what turns the link into access; the address stays the same
while the link exists.

expirationDate.description:
The moment the link stops working, written with the offset of the portal time zone. Null when the link was
left without an end.

linkType.description:
Which of the two jobs the link does: letting somebody into the room as a member, or handing out the entry
itself. The counters of uses are filled in for the first kind only.

password.description:
The password a visitor has to send before the link resolves, readable only by those who may manage the link.
Empty when the link asks for none.

denyDownload.description: Whether visitors coming through this link may only read the entry in the editor and not download or print it.

isExpired.description:
Whether the moment in `expirationDate` has already passed, which leaves the link in place but refuses
everybody who opens it.

primary.description:
Whether this is the one link the entry always keeps: a public or a form-filling room is given it at creation,
and deleting it there only makes a new one.

internal.description:
Whether the visitor has to sign in to the portal before the link resolves, as opposed to it being open to
anybody who has the address.

requestToken.description:
The key that stands for this link in the calls that resolve it, such as `GET api/2.0/files/share/{key}`. It is
filled in for links that hand out the entry, and empty for the ones that invite into a room.

maxUseCount.description:
How many accounts may still join the room through this invitation link in total. Null on a link that hands out
the entry, where nothing is counted.

currentUseCount.description:
How many accounts have already joined through this invitation link. Once it reaches `maxUseCount` the link
stops letting anybody else in. Null on a link that hands out the entry.

FileShareLink.description: A sharing link of a file, a folder or a room, with everything set on it.

shareTo.description:
The account or the group the entry is about, taken from the portal people and group listings. Leave it out and
give an email address instead to share with somebody who has no account yet.

access.description:
What the subject may do with the shared item. The value 0 takes the access away again, and which of the other
levels are accepted depends on what is being shared.

FileShareParams.description: One sharing entry: an account, a group or an email address, and the access level it is given.

extsImagePreviewed.description: Images the portal can show in its own viewer. Anything outside the list has to be downloaded to be seen.

extsMediaPreviewed.description: Audio and video the portal can play in its own player.

extsWebPreviewed.description:
Documents the editor can open read-only. A format that is here but not in the edited list can be viewed and
not changed.

extsWebEdited.description:
Documents the editor can open for editing. Uploading a format outside this list and outside the convertible
list leaves a file that can only be downloaded.

extsWebEncrypt.description: Documents that can be edited inside a private room, where the content is encrypted on the client.

docServiceEncryptionSupported.description:
Whether the connected document server can edit end-to-end encrypted files. When false, an encrypted file cannot be
opened in the editors, whatever `extsWebEncrypt` lists.

extsWebReviewed.description: Documents that support the reviewing mode, so that granting review access to them is meaningful.

extsWebCustomFilterEditing.description:
Spreadsheets that support the custom filter mode, where a filter applied by one editor does not disturb the
others.

extsWebRestrictedEditing.description:
Documents that can only be filled in or commented on rather than edited freely, whatever access the caller
holds.

extsWebCommented.description: Documents that support comments, so that granting comment access to them is meaningful.

extsWebTemplate.description: Documents the portal treats as templates to create new files from.

extsMustConvert.description:
Formats that cannot be edited as they are and are converted on upload or on first opening. Which target each
one has is in the convertible table below.

extsConvertible.description:
The conversion map of the portal: for each source extension, the extensions it can be converted into. Use it
to fill the target format of a conversion request instead of guessing one.

extsUploadable.description:
Formats the portal offers to create and upload as documents. It is not an upload filter: files of other
formats are stored as they are.

extsArchive.description: Formats recognised as archives, which is what decides the archive icon and the offer to unpack.

extsVideo.description:
Formats classified as video. The classification lists drive icons and the media filters of the listing
operations, and are wider than what the built-in player can show.

internalFormats.description:
The extension the portal creates for each kind of document, keyed by that kind. This is what a new empty
document gets when no extension is asked for.

masterFormExtension.description:
The extension of a fillable form template in this portal. It is configurable, so read it rather than assuming
the product default.

paramVersion.description:
The name of the query parameter that pins a document address to one version. Append it to the addresses below
instead of composing a version address by hand.

paramOutType.description: The name of the query parameter that asks a download address for a converted copy in another format.

fileDownloadUrlString.description:
The template of the address a file is downloaded from: substitute the file identifier for the `{0}`
placeholder. Add the version and output-type parameters named above for a particular version or format.

fileWebViewerUrlString.description:
The template of the address that opens a file in the viewer inside the portal, with `{0}` for the file
identifier. It is a portal-relative address, meant to be opened in a browser rather than called as an API.

fileWebViewerExternalUrlString.description: The same viewer address as an absolute one, for a message or a page outside the portal.

fileWebEditorUrlString.description:
The template of the address that opens a file for editing inside the portal, with `{0}` for the file
identifier. Whether the session really becomes editable still depends on the access the caller holds.

fileWebEditorExternalUrlString.description: The same editing address as an absolute one, for use outside the portal.

fileRedirectPreviewUrlString.description:
The template of the address that sends the browser on to whichever viewer or editor suits the file, with `{0}`
for the file identifier. Use it when the kind of the file is not known in advance.

fileThumbnailUrlString.description:
The template of the address a file thumbnail is fetched from, with `{0}` for the file identifier. A thumbnail
is built in the background, so the address can answer with nothing for a while after the file appears.

confirmDelete.description: Whether the caller asked to be prompted before a deletion. Written by `PUT api/2.0/files/changedeleteconfrim`.

enableThirdParty.description:
Whether this portal allows third-party storages to be connected at all. It is set portal-wide by an
administrator, so a member sees it as read-only.

externalShare.description:
Whether links that open an entry without a portal account may be created in this portal. Set portal-wide by an
administrator.

externalShareSocialMedia.description:
Whether the share-to-network buttons are offered next to an external link. It is reported as false whenever
external sharing itself is off.

storeOriginalFiles.description:
Whether the caller's uploads keep the original file when the portal converts them. With false the conversion
replaces the uploaded file with a new version of it.

keepNewFileName.description:
Whether the caller asked for new documents to be created with the default name instead of being prompted for
one.

displayFileExtension.description:
Whether the caller asked to see extensions in file titles. Stored titles always carry the extension whatever
this says.

showQuickActions.description: Specifies whether to display the quick action buttons.

convertNotify.description:
Whether the caller is told about the result of a conversion. There is no operation in this document that
writes it.

hideConfirmCancelOperation.description: Whether the prompt shown before a running operation is abandoned is hidden for the caller.

hideConfirmConvertSave.description:
Whether the prompt that offers to keep a copy in the original format on conversion is hidden for the caller.
Once true it cannot be turned back through the API.

hideConfirmConvertOpen.description:
Whether the prompt that offers to open the conversion result is hidden for the caller. Once true it cannot be
turned back through the API.

hideConfirmRoomLifetime.description: Whether the warning shown before the lifetime settings of a room are changed is hidden for the caller.

defaultOrder.description:
The ordering the listing operations fall back to when a request names none. It follows the last order the
caller asked a listing for, so it changes on its own as the account is used.

forcesave.description:
Whether the editor writes a document back to storage while the session is still open. It is on for every
portal and cannot be switched off.

storeForcesave.description:
Whether those intermediate saves are kept as separate versions. They are not, in any portal: they update the
current version instead.

recentSection.description: Whether the "Recent" section is offered to the caller among the section roots.

favoritesSection.description: Whether the "Favorites" section is offered to the caller among the section roots.

templatesSection.description: Whether the "Templates" section is offered to the caller among the section roots.

downloadTarGz.description: The archive format the caller's multi-item downloads are packed into: true for `.tar.gz`, false for `.zip`.

automaticallyCleanUp.description: The trash auto-clearing setting of the caller, the same pair `GET api/2.0/files/settings/autocleanup` returns.

canSearchByContent.description:
Whether documents in this portal can be searched by what is inside them and not only by title. It depends on
the full-text search service being configured and having indexed the portal.

defaultSharingAccessRights.description:
The access rights the sharing dialog offers the caller by default. The portal normalises the set it stores, so
this can be shorter than what was last sent.

maxUploadThreadCount.description:
How many upload requests the portal accepts from one account at a time. Sending more than this in parallel
gets the extra ones refused rather than queued.

chunkUploadSize.description:
The size in bytes of one chunk of a chunked upload. Split a large file exactly along this size: a chunk that
does not match is refused by the upload session.

openEditorInSameTab.description: Whether the caller asked for documents to open in the current browser tab.

organizeRoomsGrouping.description: Whether the caller asked to see rooms arranged by the groups they belong to.

defaultShareLinkInternal.description:
The kind of external link this portal offers first: true for a link only its own accounts can open, false for
one anyone holding it can open.

externalShareApplyToDocuments.description:
Whether the external sharing restriction covers personal documents. It matters only while external sharing is
off.

externalShareApplyToRooms.description:
Whether the external sharing restriction covers rooms, including making a new one public. It matters only
while external sharing is off.

blockExistingLinksOnRestrict.description: Whether links created before the restriction stop opening as well, rather than only new ones being refused.

extsFilesVectorized.description:
Formats whose content can be indexed for the AI features of the portal. A file outside the list is left out of
that index.

maxVectorizationFileSize.description:
The largest file size in bytes that is indexed for the AI features. A larger file is skipped even when its
format is listed above.

FilesSettingsDto.description:
Everything a client needs to work with documents in this portal: the format tables, the address templates, the
upload limits, the portal-wide switches and the preferences of the calling account.

title.description:
The name of the section as the interface shows it, translated into the language used by the caller, so it
suits display but not matching - which section an entry describes is told by the field that carries it.

usedSpace.description:
The size of the files kept in the section, in bytes, counting every folder and room inside it; 0 means the
section holds nothing. The counter is brought up to date as an operation finishes, so a reading taken right
after an upload or a delete can still show the previous value.

FilesStatisticsFolder.description: One section of the portal and the space its documents take.

myDocumentsUsedSpace.description:
The space taken by the personal "Files" sections of all accounts of the portal added together. An item deleted
to the trash keeps taking space and is counted in `trashUsedSpace` until the trash is emptied.

trashUsedSpace.description:
The space held by the items deleted to the trash from any section, which is given back only when the trash is
emptied or the items are erased for good.

archiveUsedSpace.description:
The space taken by the content of the archived rooms, the archived form filling rooms included. Restoring a
room moves its space back to `roomsUsedSpace` or `formsUsedSpace`.

roomsUsedSpace.description:
The space taken by the content of the active rooms, except the form filling rooms, whose content is reported
in `formsUsedSpace`. Archiving a room moves its space to `archiveUsedSpace`.

aiAgentsUsedSpace.description:
The space taken by the content of the "AI agents" section, which exists only in a portal where the AI agents
feature is active; creating an AI room is not enough to bring the section into being.

formsUsedSpace.description:
The space taken by the content of the active form filling rooms, which is kept apart from `roomsUsedSpace`
even though those rooms are listed among the rooms.

FilesStatisticsResultDto.description:
The space that stored documents take in each section of the portal, in bytes. The figures cover every account of
the portal rather than the caller alone, and a section the portal does not have comes back as null instead of a
zero figure.

completedForm.description:

operations of this API.

originalForm.description: The form the copy was made from, so that a client can offer filling it once more.

manager.description:
The account that owns the original form, reported with its email address, so that the person who has just
filled the form knows who receives it and whom to ask about it.

roomId.description:
The room the form was filled in. It comes back as 0 when the session was reached through a link shared for
that single form rather than for its room, in which case there is no room the caller could be sent to.

isRoomMember.description:
Tells whether the calling account may open that room: true for a member of the room and for a portal
administrator, in which case a client can offer going to the room; false for the anonymous caller who filled
the form through a link and can only be shown the copy itself.

items.description:
What every file and folder in an answer has in common; the concrete shape is a file or a folder, told apart by the
entry type.

files.description:
The file entries of this page. It is empty when the folder holds no files, when the filters matched none of
them, and in the sections that list rooms only.

items.description:
What every file and folder in an answer has in common; the concrete shape is a file or a folder, told apart by the
entry type.

folders.description:
The folder entries of this page. In a section of rooms these entries are the rooms themselves, which is where
their type, tags, logo and quota are read from.

current.description:
The folder or section the page was read from, with its own title, type and access rights. It describes the
container, not the entries, and is filled in even when the page is empty.

pathParts.description:
The breadcrumbs of the current folder, ordered from the root of the section down to it. Each element carries
the identifier, the title and the folder and room types, and folders the caller cannot read are left out, so
the chain can be shorter than the real depth.

startIndex.description:
The position of the first entry of this page in the whole result, echoing the requested start index. Add the
number of entries received to it to ask for the next page.

count.description:
How many entries this page carries, files and folders together. A page shorter than the requested size means
the result is exhausted.

total.description:
How many entries matched before paging was applied, across the whole folder. Page until the start index plus
the entries received reaches it.

new.description:
How many entries of this folder are marked as new for the caller. It is 0 for every listing when the account
has switched the new-item badges off, so a zero here does not prove that nothing has changed.

FolderContentDto.description:
One page of the contents of a folder or of a section: its entries split into files and folders, the folder itself,
and the counters needed to page through the rest.

parentId.description:
The folder this one is listed in. For a room it is the root of the section the room lives in, and for an entry
opened through a sharing link whose real parent the caller may not read it is the root of the section with the
entries shared with them.

filesCount.description:
How many files lie directly in the folder, without counting the subfolders. The roots of the `Rooms`, room
templates, default templates and AI agents sections always report 0, because the number is not collected for
them.

foldersCount.description:
How many subfolders lie directly in the folder. For an AI room the two service subfolders it always holds are
subtracted, so the number matches what a listing of it shows, and the roots of the `Rooms`, templates and AI
agents sections report 0.

isShareable.description:
Whether the caller may hand out access to the folder. It is filled in only for the folder a folder-contents
answer is about, and is null in every other answer, so null says nothing about the sharing rights.

new.description:
How many entries inside the folder the caller has not opened yet, the number drawn as the badge on it. An
account that turned the badges off in its own settings always reads 0 here, so 0 alone does not prove that
everything has been seen.

mute.description:
Whether the caller silenced the notifications of this room: true means no message about its activity reaches
them. The choice belongs to the reading account rather than to the room, so two members of one room read
different values.

tags.description:
The names of the tags attached to the room. Empty for a folder that is not a room, since only rooms carry
tags, and the names are the ones from the portal tag catalogue.

logo.description:
The addresses of the room logo in four sizes, together with the colour and the built-in cover that are drawn
when no logo was uploaded. A room without a logo answers with four empty addresses rather than with null, and
the field is null for a folder that is not a room.

pinned.description:
Whether the caller pinned the room to the top of their own room list. Pinning is personal and is lost when the
room is archived.

roomType.description:
The kind of the room, which decides the default access rules of its members. Null for a folder that is not a
room.

private.description:
Whether the room is a private one, which limits it to the accounts invited into it and needs encryption keys
set up for each of them.

indexing.description:
Whether the contents of the room are kept in an explicit numbered order, the one reported as `order` on each
entry, instead of being left to the sorting the reader asks for.

denyDownload.description:
Whether downloading and printing the contents of the room is forbidden, which leaves its members with viewing
and editing in the editor.

lifetime.description:
The rule by which the files of the room are removed once they grow old. Null when the room has no such rule,
which is also what is reported after the rule is switched off, because switching it off erases it.

watermark.description:
The watermark stamped over the documents of the room while they are viewed and printed. Null when the room has
no watermark, and for every folder that is not a room.

type.description:
The part the folder plays inside its room: one of the service folders of the form-filling flow, or the
knowledge and result storages of an AI room. It stays null for an ordinary folder and for the room itself, so
it does not describe folders in general.

inRoom.description:
Whether the caller holds the room through an invitation of their own: true for the account that created it and
for a member invited personally, false when the access comes from a group they belong to, and null for a
folder that is not a room.

quotaLimit.description:
How much space the files of the room may take, in bytes. It is the limit set on this room, or the portal
default for rooms when none was set. Null when the tariff of the portal does not count room statistics, when
room quotas are switched off, when the room lies in the archive or the trash, or when the role of the caller
in the room carries no editing rights - a viewer, a commenter, a reviewer and a form filler do not see the
figure, a room manager, a content creator and an editor do.

isCustomQuota.description:
Whether `quotaLimit` is a limit set on this room (true) or the portal default for rooms (false). Null exactly
when `quotaLimit` is null.

usedSpace.description:
How much the files of the room take, in bytes, as of the last time the counter was recomputed. The counter is
refreshed when a file operation finishes, so a read right after an upload or a deletion can still report the
previous figure. Null for a folder that is not a room.

passwordProtected.description:
Whether the sharing link the folder was opened through asks for a password that has not been entered yet.
While it is true the contents stay unreadable; send the password to `POST api/2.0/files/share/{key}/password`
first. Null when the folder was not reached through a link.

expired.description:
Deprecated, read `isLinkExpired` instead: whether the sharing link the folder was opened through has run out
of its lifetime.

chatSettings.description:
The chat configuration of an AI room. Only the system prompt is reported here, whatever else the room stores,
and the field is null for every folder that is not an AI room.

rootRoomType.description:
The kind of the room the folder lies in. It is filled in only for the folder a folder-contents answer is
about, and only when that room is an AI room, so it is null in every other answer and for every other room
kind.

saveFormAsXLSX.description:
Whether the answers collected in this form-filling room are also gathered into a spreadsheet next to the
completed copies. Filled in for form-filling rooms only.

sendFormToExternalDB.description:
Whether the answers collected in this form-filling room are also pushed into the external database configured
for the portal. Filled in for form-filling rooms only.

originalFormId.description:
The form the completed copies in this folder were filled from, taken from the copy submitted last. Null while
the folder holds no completed copy, and for every folder that does not collect them.

FolderDto.description: The folder, with the fields that only a room carries filled in when the folder is a room.

linkId.description:
Which link the request addresses: the identifier of an existing link rewrites that link, while an identifier
that is not in use, the empty one included, creates a new link. Take an existing identifier from
`GET api/2.0/files/folder/{id}/links`.

access.description:
The rights a visitor following the link is given. The value that grants nothing revokes the link instead of
setting it, and the answer is then empty.

expirationDate.description:
The moment the link stops working, sent as an ISO-8601 stamp. A moment that lies in the past is ignored,
and leaving the field out gives the link no expiry.

title.description:
The name the link is listed under for the people who manage the folder; a visitor following it never sees the
name.

password.description:
The secret a visitor has to enter before the link opens. Leave it out for a link that opens without one; the
secret itself is never given back, only the fact that one is set.

denyDownload.description:
Whether visitors are left with viewing alone: with true downloading and copying through the link are blocked,
with false they are allowed.

internal.description:
Whether the link admits signed-in portal members only: with true a visitor has to sign in before the link
opens, with false anyone holding the address may follow it.

primary.description:
Whether this link becomes the primary link of the folder, the one the "Copy link" action of a client hands
out; a folder has one primary link at a time.

FolderLinkRequest.description: The external link of a folder, as it is to be created or rewritten.

metadataTemplateId.description:
The ID of the metadata template the entries must be assigned to. On its own it narrows the listing to the entries
carrying the template; together with the conditions it also pins the template the filtered fields belong to.

items.description:
One metadata filter condition as the clients send it: an element of the "metadataFilters" JSON of the listings and of
the body of the search endpoints. All conditions are combined with AND.

metadataFilters.description: The metadata filter conditions, combined with AND. A custom field is addressed by its name instead of the field ID.

includeHiddenMetadata.description:
Whether the text search, and the "metadataMatches" it reports, also look at the values of the hidden metadata
templates (created with "visible" false for the metadata a service keeps for itself, which the web client never
shows). False, the default, leaves them out, so an entry is not found by such a value; true takes them in.
"metadataTemplateId" and "metadataFilters" are not concerned: a hidden template or field named there is searched
either way.

filterValue.description:
The text to search for in the titles and in the string metadata values of the entries, the custom fields and the
template fields alike; an entry found by its metadata says where in "metadataMatches".

withSubFolders.description: Specifies whether to search the whole subtree of the folder (the default) or its direct children only.

count.description: The number of entries to return, from 1 to 100.

startIndex.description: The zero-based index of the first entry to return.

sortBy.description: The field to sort by, a name of the SortedByType values.

FolderMetadataSearch.description:
The typed form of the metadata search of a folder: the same filter the folder listing takes in the "metadataTemplateId"
and "metadataFilters" query parameters, with the conditions as objects instead of a JSON string.

the moment the form itself was made.

carries the number of the copy and is what the submissions are ordered by. Fields holding a picture or a
signature are left out of the record, so a field missing here was not necessarily left blank.

roleName.description:
The name the role was given when the form was laid out, unique within that form. It is the value that names
the role in the calls which change or stop the filling.

roleColor.description:
The colour a client paints the role with, as a hexadecimal RGB value; empty when the role mapping assigned
none.

user.description: The account the role was assigned to, which is the person expected to fill this part of the form.

sequence.description:
The turn this role takes: the roles come back ordered by this number, roles sharing a number are filled in
parallel, and a role with a higher number waits until every lower one has been submitted.

submitted.description:
Reports whether this role has already handed in its part. The lowest sequence number that still holds an
unsubmitted role is the turn the form as a whole is waiting on.

stopedBy.description:
The account that interrupted the filling. It is filled in on the one role the filling was stopped at and stays
empty on every other role, and on all of them while the filling runs normally.

history.description:
When the role passed through the stages of its turn, keyed by stage: 0 is the moment the form was opened for
it, 1 the moment it was submitted and 2 the moment the filling was stopped at it. The times are given in the
time zone of the portal, and only the stages that have actually happened are present, so an empty object means
the role has not been opened yet.

roleStatus.description:
Where the role stands in the queue: roles of earlier turns are reported as complete, roles of later turns as a
draft, and the role whose turn it is as either yours to fill or in progress, depending on whether that person
has already opened the form. The role the filling was stopped at is reported as stopped whatever its turn.

FormRoleDto.description: One role of a PDF form, with the state the turn of that role is in.

roomId.description: The ID of the room the form is in. It is stored with the role as sent, so pass the room the form lives in.

roleName.description: The name of a role the form defines, such as the one the form author gave a group of fields.

roleColor.description: The color the editor marks the fields of this role with, as a hex code.

userId.description: The account that fills this role. It is notified once filling starts, unless it is the caller.

sequence.description: Accepted for compatibility and ignored: the position of the role in the list sets the filling order.

submitted.description: Whether this role counts as already submitted. It is stored as sent; send false when filling starts.

openedAt.description: Accepted for compatibility and ignored: the portal records when the role is opened.

submissionDate.description: Accepted for compatibility and ignored: the portal records when the role is submitted.

FormRoleRequest.description: One role of a form and the account that fills it.

items.description: The metadata of a single form field.

metadata.description:
Describes the fields of the form version that is being filled - the key each value is stored under, the type
and format of the field and, where the field offers a fixed set of answers, those answers - in the order the
fields are laid out, which is the order to build a results table in. It comes back empty when the portal holds
no indexed description of that version.

items.description: One completed copy of a form, with the values that were entered into it.

submissions.description:
One entry per completed copy, ordered by the copy number that `formsData` carries. An empty list means nothing
has been completed for the version that is currently being filled; the copies of earlier versions of the form
are not reported here, only in the spreadsheet report.

fileKey.description:
The id of the referenced file as the document service recorded it in the formula. It is tried first, and only
when `instanceId` names this portal.

instanceId.description:
The portal the reference was made on, as the document service recorded it. Only the id of this portal makes
the file key resolvable; any other value falls through to the path and the link.

sourceFileId.description:
The spreadsheet the formula sits in. The path is resolved against it - the referenced file is looked for among
the files lying next to it - and it is the file whose read access is checked.

path.description:
The title of the referenced file exactly as the formula spells it, matched against the files lying next to the
source file. It is tried after the file key, and only when no link is given.

link.description:
The web address the formula points at, an editor link of this portal or one of its short links. It is tried
last, and an address belonging to another site is not resolved at all but handed back for the client to follow
as it is.

GetReferenceDataDto.description:
The body of a spreadsheet reference request: the source spreadsheet, and the three ways of naming the document it
refers to, which are tried in the order they are described.

url.description:
Where the user is taken when they leave the document, normally the folder or the room it lies in. It is empty
when there is nowhere to return to, as in a framed opening.

GobackConfigDto.description: The settings for the "Open file location" menu button and upper right corner button.

count.description: How many items this response carries: the length of the page for a list, 1 for a single object

total.description: How many items the whole list holds across all pages, for working out how many pages to request. Sent only by the operations that page their results, and left out of every other response

links.description: List of links related to the response

status.description: HTTP status code of the response

statusCode.description: HTTP status code of the response (duplicate of status)

GroupMemberSecurityArrayWrapper.description: The successful API response containing the list of GroupMemberSecurityDto objects.

user.description:
The member the line is about, as the portal reports the account: the display name, the avatar and the portal
role to show next to the access level.

groupAccess.description:
The level granted to the group as a whole on this file or folder. It belongs to the group record rather than
to the member, so the same value repeats on every line of the answer; a group whose record was set back to
none is answered with an empty list instead.

userAccess.description:
The level granted to this member alone on the same file or folder, or `null` when the member has no record of
their own and the group level is what applies. The member who created the file or folder is always reported
here as a room manager, whatever their own record says.

overridden.description:
Whether `userAccess` is the level that decides what the member may do. When it is false the member inherits
`groupAccess`, and the creator of the file or folder is always reported as overridden because of the room
manager level forced onto them.

canEditAccess.description:
Whether the caller may still change the level of this member. It comes back false on the line of the member
who created the file or folder, on the line of the caller themselves, and on every line at once when the
caller may read the file or folder but not manage access to it.

owner.description:
Whether this member created the file or folder - the owner of the entry, not the owner of the group. Their
level is reported as a room manager one and cannot be taken away through this group.

GroupMemberSecurityDto.description:
One member of a portal group together with the access that member has on the file or folder the group was granted
rights to. Every line of the answer describes the same file or folder and differs only in the member and in the
level that applies to them.

id.description: The group ID.

isSystem.description: Indicates whether the group is a system group.

save.description:
Chooses the prompt to hide rather than the state to store: true hides the prompt that offers to keep a copy in
the original format when a document is converted, false hides the prompt that offers to open the conversion
result. Each of the two flags is stored separately for the calling account, and both are one-way - the portal
can hide a prompt but has no way to show it again.

HideConfirmConvertRequestDto.description: The body of the conversion prompt switch: which of the two prompts to hide.

id.description: The action performed on the file.

key.description: The same action as a camel-case key, for a client to look up its own wording by.

initiatorName.description: The name of the action initiator.

id.description:
The identifier of the record, which tells two records of the same action apart and stays stable as long as the
portal keeps the log.

action.description:
What happened - the kind of event the record stands for, such as a file being uploaded, renamed, moved or
shared - with the key a client can key its own wording off.

initiator.description:
Who caused the event. For an event caused by a visitor following an external link only the name they gave is
filled in, the account fields staying empty.

date.description: When the event happened, written with the offset of the portal's time zone.

data.description:
The history data. Absent for actions that carry no payload of their own - changing a room's
logo, icon colour or cover, whose interpreter returns no data (see
`RoomLogoChangedInterpreter`). It used to be declared required, which put it in the
OpenAPI document's required list while the null-dropping serializer left it out of the
response, so a generated client threw on any history page holding one of those entries.

items.description: One record of the activity log of a file or a folder.

related.description:
The records folded into this one because they belong to the same action, the separate files of one upload for
instance. It is empty when the record stands alone, and the records inside it carry no further nesting.

HistoryDto.description: One record of the activity log of a file or a folder.

ICompress.description:
The archive writer that packs a multi-item download. It is published as an object without fields: the selected
format is read from the file settings, not from this object.

icon.description:
The identifier of one of the built-in covers listed by `GET api/2.0/files/rooms/covers`. An empty string
clears the icon of the group, null or a missing member keeps the current one, and anything else is refused.

IconRequest.description: The icon to set on a room group.

height.description: The height of the image in pixels, read from the stored file rather than from any display setting.

width.description: The width of the image in pixels, read from the stored file rather than from any display setting.

ImageSizeDto.description: A pixel size measured on the image itself.

favorite.description:
Whether the caller has this document among their favorites. It is empty when favorites do not apply - for an
anonymous caller, for a guest, and for an encrypted document.

folder.description:
The place of the document as a readable path, its folders joined from the root downwards. It is empty in the
embedded layout, which shows no such panel.

owner.description: The display name of the owner of the document. It is empty for an anonymous session.

items.description:
One line of a document sharing list in display form: who the document is shared with and the label of their access
level, rather than an access record with identifiers. Entries that deny access and invitation links are left out,
so the list names only the subjects and links that can currently open the document.

sharingSettings.description:
Who the document is shared with, as the information panel lists it. An empty list means it is shared with
nobody beyond its owner.

type.description: The layout the information panel is rendered for.

uploaded.description:
When the document was created on the portal, already formatted for reading in the culture of the caller rather
than as a machine timestamp.

InfoConfigDto.description: The facts the editor information panel shows about the open document.

key.description:
The left half of the pair. Where the pair configures something, this is the identifier the value belongs to -
a setting name, a module id, a logo slot; where the pair reports the result of a call, this is the result
itself, such as the flag telling whether the call succeeded. Which of the two it is, and which keys are
accepted, is stated by the operation that sends or returns the pair.

value.description:
The right half of the pair: what is assigned to the key next to it, or what is reported for it. Its meaning
and its accepted values follow from the key, so read them from the operation that sends or returns the pair.

ItemKeyValuePairBooleanString.description:
One entry of a keyed collection, carried as an explicit pair of `key` and `value` fields instead of as a member
of a JSON object, so that the key is not restricted to a string and the entries keep the order they are sent in.

response.description: The ItemKeyValuePairBooleanString object returned by the operation.

[0 - Invitation, 1 - External]

LinkType.description: The job a sharing link does.

lockFile.description:
The state to reach: `true` locks the file, which blocks editing, renaming and deleting for everybody but the
account that locked it and the room admins, and drops the others out of a running editing session; `false`
releases the lock.

LockFileRequest.description: The lock state a file is to be put into.

image.description: The logo for the current layout and file type, as the portal branding defines it.

imageDark.description: The variant for a dark interface theme.

imageLight.description: The variant for a light interface theme.

imageEmbedded.description: The variant for the framed viewer. It is empty in every layout but the embedded one.

url.description: Where clicking the logo takes the user.

visible.description: Whether the logo is shown at all; the mobile layout hides it.

LogoConfigDto.description: The logo the editor shows, resolved for the file type and the layout of this opening.

id.description: The logo cover ID.

tmpFile.description:
The picture to cut the logo out of, named by the path that `POST api/2.0/files/logos` returned for it. The
path may be used once and only by the account that uploaded it.

x.description:
The left edge of the rectangle cut out of the uploaded picture, counted in pixels from its left side. The
picture itself was already scaled down to fit 1280 by 1280 pixels when it was uploaded.

y.description: The top edge of the rectangle cut out of the uploaded picture, counted in pixels from its top.

width.description:
How wide a piece of the uploaded picture to cut out, in pixels. It has to be sent together with the height,
and the portal builds the four logo sizes out of the piece.

height.description: How tall a piece of the uploaded picture to cut out, in pixels. It has to be sent together with the width.

LogoRequest.description: The part of an uploaded picture to use as the logo.

formId.description:
The PDF form the action applies to. This is the value the operation reads, rather than the identifier in its
route, and the two are to be sent the same.

user.description: The account itself, as the portal stores it.

email.description: Where a mention notification for this user is delivered.

id.description:
The account id as text, the same value the account object carries; it is what identifies the user in a sharing
request built from this list.

image.description:
An absolute address of the medium-sized avatar. A generated default avatar is reported when the user never
uploaded one, so the field is never empty.

hasAccess.description:
Not filled in by the operations that return this list: it always comes back false. Whether a user can already
open the document has to be read from the sharing settings of the file.

name.description: The name to display, assembled the way the portal is configured to show names.

MentionDto.description:
A portal member the editor can offer when the author types a mention: who they are, where the notification goes
and how to show them in the suggestion list.

actionLink.description:
The place in the document the notification link should open at, as the editor reports it when the mention is
made. Left out, the link opens the file at its beginning.

emails.description:
The addresses to notify. Only an address that belongs to a portal account receives a mail; an unknown address
is skipped, and the answer then carries the access list of the file so that the client can invite its owner.

message.description:
The note shown next to the link in the mail. Only its first 200 characters are sent, and a value longer than
the field allows is refused.

fieldId.description: The ID of the template field the condition is on. A custom field is addressed by ASC.Files.Core.MetadataFilterConditionRequest.Name instead.

name.description:
The name of a custom field, for the conditions on the custom fields, which have no identifier outside. Either the
field ID or the name is given; the name is matched without regard to case.

op.description:
The operator, one of ASC.Files.Core.MetadataFilterOperators: "eq" or "contains" for a string field, "eq", "range",
"gt", "gte", "lt" or "lte" for a number field, "range", "gt", "gte", "lt" or "lte" for a date field, "in" for a
choice field. Optional: an omitted operator is read as "eq" for a string, as "range" for a date, as "in" for a
choice, and for a number as "eq" when a value is given or as "range" when a bound is. A present one has to belong
to the field type and to the arguments: "eq" takes a value, "range" takes bounds.

value.description:
The value of a single-valued condition: the whole or a part of a string field, the exact value of a number field,
or the bound of a "gt", "gte", "lt" or "lte" condition on a number or a date field. A JSON number is accepted as
well as a string. A number is a whole number of at most 2^53-1 in magnitude, the limit of a stored number value.
A date given without a time ("2026-06-30") names the whole day (UTC).

from.description:
The inclusive lower bound of a range. A number is a whole number of at most 2^53-1 in magnitude, the limit of a
stored number value. A date given without a time ("2026-06-01") is the start of that day (UTC).

to.description:
The inclusive upper bound of a range. A number is a whole number of at most 2^53-1 in magnitude, the limit of a
stored number value. A date given without a time ("2026-06-30") covers the whole day (UTC); a value with a time
is an instant and is taken as is.

optionIds.description: The options any of which the choice field must hold.

reviewDisplay.description:
How the editors render tracked changes at first: with the markup, in a simplified markup, as the final text,

deletePermanently.description:
Decides what happens to a file that has grown too old: it is erased outright, or it is moved to the trash of
the account that created the room, from where it can still be brought back.

period.description:
The unit the age is counted in. Months and years are counted as calendar ones, so the same number of them
covers a different number of days depending on when the clean-up runs.

value.description:
How many periods a file may stay in the room, counted from the moment it was last changed rather than from the
moment the rule was set. Files that are already older than this are removed by the next clean-up.

enabled.description:
Switches the rule on and off. Switching it off erases the rule instead of keeping it aside, so afterwards the
room reports no rule at all and the other three values have to be sent again to bring it back.

RoomDataLifetimeDto.description: The rule by which the files of a room are removed once they have been lying in it for too long.

roomId.description:
The room the job is creating. It is meaningful once the room exists, which is guaranteed only after
`isCompleted` turns true and `error` stays empty; until then it carries no usable id.

progress.description:
How far the job has got. The value climbs while the contents of the template are being copied into the new
room and reaches its maximum at the very end.

error.description:
Why the job stopped. It is empty while the job runs and after a successful one, and a filled value means that
no room was created, so the request has to be repeated rather than waited out.

isCompleted.description:
Whether the job has ended. It is set both after a successful creation and after a failure, so it is the flag
to poll for, while `error` is what separates the two outcomes.

id.description:
The identifier of the group, which addresses it in every other group operation and is kept for as long as the
group exists.

name.description:
The name its owner gave the group, stored trimmed of surrounding spaces. Names are not unique, so two groups
of the same account can be told apart only by their identifier.

icon.description:
The built-in cover chosen for the group, carrying the cover identifier and its rendering in each available
size. Null when the group has no icon, either because it was never given one or because the icon was cleared
by setting it to an empty value.

userId.description:
The account that created the group and the only one able to read, change or delete it; for any other member of
the portal the group does not exist.

searchArea.description:
The section the group belongs to, which categorizes it within the application's structure. This property determines
which area of the interface the group is associated with and affects how its rooms are filtered and displayed.
Common values include Active for standard rooms, Forms for form-based rooms, Archive for archived content, and
Templates for template rooms. The search area ensures that when retrieving a group, only rooms that belong to
the specified section are included in the results, maintaining proper organizational boundaries within the system.

items.description:
What every file and folder in an answer has in common; the concrete shape is a file or a folder, told apart by the
entry type.

rooms.description:
The rooms the group gathers, those stored in the portal first and those on connected third-party accounts
after them. Null when the group was asked for without its members, and an empty array when the group holds no
room the caller can still see. A room moved to the archive is left out until it is taken out of the archive.

totalRooms.description:
How many rooms the group shows: the same rooms `rooms` lists, so archived ones are not counted either. It is
filled even when the rooms themselves were not asked for, which makes it the cheap way to tell an empty group
from a populated one.

RoomGroupDto.description:
A personal collection of rooms: the name and icon it was given, the account that owns it, and the rooms it gathers
at the moment it was read.

name.description:
The name to show the group under. Surrounding spaces are trimmed before it is stored, a name that is blank
once trimmed is refused, and the name does not have to differ from the names of the caller's other groups.

icon.description:
The icon of the group, given as the identifier of one of the built-in covers listed by
`GET api/2.0/files/rooms/covers`. An uploaded image cannot be used, and any value that is not one of those
identifiers is refused.

rooms.description:
The rooms to gather in the group, each given as a number for a room stored in the portal or as a string for a
room on a connected third-party account. Every identifier has to name a room the caller can read; repeats are
collapsed, and an element of any other shape - a decimal number, a number sent as a string, null - is refused.

searchArea.description: The section the group belongs to: Active for Rooms and Forms for Forms. Active when omitted.

id.description:
The account or the group the entry is about, taken from the portal people and group listings. Leave it out and
give an email address instead to invite somebody who has no account yet.

access.description:
What the subject may do in the room. The value 0 removes the subject from the room, and the levels on offer
depend on the kind of room.

RoomInvitation.description: One membership change in a room: an account or an email address, and the access level it is given.

items.description: One membership change in a room: an account or an email address, and the access level it is given.

invitations.description:
Who is added, changed or removed, one entry per subject. The same subject named twice keeps the level of the
last entry, and an empty list is accepted and changes nothing.

notify.description:
Whether the subjects that gained access are told about it by email. With it off the change is silent, which is
the usual choice when membership is synchronised from another system.

examples: Please review the contract by Friday
message.description:
The line added to the invitation email. It is used only while the notification is on, and it reaches nobody
whose access was removed.

culture.description:
The language of the invitation email, as a portal culture name such as en-US. Leaving it out sends each
message in the language of its recipient.

force.description:
Whether a member who still holds a role in an unfinished form is removed anyway. With it off such a removal is
refused and reported through the error of the answer, so the form can be reassigned first.

RoomInvitationRequest.description: One batch of membership changes for a room.

linkId.description:
Which link to change, taken from `GET api/2.0/files/rooms/{id}/links`. Leaving it out creates a link, and an
identifier the room does not know creates a link carrying that identifier.

access.description:
What whoever opens the link may do in the room. The value 0 revokes the link instead of changing it, and the
levels a room accepts depend on its kind.

expirationDate.description:
When the link stops working, written with the offset of the portal time zone. A date already past is dropped
silently for an external link and refused for an invitation link, and a date further ahead than the portal
allows is refused as well; leaving it out means the link does not expire.

internal.description:
Whether the external link works only for people already signed in to the portal. With it off the link opens
the room for anyone who has the address, subject to the password.

title.description:
The name the link is shown under in the room. An empty value is accepted and the portal names the link itself,
so the answer is what tells the caller the name in use.

linkType.description:
Which kind of link to create: an invitation link makes whoever opens it a member of the room, while an
external link opens the room without an account. It is fixed when the link is created and is ignored on later
changes.

password.description:
The password an external link asks for before it opens the room. An empty value leaves the link open to anyone
who has the address, and the password is never returned when links are listed.

denyDownload.description:
Whether people arriving through the link are stopped from downloading and printing what they open. They can
still read the documents in the editor.

maxUseCount.description:
How many people an invitation link may still let in before it stops working. A value below the number of
people who already used it is refused, and leaving it out puts no ceiling on the link.

currentUseCount.description:
How many people have already joined through this invitation link. The value is kept by the portal: it is
reported back when links are listed and anything sent here is ignored.

One access entry on a file, a folder or a room: who holds it, at which level, and what the caller may change about

members.description:
The access entries of the subjects named in the request, read back after the change was applied. A subject the
caller may not see is missing from it, so comparing this list with the request is the way to learn who was
skipped; it is null when nothing was applied at all.

examples: The maximum number of links is 10
warning.description:
The reason the first subject that could not be handled was skipped, in the language of the request, while the
rest of the list was still applied. Null when every named subject went through. The text is meant to be shown
to a person, not matched against.

error.description:
Reports the one case in which nothing at all was changed: a member being removed still holds a role in a form
of the room, and the request did not ask to remove them anyway. Repeat the call with `force` to remove them
together with the role.

roomId.description:
The identifier of the room the template is built from. Take it from the room listing of
`GET api/2.0/files/rooms`; a folder identifier is not accepted.

title.description:
The title the template is saved under in the Templates section. Characters that a folder name cannot contain
are replaced with an underscore on save, and two templates may share a title.

logo.description:
A picture of the caller's own for the template, cropped out of an image already placed in the temporary
storage.

copyLogo.description:
Whether the template takes over the picture already set on the source room. When false the template gets no
picture from that room.

share.description: The email addresses of the portal members who are granted read access to the finished template.

groups.description: The identifiers of the portal groups whose members are granted read access to the finished template.

public.description:
Whether the finished template is shared with everyone allowed to create rooms. When false it stays reachable
only for the recipients named for it.

tags.description: The labels attached to the template and shown next to it in listings.

color.description:
The accent colour of the generated cover, written as six hexadecimal digits with no leading hash sign. When it
is left empty a colour is picked at random.

cover.description:
The identifier of a built-in cover picture, as listed by `GET api/2.0/files/rooms/covers`. When it is left
empty the template gets no cover.

quota.description:
The storage limit assigned to the template, in bytes. When it is not set the template keeps the limit of the
source room.

RoomTemplateDto.description: The parameters of a room template built from an existing room.

templateId.description:
The template the job is building. It is meaningful once the job has created the template folder, and the
template can be opened with the room operations only after `isCompleted` turns true.

progress.description:
How far the job has got. The value climbs while the contents of the room are being copied and reaches its
maximum at the very end, so it is an indication of life rather than a reliable estimate of the time left.

error.description:
Why the job stopped. It is empty while the job runs and after a successful one; when it is filled the
half-built template has already been removed, so nothing has to be cleaned up by the caller.

isCompleted.description:
Whether the job has ended. It is set both after a successful build and after a failure, so `error` is what
tells the two apart, and the record keeps answering with the same values until another job is started.

metadataTemplateId.description:
The ID of the metadata template the rooms must be assigned to. On its own it narrows the listing to the rooms
carrying the template; together with the conditions it also pins the template the filtered fields belong to.

items.description:
One metadata filter condition as the clients send it: an element of the "metadataFilters" JSON of the listings and of
the body of the search endpoints. All conditions are combined with AND.

metadataFilters.description: The metadata filter conditions, combined with AND. A custom field is addressed by its name instead of the field ID.

includeHiddenMetadata.description:
Whether the text search, and the "metadataMatches" it reports, also look at the values of the hidden metadata
templates (created with "visible" false for the metadata a service keeps for itself, which the web client never
shows). False, the default, leaves them out, so an entry is not found by such a value; true takes them in.
"metadataTemplateId" and "metadataFilters" are not concerned: a hidden template or field named there is searched
either way.

filterValue.description:
The text to search for in the room titles and in the string metadata values of the rooms, the custom fields and
the template fields alike; a room found by its metadata says where in "metadataMatches".

searchArea.description: The section to search in: the active rooms (the default), the archive or the templates.

items.description: The room type.

type.description: The room types to search among.

count.description: The number of rooms to return, from 1 to 100.

startIndex.description: The zero-based index of the first room to return.

sortBy.description: The field to sort by, a name of the SortedByType values.

RoomsMetadataSearchRequestDto.description:
The typed form of the metadata search of the rooms: the same filter the rooms listing takes in the "metadataTemplateId"
and "metadataFilters" query parameters, with the conditions as objects instead of a JSON string.

fileId.description:
The id of a portal file to store the result in as a new version, as reported by a folder listing such as
`GET api/2.0/files/{folderId}`.

folderId.description:
The id of a folder to save the result in as a new file, as reported by a folder listing such as
`GET api/2.0/files/{folderId}`.

title.description: The title of the new file, when it has to differ from the name the script saved the result under.

script.description:
The document builder script. It names a portal file by its id where the document builder documentation
writes an address - `builder.OpenFile("1234")`; an address written out in the script is refused.

folderId.description:
The id of the folder for the produced files that `outputs` does not list, as reported by a folder listing
such as `GET api/2.0/files/{folderId}`.

outputs.description:
Destinations of the produced files, keyed by the name the script saves each one under - the second argument of
`builder.SaveFile("docx", "result.docx")`.

argument.description:
Values the script reads through the global `Argument` object, such as `Argument.title`. A JSON object without
http or https addresses.

RunBuilderScriptRequestDto.description: The document builder script to run and where to put what it produces.

folderId.description: The folder the PDF is created in; the caller has to be allowed to create files there.

title.description:
The name of the PDF, without an extension - `.pdf` is appended. Left empty, the name of the source file is
reused with its extension replaced.

SaveAsPdfRequest.description: The place and the name the PDF copy of a file is stored under.

formId.description:
The PDF form the roles belong to. This is the value the operation reads, rather than the identifier in its
route, and the two are to be sent the same.

items.description: One role of a form and the account that fills it.

roles.description:
The roles with the account taking each of them and the sequence number that decides the turn: the same number
means the roles may be filled in parallel, different ones make a queue. The whole set is replaced on every
call, and an empty set resets the filling.

SaveFormRoleMappingDto.description: The people who are to fill in the roles of a PDF form.

The search area. Serialized by name ("Active", "Forms", ...) so that request bodies and
responses carry the section as the same readable word the query string already accepts.

folderIds.description:

number on the portal, a string on a connected third-party account.

fileIds.description:
The files whose rights are being changed, identified as a listing operation returns them - a number on the
portal, a string on a connected third-party account.

share.description:
One record per account or group whose rights are being set, each naming the subject and the level it gets on
all of the listed entries; a level of `None` takes the access away. An empty collection makes the call change
nothing.

notify.description:
Set to true to have every account named in `share` emailed about the access it just received; false changes
the rights without telling anyone.

examples: You have been granted access to the file
sharingMessage.description:
The text put into that email, ignored while `notify` is false. Markup is stripped before sending, so only the
plain text of the value survives.

The window a service limit counts the spending over, in UTC. The windows are calendar-aligned rather than rolling,
except for a lifetime limit, which never resets. Numbered as the accounting service numbers it.

fileName.description:
The name to store the file under, extension included. Characters a title cannot hold are replaced and the name
is truncated, so the stored title can differ from the one sent.

fileSize.description:
The exact number of bytes that will be sent. The size is reserved when the session opens and compared with the
parts as they arrive; below the portal chunk size the session takes the whole payload in one part, and above
the portal limit for chunked uploads it is refused.

relativePath.description:
A slash-separated chain of folder titles under the target folder to store the file in; folders in the chain
that do not exist yet are created. Leave it empty to store the file in the folder from the path itself.

createOn.description:
The creation time to stamp on a newly created file instead of the moment the upload finishes. It is ignored
when the upload lands on a file that already exists.

encrypted.description:
Marks the stored file as client-side encrypted, which is how content uploaded into a private room is kept;
with false the bytes are stored as they arrive.

createNewIfExist.description:
Settles the clash when the folder already holds a file with this name: true stores the upload beside it under
a name with a numeric suffix, false takes the existing file over and adds the content to it as a new version.

SessionRequest.description: The file a chunked upload session is opened for, and how a clash with an existing name is settled.

items.description: The parameters of a custom text field.

fields.description:
The custom fields to set on the entry. A listed field gets the value, a null or empty value removes the field
from the entry, the fields not listed are left alone. A name the portal has not seen yet creates the field.

SetCustomFields.description: The parameters for setting custom fields.

version.description: The version of the form the editor opened; the old keys are the keys of that version.

sequence.description:
The number of this report within the editor session, growing with each one, such as the time it was taken in
milliseconds.

sessionId.description:
The editor session the report comes from: an id the editor makes up once each time it opens the form, such as a
GUID, of letters, digits, hyphens and underscores.

items.description: A field whose key the user changed in the editor.

renames.description:
Every field whose key the user changed since the editor opened the form, told apart by the field id the editor
keeps, with the key it had in the opened version and the key it has now; empty when no key changed.

SetFormFieldChangesRequest.description: The field keys the user changed in the editor.

items.description: The parameters of a metadata field value.

values.description: The metadata field values. An empty value clears the field.

SetMetadataValues.description: The parameters for setting metadata values.

id.description:
The identifier of the room template. Take it from `templateId` of `GET api/2.0/files/roomtemplate/status`, or
from the folder list of `GET api/2.0/files/rooms` called with `searchArea` set to 4; an identifier of an
ordinary room is not accepted.

public.description:
Whether the Everyone group keeps read access to the template. True shares it with every member allowed to
create rooms; false leaves it reachable only for its owner.

SetPublicDto.description: The public access to set on a room template.

set.description:
The state to store for the setting the operation addresses: true switches it on, false switches it off. The
flag carries no meaning of its own - what is switched, who is allowed to switch it, and whether the value
belongs to the calling account or to the whole portal are stated by the operation that binds this body. The
answer repeats the value the portal read back afterwards, which is not always the one that was sent.

SettingsRequestDto.description: The body of a file settings switch: a single flag carrying the state to store.

co-editing, and the call is refused when anybody else already has the file open. Left off, an ordinary
co-editing session is opened and others may join it.

TemplatesConfigDto.description:
One creation template offered in the editor. The portal no longer offers any, so this never appears in an editor
configuration.

fileIds.description:
The files to put on the template list, by id, as reported by a folder listing such as
`GET api/2.0/files/{folderId}`. Only a file stored in the portal itself can become a template, which is why an
id here is always numeric.

TemplatesRequestDto.description: The files to put on the personal template list of the calling account.

corporate.description:
Whether the account is attached to the legacy Common section, which is the case only for accounts inherited
from an older portal.

roomsStorage.description:
Whether the account is attached to the Rooms section, room templates and the archive counted in. This is where
`POST api/2.0/files/thirdparty` puts every account it connects.

customer_title.description: The name the account is shown under in the portal, as it was saved when the account was connected.

provider_id.description:
The account ID to send to `DELETE api/2.0/files/thirdparty/{providerId}`, or as `providerId` to
re-authenticate the account.

provider_key.description:
The storage service behind the account. `WebDav` stands for every WebDAV preset, so it does not tell which of
them was chosen when the account was connected.

ThirdPartyAccountDto.description: A third-party storage account the caller has connected.

url.description:
The address of the storage server to connect to. It is needed by the WebDAV presets whose server is not known
in advance (`WebDav`, `Nextcloud`, `ownCloud`), where it points at the WebDAV endpoint of that server, and by
`SharePoint`. For `kDrive` it is the WebDAV address of the drive, `https://{kDrive ID}.connect.kdrive.infomaniak.com`,
optionally followed by a folder path; the kDrive ID is the number after `/drive/` in the URL of the kDrive web app.
The OAuth services ignore it.

login.description:
The account name at the storage service, used by the services that authenticate by login and password. A login
sent without a password is rejected as an invalid request.

password.description:
The password, or the application password, for `login` at the storage service. Either this or `token` has to
be sent, and the credentials are verified against the service before the account is saved.

token.description:
The OAuth 2.0 authorization code from the consent screen of `Box`, `DropboxV2`, `GoogleDrive` or `OneDrive` -
not an access token: the portal exchanges the code for its own token and keeps that. The client ID and
redirect URL the consent screen URL is built from come from `GET api/2.0/files/thirdparty/capabilities`.

customerTitle.description:
The name the backup account is shown under in the portal. Characters that a folder title cannot hold are
replaced and the value is truncated; on the first connection a title that comes out of that empty is refused.

providerKey.description:
The storage service to connect, as the `key` of `GET api/2.0/files/thirdparty/providers`; the value is matched
case-insensitively. `Nextcloud` and `ownCloud` are presets over WebDAV and are stored and reported back as
`WebDav`.

ThirdPartyBackupRequestDto.description: The credentials and the title of the third-party storage account the portal writes its backups to.

fileId.description: The file to convert. It is taken from the route of the operation, so a value sent in the body is overwritten.

sync.description:
How to wait for the result: `true` converts inside the request and answers with the finished result, which is
only sensible for small documents, while `false` queues the conversion and answers with an entry to poll.

startConvert.description:
Whether the conversion is to be started. It is set by the operation itself, so a value sent in the body is
overwritten.

version.description: The version to convert; 0 or less means the current version.

password.description:
The password that opens the source document, for a file that is protected by one; anything else may be left
out.

outputType.description:
The extension of the format to convert into, without the dot, and one the portal can produce from that
source format; left out, the default of the portal for that kind of document is used.

createNewIfExist.description:
Where the result goes when the file has been converted before: `true` creates another file beside the source,
`false` replaces the converted file that already exists.

ThirdPartyCheckConversionRequestDto.description: The parameters of one file conversion.

id.description:
The identifier of the reserved upload, repeated in the path of every call that follows it - the chunk uploads,
the finalize and the abort. It is thirty-two hexadecimal characters without separators, and it is the only
thing the server checks, so anyone holding it can write into this upload.

path.description:
The chain of folders leading to the destination, outermost first and the destination itself last, with folders
the caller cannot read left out. An answer that reports a stored part carries the destination folder alone
instead of the whole chain.

created.description: The moment the upload was reserved, in UTC.

expired.description:
The moment the reservation lapses and the parts buffered for it are dropped, in UTC. It is a gap rather than a
deadline for the whole transfer: every accepted part pushes it twelve hours past that part, so only a long
silence loses the upload.

location.description:
The absolute address of the separate chunk handler that also accepts the parts of this upload, kept for
clients written against it. A caller working through this API does not need it and sends the parts to the
session operations instead.

bytes_total.description:
The size in bytes that was declared when the upload was reserved, echoed back. It is what the arriving parts
are counted against to decide the file is complete, not the amount received so far.

ThirdPartyChunkedUploadSessionDto.description:
The reserved chunked upload: where the parts are sent, how much was declared and when the reservation lapses. No
content of the file is described here.

success.description:
Always true in a body that reaches the caller, because a call that does not succeed answers with an error
status and no body at all. It cannot be used to tell a refusal from a success.

data.description: The reserved upload itself, in the same shape the newer session operations answer with directly.

ThirdPartyChunkedUploadSessionResultDto.description: The reserved chunked upload wrapped in the envelope the two older session operations answer with.

response.description: The ThirdPartyChunkedUploadSessionResultDto object returned by the operation.

count.description: How many items this response carries: the length of the page for a list, 1 for a single object

total.description: How many items the whole list holds across all pages, for working out how many pages to request. Sent only by the operations that page their results, and left out of every other response
