document.description:
The document as the editors address it: its revision key, title, type, download address and the permissions of
this caller on it.

documentType.description:
The editor family the file opens in - `word`, `cell`, `slide`, `pdf` or `diagram`. It comes back empty for a
format no editor handles.

editorConfig.description:
How the editor is set up for this opening: the mode, the language, the interface customization, the callback
the editors save through, and the account they attribute changes to.

editorType.description:
The layout the configuration was actually built for. It echoes the requested one except where the room
overruled it, as the templates folder does by forcing the embedded viewer.

editorUrl.description:
The address of the editor api script the client has to load, with the shard key of this document already
appended. Load it as it is given rather than assembling it by hand.

token.description:
Signs this whole configuration so that the editors can trust it; anything a client changes in the
configuration invalidates it. It stays empty on a portal that has no signature secret configured for the
document service.

type.description:
The layout spelled as a lowercase word - `desktop`, `mobile` or `embedded` - the same value the editor type
carries as a number.

file.description: The file the configuration was built for, in the same shape the file listings report it.

errorMessage.description:
Filled in when the document could not be prepared for opening; the rest of the configuration should then not
be handed to the editors.

startFilling.description:
Whether this caller may start a filling session on the form from inside the editor. It stays empty when the
file is not a form opened where starting is possible at all.

fillingStatus.description:
True once the caller holds a role in the running filling session of this form. It stays empty outside a
virtual data room, where roles are the only place it is set.

startFillingMode.description:
Which filling button the editor offers: none at all, sharing the form out for others to fill, starting a
filling session, or starting one inside the form-filling room.

trackFormFieldChanges.description:
True when the editor should report the form fields renamed while the original form of a form-filling room is
edited, which is exactly when `PUT api/2.0/files/file/{fileId}/fieldchanges` accepts the reports. It is false
when the form is opened for viewing or filling, when the caller may not edit it, for a copy of a form, outside
a form-filling room, and with Document Server Community Edition, whose editors cannot tell the fields of the
open form.

fillingSessionId.description:
Identifies the filling session this opening belongs to, and is empty when the document is not opened as part
of one. Submissions made in the editor are collected under it.

quotaExceededScope.description:
Names the quota that ran out - the user, the room or the portal - and is set only when the document had to be
opened read-only because of it.

generationToolCallState.description:
The generation the editor should run as soon as the document opens. It is set only for a document an AI agent
produced and left waiting for its content, and is empty for every other file.

ThirdPartyConfigurationDto.description:
Everything an editor client needs in order to open one document: the document itself, the editor setup for this
caller, and the signature that lets the editors trust both.

response.description: The ThirdPartyConfigurationDto object returned by the operation.

count.description: How many items this response carries: the length of the page for a list, 1 for a single object

total.description: How many items the whole list holds across all pages, for working out how many pages to request. Sent only by the operations that page their results, and left out of every other response

folderId.description:
The folder holding the draft: the sub-folder that the room for filling keeps for drafts of this particular
form.

folderTitle.description: The title of that folder, which the portal takes from the form itself when the form is released for filling.

fileId.description:
The draft itself - the copy the caller fills in, not the original form, and the identifier to pass to the file
operations while filling.

fileTitle.description:
The title of the draft, which the portal builds from the name of the person filling it and the name of the
form. Null when the draft the record points at no longer exists.

ThirdPartyDraftLocation.description: Where the caller's own filling draft of a form is kept.

ThirdPartyFileArrayWrapper.description: The successful API response containing the list of ThirdPartyFileDto objects.

folderId.description:
The folder the file is stored in. When the file was reached through a share and the caller cannot open its
real parent, the identifier of the Shared with me section is reported instead, so this is where the file is
visible rather than where it physically sits.

version.description:
The revision this entry describes. It starts at 1 and moves to the next number each time new content is stored
over the file, except for an editing session opened against the file itself, which replaces the content and
keeps the number. `GET api/2.0/files/file/{fileId}/history` lists them all.

versionGroup.description:
Groups revisions that belong together, which is how a history can fold a long editing session into one entry:
versions saved inside one session share this number, and an upload over the file starts a new group.

contentLength.description:
The size already formatted for display, with a unit and the separators of the caller's language. Read
`pureContentLength` for a number to calculate with.

pureContentLength.description: The size of the stored content in bytes, and null for an empty file.

fileStatus.description:
What the portal is currently doing with the file and how the caller stands towards it - open in the editor,
unread, being converted, and so on. The value is a bit mask that combines those states, so a file can report a
number that matches none of the published members on its own.

editingBy.description:
The accounts that have the file open in the editor at this moment, as account identifier to display name, and
empty when nobody has. The all-zero identifier stands for people who came in through an external link without
signing in, and its name carries their number in brackets when there is more than one.

mute.description:
Not a property of the file at all: it repeats, inverted, the calling account's own switch for new-item badges,
so it is the same in every entry of one answer. True means that account has badges turned off.

viewUrl.description:
The address that returns the bytes of the file - a download, in spite of the name; `webUrl` is the address a
person opens. When the file was reached through an external link the address carries the key of that link, so
it keeps working without signing in.

webUrl.description:
The page that opens the file in a browser: the editor for a format the portal edits, the media viewer for
pictures, audio and video, and the download address for a format it cannot show at all.

fileType.description:
The broad kind of content, worked out from the extension, which is what a client uses to pick an icon or a
viewer without parsing `fileExst` itself.

fileExst.description:
The extension of the stored file, leading dot included and always lower case. For a format the portal keeps in
a converted shape this is the extension it is served under, not the one it was uploaded with.

comment.description:
The note kept with this revision. The portal writes it itself for revisions it creates, an upload over an
existing file among them, and an editor stores the note a person typed when saving a version.

encrypted.description:
True for a file in a private room, whose content the server never sees and which therefore cannot be converted
or taken over by an upload. Null, rather than false, for an ordinary file.

thumbnailUrl.description:
The address of the generated preview image. It is filled in only while `thumbnailStatus` says the preview has
been created, and it carries a suffix that changes with the file, so an image cached for an earlier revision
is not reused.

thumbnailStatus.description:
How far the preview image has got. Only the created state means `thumbnailUrl` holds an address; the others
mean there is none, either because it is still being produced or because this format has no preview.

locked.description:
True while the file is held under a lock that stops anyone but its holder from editing it, and null rather
than false when there is no lock. `lockedBy` names the holder unless the caller is the holder.

lockedBy.description:
The display name of the account holding the lock, and null when the caller holds it - so `locked` true
together with no name here means the lock is the caller's own.

hasDraft.description:
For a fillable PDF form, whether the caller already has a filling draft of it, in which case `draftLocation`
says where that draft lives. Null for anything that is not a form.

formFillingStatus.description:
How far the filling of this form has got for the calling account, and whose turn it is now. It is worked out
only inside a virtual data room, where filling runs in steps; everywhere else it stays at the none value.

isForm.description: Whether the file is a PDF, and so offered as a fillable form. It is null for any other file type.

customFilterEnabled.description:
True while a spreadsheet is in the mode where each person sorts and filters their own view without changing
what the others see, and null rather than false when it is not.

customFilterEnabledBy.description: The display name of the account that turned that mode on, and null when the caller turned it on themselves.

startFilling.description:
For a form in a room for filling, whether it has been released for filling; until then it is still being
prepared and only the people running the room work with it. Null for a file this does not apply to.

isFillingPreparing.description:
True during the short window in which a released form is still being written out by the editor. Neither
filling nor editing is accepted while it lasts, so a client should wait and read the file again.

inProcessFolderId.description: Left empty by the portal: the folder holding the caller's draft is reported in `draftLocation` instead.

inProcessFolderTitle.description: Left empty by the portal, like the identifier beside it; the draft's folder is named in `draftLocation`.

resultsFolderId.description:
The folder that collects the completed copies of this form. It is filled in only for the original form of a
room for filling, and only for a caller allowed to work with that form; null everywhere else.

draftLocation.description:
Where the caller's own filling draft of this form is kept. Null when there is no draft yet, which is the same
thing `hasDraft` reports.

viewAccessibility.description:
Which ways of opening this format the portal supports at all - its own editor, the picture viewer, the media
player and so on. It answers whether the format can be shown, not whether this account may do it; rights are
reported in `security`.

lastOpened.description:
The moment the caller last opened the file. It is kept per account and is what orders the Recent section, so
it is null for a file this account has never opened. Written with the offset of the portal's time zone.

expired.description:
The moment the file falls under the lifetime rule of the room holding it and is removed. It is counted from
the first revision rather than the latest one, so editing a file does not postpone it, and it is null when the
room sets no lifetime. Written with the offset of the portal's time zone.

vectorizationStatus.description:
How far the indexing of the file's content for AI search has got. It is null for a file that has never been
queued for indexing, which is every file while the feature is off for the portal.

externalDbTableName.description:
The table collecting the submitted values of this form in the external database configured for its room. The
field is left out of the answer entirely when the form has no such table.

dimensions.description:
The pixel size of the picture, measured by reading the stored file rather than taken from any stored metadata.
Null for anything that is not a picture the portal can show, and also when the file could not be read.

ThirdPartyFileDto.description:
A stored file as the calling account sees it: where it lives, which revision this is, how it can be opened and
what the portal is currently doing with it.

id.description:
The identifier to pass back to the other operations of this entry. It is a number for storage on the portal
and a string for a connected third-party account, and it is unique only within its own kind, so files and
folders may carry the same value.

rootFolderId.description:
The section the entry ultimately lies in, as an identifier that can be listed like any other folder. For an
entry inside a room this is the rooms section, not the room.

originId.description:
The folder the entry was deleted from, which is where restoring it puts it back. It is left out of the answer
unless the entry is in the trash.

originRoomId.description: The room the entry was deleted from, left out of the answer for anything that was not deleted out of a room.

originTitle.description:
The name of the folder the entry was deleted from, for showing where it would be restored to. It is null for
an entry that is not in the trash.

originRoomTitle.description: The name of the room the entry was deleted from, null for anything that was not deleted out of a room.

canShare.description:
Whether the calling account may change who has access to the entry, and so whether offering a sharing dialog
for it makes sense. It is false in rooms whose access is fixed by the room itself, such as a private one, even
for its manager.

shareSettings.description:
How many links of each kind currently exist for the entry, counted separately for the primary link and the
additional ones. Kinds with no links are left out, and the whole field is null when the caller may not change
the access or no link exists at all.

security.description:
What the calling account may do with this entry, one flag per action, and the cheapest way to decide which
operations to offer without trying them. The flags already take the room's settings and the account's role
into account.

availableShareRights.description:
Which access levels may be handed out on this entry, listed per kind of recipient, so that a client offers
only levels the entry actually supports - a room for filling forms and a plain folder do not accept the same
ones.

requestToken.description:
The token of the link the entry is being read through, which is the value the external-share operations expect
and which also has to be carried by the download and preview addresses. It is null whenever the entry is not
being read through a link.

external.description:
Set when the link being used was made for this very entry, and false when the entry is reached through a link
to the room around it. It is null when no link is involved.

expirationDate.description:
When the link being used stops working, written with the offset of the portal's time zone. It is null for a
link that never expires and whenever no link is involved.

isLinkExpired.description:
Set when the link being used has already passed its expiration date, which is why the entry cannot be opened
even though it is described here. It is null when no link is involved.

assignedMetadataTemplates.description: The IDs of the metadata templates assigned to the file entry.

hasMetadataFields.description:
Whether the entry has a metadata field a user can see and fill, by hand or with the AI filling: a field of a
visible assigned template, or a custom field. False when the entry has no metadata, when its assigned templates
are all hidden, or when they have no fields. It says nothing about the values: it stays true once every field is
filled, and nothing about the caller's rights: writing the values still needs the right to edit the entry
(`security.Edit`). It cannot be derived from `assignedMetadataTemplates`, which lists hidden templates too and
never lists the custom fields. Present, with a value, in the folder listing and in the file and folder info
responses; absent in the other responses that carry an entry (the answer to a creation, an upload or a rename),
which do not compute it, and for an entry of a third-party storage, which has no metadata. The same flag is
answered by `GET api/2.0/files/metadata/file/{fileId}` and `GET api/2.0/files/metadata/folder/{folderId}`.

items.description:
Where a text search met the metadata of a file, a folder or a room: one string value that holds the searched text,
with the field it belongs to.

metadataMatches.description:
Where the search text of the listing was met in the metadata of the entry: one item per string value holding
the text, in the order of the fields. Present only in a listing filtered by text, and only for the entries whose
metadata contain it; an entry found by its title alone carries nothing here.

ThirdPartyFileEntryDto.description:
The part of a file or folder that depends on how the entry is identified: by a number on the portal, or by a
string on a connected third-party account.

ThirdPartyFolderArrayWrapper.description: The successful API response containing the list of ThirdPartyFolderDto objects.

items.description:
What every file and folder in an answer has in common; the concrete shape is a file or a folder, told apart by the
entry type.

files.description:
The file entries of this page. It is empty when the folder holds no files, when the filters matched none of
them, and in the sections that list rooms only.

items.description:
What every file and folder in an answer has in common; the concrete shape is a file or a folder, told apart by the
entry type.

folders.description:
The folder entries of this page. In a section of rooms these entries are the rooms themselves, which is where
their type, tags, logo and quota are read from.

current.description:
The folder or section the page was read from, with its own title, type and access rights. It describes the
container, not the entries, and is filled in even when the page is empty.

pathParts.description:
The breadcrumbs of the current folder, ordered from the root of the section down to it. Each element carries
the identifier, the title and the folder and room types, and folders the caller cannot read are left out, so
the chain can be shorter than the real depth.

startIndex.description:
The position of the first entry of this page in the whole result, echoing the requested start index. Add the
number of entries received to it to ask for the next page.

count.description:
How many entries this page carries, files and folders together. A page shorter than the requested size means
the result is exhausted.

total.description:
How many entries matched before paging was applied, across the whole folder. Page until the start index plus
the entries received reaches it.

new.description:
How many entries of this folder are marked as new for the caller. It is 0 for every listing when the account
has switched the new-item badges off, so a zero here does not prove that nothing has changed.

ThirdPartyFolderContentDto.description:
One page of the contents of a folder or of a section: its entries split into files and folders, the folder itself,
and the counters needed to page through the rest.

response.description: The ThirdPartyFolderContentDto object returned by the operation.

parentId.description:
The folder this one is listed in. For a room it is the root of the section the room lives in, and for an entry
opened through a sharing link whose real parent the caller may not read it is the root of the section with the
entries shared with them.

filesCount.description:
How many files lie directly in the folder, without counting the subfolders. The roots of the `Rooms`, room
templates, default templates and AI agents sections always report 0, because the number is not collected for
them.

foldersCount.description:
How many subfolders lie directly in the folder. For an AI room the two service subfolders it always holds are
subtracted, so the number matches what a listing of it shows, and the roots of the `Rooms`, templates and AI
agents sections report 0.

isShareable.description:
Whether the caller may hand out access to the folder. It is filled in only for the folder a folder-contents
answer is about, and is null in every other answer, so null says nothing about the sharing rights.

new.description:
How many entries inside the folder the caller has not opened yet, the number drawn as the badge on it. An
account that turned the badges off in its own settings always reads 0 here, so 0 alone does not prove that
everything has been seen.

mute.description:
Whether the caller silenced the notifications of this room: true means no message about its activity reaches
them. The choice belongs to the reading account rather than to the room, so two members of one room read
different values.

tags.description:
The names of the tags attached to the room. Empty for a folder that is not a room, since only rooms carry
tags, and the names are the ones from the portal tag catalogue.

logo.description:
The addresses of the room logo in four sizes, together with the colour and the built-in cover that are drawn
when no logo was uploaded. A room without a logo answers with four empty addresses rather than with null, and
the field is null for a folder that is not a room.

pinned.description:
Whether the caller pinned the room to the top of their own room list. Pinning is personal and is lost when the
room is archived.

roomType.description:
The kind of the room, which decides the default access rules of its members. Null for a folder that is not a
room.

private.description:
Whether the room is a private one, which limits it to the accounts invited into it and needs encryption keys
set up for each of them.

indexing.description:
Whether the contents of the room are kept in an explicit numbered order, the one reported as `order` on each
entry, instead of being left to the sorting the reader asks for.

denyDownload.description:
Whether downloading and printing the contents of the room is forbidden, which leaves its members with viewing
and editing in the editor.

lifetime.description:
The rule by which the files of the room are removed once they grow old. Null when the room has no such rule,
which is also what is reported after the rule is switched off, because switching it off erases it.

watermark.description:
The watermark stamped over the documents of the room while they are viewed and printed. Null when the room has
no watermark, and for every folder that is not a room.

type.description:
The part the folder plays inside its room: one of the service folders of the form-filling flow, or the
knowledge and result storages of an AI room. It stays null for an ordinary folder and for the room itself, so
it does not describe folders in general.

inRoom.description:
Whether the caller holds the room through an invitation of their own: true for the account that created it and
for a member invited personally, false when the access comes from a group they belong to, and null for a
folder that is not a room.

quotaLimit.description:
How much space the files of the room may take, in bytes. It is the limit set on this room, or the portal
default for rooms when none was set. Null when the tariff of the portal does not count room statistics, when
room quotas are switched off, when the room lies in the archive or the trash, or when the role of the caller
in the room carries no editing rights - a viewer, a commenter, a reviewer and a form filler do not see the
figure, a room manager, a content creator and an editor do.

isCustomQuota.description:
Whether `quotaLimit` is a limit set on this room (true) or the portal default for rooms (false). Null exactly
when `quotaLimit` is null.

usedSpace.description:
How much the files of the room take, in bytes, as of the last time the counter was recomputed. The counter is
refreshed when a file operation finishes, so a read right after an upload or a deletion can still report the
previous figure. Null for a folder that is not a room.

passwordProtected.description:
Whether the sharing link the folder was opened through asks for a password that has not been entered yet.
While it is true the contents stay unreadable; send the password to `POST api/2.0/files/share/{key}/password`
first. Null when the folder was not reached through a link.

expired.description:
Deprecated, read `isLinkExpired` instead: whether the sharing link the folder was opened through has run out
of its lifetime.

chatSettings.description:
The chat configuration of an AI room. Only the system prompt is reported here, whatever else the room stores,
and the field is null for every folder that is not an AI room.

rootRoomType.description:
The kind of the room the folder lies in. It is filled in only for the folder a folder-contents answer is
about, and only when that room is an AI room, so it is null in every other answer and for every other room
kind.

saveFormAsXLSX.description:
Whether the answers collected in this form-filling room are also gathered into a spreadsheet next to the
completed copies. Filled in for form-filling rooms only.

sendFormToExternalDB.description:
Whether the answers collected in this form-filling room are also pushed into the external database configured
for the portal. Filled in for form-filling rooms only.

originalFormId.description:
The form the completed copies in this folder were filled from, taken from the copy submitted last. Null while
the folder holds no completed copy, and for every folder that does not collect them.

ThirdPartyFolderDto.description: The folder, with the fields that only a room carries filled in when the folder is a room.

url.description:
The address of the storage server to connect to. It is needed by the WebDAV presets whose server is not known
in advance (`WebDav`, `Nextcloud`, `ownCloud`), where it points at the WebDAV endpoint of that server, and by
`SharePoint`. For `kDrive` it is the WebDAV address of the drive, `https://{kDrive ID}.connect.kdrive.infomaniak.com`,
optionally followed by a folder path; the kDrive ID is the number after `/drive/` in the URL of the kDrive web app.
The OAuth services ignore it.

login.description:
The account name at the storage service, used by the services that authenticate by login and password. A login
sent without a password is rejected as an invalid request.

password.description:
The password, or the application password, for `login` at the storage service. Either this or `token` has to
be sent, and the credentials are verified against the service before the account is saved.

token.description:
The OAuth 2.0 authorization code from the consent screen of `Box`, `DropboxV2`, `GoogleDrive` or `OneDrive` -
not an access token: the portal exchanges the code for its own token and keeps that. The client ID and
redirect URL the consent screen URL is built from come from `GET api/2.0/files/thirdparty/capabilities`.

customerTitle.description:
The name the connected account is shown under in the portal. Characters that a folder title cannot hold are
replaced and the value is truncated, and a title that comes out of that empty is refused.

providerKey.description:
The storage service to connect, as the `key` of `GET api/2.0/files/thirdparty/providers`; the value is matched
case-insensitively. `Nextcloud` and `ownCloud` are presets over WebDAV and are stored and reported back as
`WebDav`.

providerId.description:
The account to re-authenticate instead of connecting a new one, as `providerId` of
`GET api/2.0/files/thirdparty`; both a number and its decimal string form are accepted.

ThirdPartyRequestDto.description: The credentials and the title of a third-party storage account to connect or to re-authenticate.

folderId.description: The folder the PDF is created in; the caller has to be allowed to create files there.

title.description:
The name of the PDF, without an extension - `.pdf` is appended. Left empty, the name of the source file is
reused with its extension replaced.

ThirdPartySaveAsPdfRequest.description: The place and the name the PDF copy of a file is stored under.

id.description:
The file the parts are being written into. An upload that took over a file of the same title carries it from
the start, while an upload that creates a new file has nothing to name yet and reports 0 until the answer that
sets `uploaded` to true.

folderId.description:
The folder receiving the file. It is the folder the upload was reserved against, or the sub-folder created for
it when the reservation declared a relative path.

version.description:
The revision the content is being written as: 1 for a file that did not exist, the next number when the upload
took over a file of the same title, and the unchanged current number for an upload opened over an existing
file, which replaces its content in place.

title.description:
The title the file is stored under, after characters a title cannot hold were replaced and, where a second
copy was asked for, a numeric suffix was added - so it can differ from the name that was sent.

providerKey.description:
The third-party service holding the destination, such as `GoogleDrive` or `OneDrive`, and null for a folder
stored on the portal itself.

uploaded.description:
False while bytes are still missing, when the answer only reports progress; true in the answer that reports
the stored file, which is also the answer that arrives with 201.

file.description:
The file as it stands. It is filled in both answers, but while `uploaded` is false it describes a file that
has not been written yet, so its identifier, size and links are only worth reading once that flag turns true.

ThirdPartyUploadSessionResponseDto.description: How far a chunked upload has got, and the file it produced once the last byte has arrived.

roomIds.description: IDs of the rooms to unlink. IDs that are not linked to the project are ignored.

UnlinkAiProjectSourcesRequest.description: Rooms to unlink from the AI project.

profileId.description: ID of the AI model profile that answers in the project's chat; take it from the `id` of a profile that `GET api/2.0/ai/profiles/list` returns.

UpdateAiProjectModelRequest.description: The AI model to set for the AI project.

version.description:
The version the comment belongs to, as reported by `GET api/2.0/files/file/{fileId}/edit/history`. A version
that does not exist is rejected as an invalid request.

comment.description:
The note that explains what changed in that version, as the version history shows it. An empty text clears the
note, and a longer one is cut rather than refused, so read the stored text from the answer.

UpdateCommentRequest.description: The comment to store on one version of a file.

title.description:
The new title of the file, without an extension - the stored extension is kept whatever the title says, so a
rename cannot change the format. Left empty, the file keeps its name.

lastVersion.description:
The version to restore on top of the history, as reported by `GET api/2.0/files/file/{fileId}/history`; 0 or
less leaves the versions untouched.

UpdateFileRequest.description: The changes to make to a file: a new title, an earlier version to restore, or both.

cascade.description:
Whether the template cascades from the folder to the folders and files below it: true turns the cascade on,
false turns it off while the template stays on the folder.

conflictResolveType.description: How the cascade treats a value an entry below already holds.

UpdateFolderMetadataTemplateRequest.description: The new state of a template assignment on a folder: whether the template cascades to the content of the folder and how.

type.description: The new field type. The type can be changed only while the field has no values.

items.description: The parameters of a metadata field choice option.

options.description: The new choice options of the field. The options in use cannot be removed.

order.description: The new display position of the field inside the template: the fields are shown by it ascending.

UpdateMetadataFieldRequest.description: The parameters of a metadata field update. Every property is optional: a property that is omitted keeps its current value.

visible.description: Specifies if the template is visible in the UI pickers.

UpdateMetadataTemplate.description: The parameters for updating a metadata template.

roomsToAdd.description:
The rooms to attach to the group, each given as a number for a room stored in the portal or as a string for a
room on a connected third-party account. Every identifier has to name a room the caller can read; repeats and
rooms the group already holds are collapsed rather than refused.

roomsToRemove.description:
The rooms to detach from the group, in the same two forms. Detaching leaves the room and its content
untouched, and a room the group already holds can be detached even when the caller has lost access to it in
the meantime.

groupName.description:
The new name of the group, trimmed of surrounding spaces before it is stored. Leaving the member out keeps the
current name, and a name that is blank once trimmed is refused.

UpdateRoomGroupRequest.description: The changes to apply to a room group: a new name, rooms to attach and rooms to detach, in any combination.

title.description:
The new name of the room. It is trimmed and sanitised the way a room title is at creation, and a blank or
missing value leaves the current name alone rather than clearing it.

quota.description:
The new storage limit of the room, in bytes. A value of -1 leaves the room with no limit of its own, any other
negative value puts it back on the portal default, and a positive one is accepted only while the per-room
quota feature is on.

indexing.description:
Whether the room keeps a manual order of its contents. With it on every file and folder carries a position
that listings follow and that `PUT api/2.0/files/rooms/{id}/reorder` compacts; with it off the contents are
ordered by the sorting of the request. Turning it on renumbers the existing contents at once.

denyDownload.description:
Whether members without editing rights are stopped from downloading and printing the contents of the room.
They can still open the documents in the editor.

lifetime.description:
How long files may stay in the room before they are deleted automatically. The countdown starts when the
setting is saved, and leaving the field out keeps the files forever. Sending it with the switch off stops the
automatic deletion.

watermark.description:
The watermark drawn over documents opened in the room. Leaving the field out adds no watermark, and sending it
with the switch turned off removes the one the room has.

logo.description:
The picture to use as the room logo, named by the path that `POST api/2.0/files/logos` returned for an image
uploaded beforehand, plus the crop to take from it. Leaving the field out keeps the room on its cover and
colour.

tags.description:
The labels the room is to carry from now on. The list replaces the whole tag set rather than adding to it, an
empty list clears it, and names the portal catalogue does not hold yet are added to it.

color.description:
The background colour the room is drawn with while it has no logo, as six hexadecimal digits with no leading
number sign. An empty value restores the default colour of the room type.

cover.description:
The picture drawn on the room while it has no logo, named by an identifier from
`GET api/2.0/files/rooms/covers`. Any other value is rejected, and an empty value leaves the room without a
cover.

chatSettings.description:
The model and the prompt an AI room answers with. It belongs to AI rooms only and is rejected for a room of
any other kind.

sendFormToExternalDB.description:
For a form filling room, whether the data of every completed submission is also pushed to the external
database configured for the portal. It is what `POST api/2.0/files/rooms/{id}/externaldbsync` re-runs for the
forms already collected.

saveFormAsXLSX.description:
For a form filling room, whether the collected submissions are also gathered into a spreadsheet stored next to
the completed forms. With it off the submissions are kept only as the filled documents themselves.

UpdateRoomRequest.description: The fields of a room that a partial update changes.

roomIds.description:
The rooms to change, named by the identifiers that `GET api/2.0/files/rooms` reports. Only whole numbers are
processed, so identifiers of rooms kept in a connected third-party account are skipped without an error.

quota.description:
The storage each of the listed rooms may take, in bytes. It has to stay inside the portal own limit, and the
per-room quota feature has to be on, otherwise nothing is changed.

UpdateRoomsQuotaRequestDto.description: The rooms whose storage limit is to be changed, and the limit to give them.

roomIds.description:
The rooms to reset, named by the identifiers that `GET api/2.0/files/rooms` reports. Only whole numbers are
processed, so identifiers of rooms kept in a connected third-party account are skipped without an error.

UpdateRoomsRoomIdsRequestDto.description: The rooms that are to go back to the default storage limit of the portal.

oldName.description:
The name of the tag to rename, matched against the catalog exactly as it is stored rather than searched for.
Read the stored spelling from `GET api/2.0/files/tags`.

newName.description:
The name to store instead. It has to be free: names are unique across the portal, so a name another tag
already carries is refused, and merging two tags this way is not possible.

UpdateTagRequestDto.description: The parameters for renaming a custom room tag in the portal catalog.

success.description:
True when the image was stored and its path is in the data field. A rejected image is reported with an error
response rather than with a false here, so this field is true in every answer that carries a body.

data.description:
The path of the stored image, which is the value to send as the temporary file when the logo of a room is set.
It is opaque: do not build or parse it, and expect a different path from every upload.

message.description:
Left empty by this operation: nothing is reported here, and a refused image comes back as an error response
instead.

UploadResultDto.description: The outcome of storing an image in temporary storage before it is used as a room logo.

id.description:
The account the changes are recorded under. Two sessions carrying the same value are taken by the editors for
the same person.

name.description: The name shown next to the changes and in the list of participants.

image.description: An absolute address of the avatar shown for this participant.

roles.description:
The filling roles this participant holds in the form being filled out. It is set only for a form in a virtual
data room, where the role decides which fields open for them.

customerId.description:
Identifies the paying customer this participant belongs to, on deployments where the editors are licensed per
customer.

UserConfigDto.description: The account the editors attribute the changes of this session to.

usersIds.description:
The accounts to write to, taken from `GET api/2.0/files/rooms/{id}/share`. Anyone who has already joined, is
not in the room, or is invisible to the caller is skipped without an error, and the field is ignored once
every pending invitation is being resent.

resendAll.description:
Whether every invitation of the room that is still waiting is sent again. With it on the list of accounts is
ignored, and with it off an empty list means that nothing is sent at all.

UserInvitation.description: Which pending room invitations are to be sent again.

id.description:
The service limit ID, used to read, change, switch off or delete the limit through the
`api/2.0/portal/payment/servicelimit` operations. For the limit for every user it is the same for all users.

scope.description: Whether the limit is the user's own (`Custom`) or the limit for every user (`Global`) the user falls back to.

amountValue.description:
The most money the AI services may cost the user per period, in `currency`. It is the only threshold a limit on
the AI services has: their services count in different units, so a threshold on a quantity is refused for them.

amountConsumed.description:
The money the AI services cost the user in the current period, in `currency`; 0 when nothing was spent yet,
including a user who has never used the AI services.

currency.description: The currency `amountValue` and `amountConsumed` are expressed in; null when the limit has no money threshold.

period.description:
The window the threshold applies to. It resets at the start of the next day, week or month in UTC (a week on
Monday), not a fixed time after the first charge; a lifetime limit never resets.

periodEnd.description:
The moment the current period ends and the spending starts over from zero, in UTC. Null for a lifetime limit,
which never resets.

UserServiceLimitDto.description:
The spending limit on the AI services in force for one user: the user's personal limit, or else the limit for every
user, together with the money the user spent against it in the current period.

oneOf.description: [InProgress - In Progress, Completed - Completed, Failed - Failed]
[0 - In Progress, 1 - Completed, 2 - Failed]

VectorizationStatus.description: The status of a file's vectorization for AI search.

additions.description:
Which details of the reader and of the room are stamped alongside the text. The values combine, so a number
that is not a member on its own is the sum of several of them, and 0 means that only the text is stamped.

text.description:
The fixed line drawn over the document, printed before the details selected alongside it. Empty when the room
stamps an image instead.

rotate.description:
How far the stamp is turned, in degrees, with negative values turning it anticlockwise and 0 drawing it
horizontally.

imageScale.description:
How large the image is drawn, as a percentage of its own size. It is 0 for a text watermark, where nothing is
scaled.

imageUrl.description: The address the stamped picture is served from, inside the storage of the room. Empty for a text watermark.

imageHeight.description:
The height the picture is drawn with, in pixels, kept together with the width so that the proportions survive.
It is 0 for a text watermark.

imageWidth.description:
The width the picture is drawn with, in pixels, kept together with the height so that the proportions survive.
It is 0 for a text watermark.

WatermarkDto.description: The watermark drawn over the documents of a room while they are viewed and printed.

width.description: Defines the watermark width measured in millimeters.

height.description: Defines the watermark height measured in millimeters.

margins.description: Defines the watermark margins measured in millimeters.

items.description: One paragraph of the watermark text.

paragraphs.description: The list of paragraphs of the watermark.

WatermarkOnDrawDto.description: The watermark the editor draws over every page.

items.description: A run of watermark text with its own colour and size.

runs.description: The list of text runs from the paragraph.

WatermarkParagraphDto.description: One paragraph of the watermark text.

enabled.description:
Whether the room draws a watermark at all. Sending the object with this turned off removes the watermark the
room has, and the rest of the fields are then irrelevant.

additions.description:
Which details of the reader and of the room are stamped into the watermark alongside the text. The values
combine, so several of them can be added together to stamp more than one.

text.description:
The fixed line drawn over the document, shown before the details selected alongside it. It is the whole
watermark when no details are added.

rotate.description:
How far the watermark is turned, in degrees, with negative values turning it anticlockwise. Zero draws it
horizontally across the page.

imageScale.description:
How large the watermark image is drawn, as a percentage of its own size. It applies to the image form of the
watermark only.

imageUrl.description:
The picture to use instead of a text watermark, named by the path that `POST api/2.0/files/logos` returned for
an image uploaded beforehand. The portal copies it into the room when the setting is saved.

imageHeight.description: The height the watermark image is drawn with, in pixels, used together with the width to keep its proportions.

imageWidth.description: The width the watermark image is drawn with, in pixels, used together with the height to keep its proportions.

WatermarkRequestDto.description: The watermark drawn over the documents of a room.

fill.description: The fill color of the text run in RGB format.

font-size.description: The font size of the text run in points.

WatermarkTextRunDto.description: A run of watermark text with its own colour and size.

form.description:
The original form the answers are collected from. It is not the produced spreadsheet - that one arrives with
the task, once the task reports completion.

task.description:
The queued generation. Poll it with `GET api/2.0/files/file/{fileId}/xlsx` until it reports completion, and
take the produced file from it then.

isNewFile.description:
True when this run creates the report file, false when an existing report is rewritten in place, which means
it keeps its id and the links already shared for it.

XlsxReportResponseDto.description:
The answer to a report generation request: the queued task, the form whose answers are collected, and whether the
report file is being created or refreshed.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: Sliding window rate limit: 1500 requests per minute per user/IP.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Number of requests remaining in the current sliding window (1500 req/min). Concurrent limits also apply: 50 parallel GET requests, 15 parallel POST/PUT requests.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the current sliding window rate limit resets.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. Up to 60s for the sliding window (1500 req/min), up to 86400s for the daily POST/PUT limit (10000/day).

Bearer.description: Enter 'Bearer {JWT Token}'. Tokens are validated per RFC8725 (JSON Web Token Best Current Practices): signatures are required and checked against a server-side algorithm allow-list (ES256, RS256) rather than the token header, and issuer, audience and expiry are all verified.

ApiKeyBearer.description: Authentication is determined by the 'Authorization' header
ApiKeyBearer.name: ApiKeyBearer

OAuth2.description: OAuth2 flow with Authorization Code. The access tokens it issues are JWTs, validated per RFC8725 exactly as the Bearer scheme describes.
